guide.area: Learning and study products (Study mode: tutoring sessions, study plans, quizzes and flashcards)
guide.what_it_is_for: Study mode lets a person pick a subject, say how they want to learn it and how far they already got, and then have the assistant teach it in a chat that keeps to that method. It asks one question at a time, gives hints before answers, and can offer a study plan. The session is a normal chat conversation with a small extra record that marks it as a study session, so the person can find it again, leave the mode, or resume it.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-in users. The API routes require a logged-in user and use the user-scoped database (apps/web/app/api/study/sessions/route.ts:57-104). The interaction registry lists the study entitlement as managed_chat and trust mode as managed only (packages/contracts/types/src/interaction-modes.json:381-420), so Study mode is a Cloud feature, not a Local or own-key one. The code read here does not show the entitlement being checked in the study route, so the plan gate is not confirmed. Workspace admins, developers and paid-plan-only rules: not found in this area.

how_it_works.step: Person opens the Study page and starts a session
how_it_works.detail: The page takes the subject, mode, level, optional project and optional plan tick. Start is blocked until the subject is non-empty. The page first creates a chat conversation, then records a study session for it.

how_it_works.step: Conversation is created with a CSRF header
how_it_works.detail: The page calls the chat conversations endpoint with a CSRF token header. The server checks the token before creating the chat (requireCsrfToken). The study code sends the same header on its own start call.

how_it_works.step: Study record is written to the server
how_it_works.detail: The client calls /api/study/sessions with POST. The route checks CSRF and a rate limit, validates the body with a schema (topic 1-200 characters, mode and level enums), and writes one row for the conversation. A conversation can have only one study row (unique conversation_id in the migration).

The study code builds the teaching text from the subject, mode, level, a fixed rule (no answer before the learner tries) and a list of teaching practices. The account's own instruction and the current request are passed through the same precedence resolver, so the study text can lose a conflict.

how_it_works.step: Person chats; the server reads the active study row
how_it_works.detail: When a chat message is sent, the server looks up the conversation and, in the same step, reads the active study row (ended_at is null). If one exists, the instruction is added as a developer-layer message. The free-usage path does the same.

Leave calls DELETE on the same route, which sets ended_at. The conversation and its messages stay. Resume calls POST again on the same conversation, which the code expects to reactivate the mode. The chat page shows an indicator with a leave or resume button.
Delete on the Study page asks for confirmation through the shared confirm dialog, then deletes the whole chat conversation. The session row goes with it through the foreign key.

how_it_works.step: Quiz and flashcard blocks are drawn by viewers
how_it_works.detail: The model is asked to write quiz and flashcard blocks. Shared types and limits define their shape. Web and mobile have viewer components for them. The viewers were not read in this pass.

guide.area: 039 Memory product (AGI Workforce: saved facts about the user that later chats use)
guide.what_it_is_for: Memory lets the assistant keep useful facts about the person (preferences, work, background) and use them in later chats, so the person does not repeat themselves. The person can see what is saved, change or delete it, pin important items, turn it off, and keep work and project facts apart from personal ones. It matters because a remembered fact that is wrong or hidden is worse than none, so the area is built around visibility and control.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user of the web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome apps, as far as the code shows the memory API and screens are not limited to one plan (plan gating was not confirmed; see not_sure). Organization admins control whether memory is allowed for their workspace, via the organization policy row read in managed-memory-context-service.ts. Developers use the same API (the brief lists "api" status for some items). Mobile also has a separate on-device memory store that works without the cloud.

features.name: Turn Memory on or off
features.use: A switch turns Memory on or off for the person. A second switch decides whether the assistant may look up excerpts from other past chats. The onboarding intro that explains Memory before first use is not built in any app.
how_people_use_it: Web: open Settings, go to the Memory section, flip the Memory switch or the past-chat switch.
Mobile: open Profile, or Settings then Memory, and use the controls card toggles.
Desktop: same Memory settings as web. CLI, VS Code and Chrome: see on_each_app.
how_it_should_work: When Memory is off, the assistant neither reads nor saves memories (brief Should). The server enforces this: a turn with memory off gets no memory tool and no memory context.
The past-chat switch is separate from the Memory switch.

how_it_works.step: Person changes a setting or memory on screen
how_it_works.detail: The settings section renders the Memory switch, the delete-all control and the confirm dialog. Delete-all uses a confirm dialog that states how many facts will go.

how_it_works.step: Client store calls the memory API
how_it_works.detail: The shared memory store fetches a CSRF token first, then calls the /api/memory endpoints with the request signal so stale calls can be cancelled.

how_it_works.step: API reads or writes the user's memories
how_it_works.detail: GET lists memories with paging, pinned first. POST creates a memory after CSRF and rate-limit checks. DELETE soft-deletes all memories in the current workspace.
The write is refused if the text contains a term from the person's exclusion list. The exclusion list is read from the user settings row; if that read fails, the write is refused.

how_it_works.step: Chat turn decides whether memory is on
how_it_works.detail: A chat turn gets no memory tool and no memory context when memory is off, the chat is temporary, or the person turned personalization off. Memory is also limited by the organization policy row.

how_it_works.step: Relevant memories are loaded into the prompt
how_it_works.detail: Up to 500 candidates are read, at most 30 are used, each is capped at 1,000 characters and the total at 8,000 characters. The memories are fenced as untrusted text before going to the model.

After a completed turn, facts are extracted (pattern-based, or model-based after the response). Turns with Google user data, or with a tool run where the rule forbids it, save nothing. Project chats save to their project. At most 5 facts per turn are written.

how_it_works.step: Stored as rows in the account database
how_it_works.detail: Memories are rows in the user_memories table. Reads filter out deleted, superseded and expired rows, and filter by workspace. A delete blanks the content and keeps the row so other devices learn of the deletion.

how_it_works.step: Conflicts are listed from superseded rows
how_it_works.detail: A memory replaced by a newer one keeps a pointer to the winner. The conflicts endpoint joins the two and returns up to 50.

how_it_works.step: Mobile writes to on-device storage first
how_it_works.detail: The mobile writer refuses prohibited categories, refuses sensitive topics for learned facts unless opted in, drops duplicates, and supersedes rival facts on the same topic. It stores into the on-device memory storage.

how_it_works.step: CLI keeps its own settings file
how_it_works.detail: The CLI writes memory settings (automatic memory on or off, decay days, maximum facts) to a JSON file under the user's home folder.

key_files.role: Memory list, create and delete-all endpoints; the main web and API entry point.
Core memory logic: exclusions, active/expired/workspace filters, limits, writes, and the memory context sent to the model.
Saves facts after each completed chat turn, with Google-data and project rules.
Refuses a memory write that contains a never-remember term; fails closed if the list cannot be read.
Decides per chat turn whether the memory tool and memory context are offered (memory off, temporary chat, personalization off).
Web settings screen for the Memory switch, delete-all and export/import entry points.
Shared client store for memory calls, used by web and desktop surfaces.
Lists memories replaced by newer ones, for the conflicts screen.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Never-remember matching is a plain lowercase substring test with a 3-character minimum, with no word boundary. A short term matches inside other words (for example a 3-letter term inside a longer word), so an unrelated memory can be refused.

Mobile's sensitive-topic check runs only for facts with source 'learned'. A fact the person types as a memory is not checked for sensitive topics (only prohibited categories are checked), which is looser than the server path.

Brief says Chrome is missing for the Memory switch and the saved-memory search, but the Chrome side panel contains memory code (about 97 memory references in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts). The brief status and the code disagree; not verified in the UI.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area lets a person tell the assistant who they are, how they want replies to sound and be shaped, and what standing rules should apply. It covers a name and background, a response style preset, fine sliders for tone and length, custom instructions for every chat, per-project and per-conversation overrides, and custom output styles. It matters because the same question gets a different answer for a student, a manager or a developer, and the user should not have to repeat these preferences in every chat.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user on the Web, Mobile, CLI, Desktop and extension surfaces, per the brief's Status lines. The web server code that builds the preference text is in the Cloud chat path (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions). I did not establish any plan gate for these settings in the code I read. Workspace admins appear only through the project-sharing check in apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:213-229, which reads organization shared projects. Developers use the CLI output-style code and its custom style files.

guide.what_it_is_for: A temporary chat is a conversation that leaves no trace in the person's history, search, memory or Library. Local-only use keeps chats, files and memory on the person's own device so that nothing is uploaded to the account. The area exists so that people can choose how much the product keeps, and so that the product says accurately what it keeps. Some parts are not built yet, such as private search and a private browser session.
guide.who_uses_it: Web and desktop: every signed-in user who opens a chat; no plan gate was found in the files read. Mobile: every user, with temporary chat and the explainer on the chat tab; the Personalized switch appears only in Cloud mode. Local-only conversations, files and memory: users of the mobile app in Local mode, the CLI, the VS Code extension (local models and CLI session history) and the Chrome extension (mirror switch). Workspace administrators: not seen in these files. Developers: the CLI and the Rust crate parts are used by developers who run the CLI. Temporary chats are refused inside a project on every app that reads the shared policy.

features.name: Start a temporary chat
features.use: Starts a chat that is not kept. It can be the default for every new chat.
how_people_use_it: Web: open the + menu in the composer and choose the Temporary chat row (it is a switch). Or open Settings, Privacy, and turn on Start new chats as temporary.
Desktop: click the Temporary chip in the composer context controls.
Mobile: on the chat tab, tap the eye-off Enable temporary chat pill; confirm the alert Turn on temporary chat? with Turn on. Tap the pill again to turn it off.
how_it_should_work: The default is off unless the setting is on. A chat that has a project cannot be temporary; the message is 'A temporary chat cannot be part of a project. Turn off temporary chat, or start the chat outside the project.'
Turning it on in a chat that already has messages opens a Save this chat? question first. Confirming keeps the messages; cancelling leaves the chat as it was.
While a switch-off save is running, the menu label reads 'Temporary chat · saving…'.
If the database write fails, the composer shows an error and does not show a mode the database does not have.
Mobile: the setting is for this app session only. It is not stored across launches.
No plan limit was found in these files.

features.name: Save a temporary chat to history
features.use: Turns a temporary chat into a normal, kept chat. The person sees what will be kept first.
how_people_use_it: Web: turn off the Temporary chat switch in the + menu (or the header). A dialog titled Save this chat? appears; confirm with Save chat. Cancel keeps the chat temporary.

how_it_should_work: The web dialog says how many messages will be kept and that files will be kept too. It keeps only user and assistant messages that are not still streaming.

The save is one database transaction: the chat is flipped to kept, messages are written in order, the active leaf is set and the files are flipped. If any part fails, nothing changes and the person sees 'This chat could not be saved.'
A chat that is already saved returns 'This chat is already saved.'
At most 1000 messages are accepted. Free users pass a daily message-write allowance check first.
Mobile: the alert does not list what will be kept, so it does not fully meet 'sees what will be kept and confirms'.

how_it_works.detail: On web the switch lives in the composer + menu. The menu row is built in TemporaryChatRows. The composer computes whether the chat is temporary from the pending choice, the default setting and the project. On mobile a pill on the chat tab sets a session-only flag after an alert confirmation.

how_it_works.step: Decide whether the next chat is temporary
how_it_works.detail: A shared rule says a chat is temporary when there is no project and either the per-chat choice or the default is on. The chat page uses this rule to decide what the next send does.

how_it_works.step: Send the turn with the temporary flag
how_it_works.detail: The web chat page marks the conversation as temporary when the chat is created or sent. Mobile reads the conversation's temporary flag when it sends. Local-model turns on web are refused inside projects.

how_it_works.step: Server removes memory from a temporary turn
how_it_works.detail: The completions request processor refuses to add the memory-write tool for a temporary turn. The turn-context service leaves out memory and past-chat search when the turn is temporary. The web chat page also writes no message rows for temporary turns.

how_it_works.step: Save a temporary chat to history
how_it_works.detail: The person confirms in a dialog. The client posts the kept messages. The server runs one transaction that flips the chat to kept, inserts messages in order, sets the active leaf, and flips the chat's files. A failure rolls everything back. Artifact indexing is scheduled after the commit.

An uploaded chat file in a temporary chat is recorded with a temporary flag. Saving a generated image to the Library goes through the media keep endpoint, which moves the stored asset out of temporary status.

A nightly cron job deletes temporary chats created more than 30 days ago, in batches, skipping chats under a legal hold. It deletes image and video jobs linked to them and then purges temporary files.

The app mode (Local or Cloud) is stored in device storage and admitted through a gate. Local conversations are filtered out of history when they are temporary. Clear-all-data deletes the local tables.

how_it_works.step: Local-only use in CLI and Chrome
how_it_works.detail: The CLI blocks a Local session from moving to BYOK or Cloud without an explicit handoff command, and prints the privacy settings. The Chrome extension reads a stored switch that decides whether Managed Cloud chats are mirrored to the account.

guide.area: Proactive assistance, briefings, and reflection (brief area 042, 25 items)
guide.what_it_is_for: A briefing is a scheduled agent task, usually a daily "Daily briefing" that runs on weekday mornings and sends its result to the person. Scheduled runs are the one part that is built end to end: a person creates a schedule, the server runs it when it is due, and a completion notice goes out by push or email. Reflection is a separate, on-demand summary of how the person used the product over a past period, and Time and focus holds quiet hours and break reminders. Most of the brief's items (topics, sources, briefing home, cards, calendar and email summaries, listen mode, helpful ratings, important-change alerts, the "caught up" end state) are not built anywhere in the code I read.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person who has a schedule, for the Daily briefing and other scheduled tasks. The daily brief on mobile is shown only when the schedules feature flag is on and the plan's scheduled-task limit is not zero (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/notifications/dailyBrief.ts:56-58); the per-plan numbers are not shown here. Reflect needs the Memory setting turned on (apps/web/app/api/reflect/route.ts:33-42). Time and focus is a personal setting. Workspace admins do not get a view in this area; the server only logs when a workspace member's scheduled work cannot run (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1317-1339). Developers use the CLI schedule commands, which need a managed (Cloud) session (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs:233-234).

Mobile: flip the Daily brief switch on; the app creates the schedule with the 08:00 default time.
CLI: create or update the schedule through the schedules command (time and timezone are part of the saved schedule).
how_it_should_work: The template is weekdays at 08:00 with the fixed prompt text in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:843-856.
The run is done by the server executor when the schedule is due; the result is delivered through the completion notice (see the Work-completion feature).

Empty, waiting and failure states: the code shows a run as running, failed or awaiting approval (apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.tsx:405-415; apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/service.ts:140-143). Only the setup failure text 'Could not set up the daily brief.' is seen (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/notifications/dailyBrief.ts:30).
Limits: the plan's scheduled-task limit applies (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:816).

Email: the completion email is queued to run after quiet hours end (apps/web/lib/jobs/job-handlers.ts:111-127).

how_it_works.detail: A person picks the Daily briefing template (or the mobile Daily brief switch). The template is a fixed prompt plus weekday timing and default sources. The mobile app sends the schedule to the schedules API.
The saved schedule is a row in the scheduled tasks table, owned by the person. CLI updates use the same API with a managed session.
The server claims due schedules in batches. Schedules whose owner is no longer an active workspace member are left unclaimed and logged.

how_it_works.step: Run is executed on the server
how_it_works.detail: The executor picks a model route. It refuses the run when no model on the plan keeps chats out of training, and it checks whether the task reads Google user data.
When a run finishes, a job is queued. The job reads the person's notice settings and the schedule's notice settings, and sends push and email only where allowed. Email is held if quiet hours apply.
Quiet hours are read from the person's saved settings. Each push device is kept or dropped. Accepted devices get a request to the push service, and tokens that the service rejects are cleared.
The client loads recent runs through the runs endpoint and shows status, timing notes and errors.
The Reflect page asks the server for a recap for the chosen range and timezone. The server checks Memory, reads the period's conversations, and returns the recap without caching.

key_files.role: Shared schedule contract: the Daily briefing template (843-856), default sources, and the run-timing note helper (740-760).
Runs due schedules on the server: model route choice, the training-policy refusal, and the Google user-data check.
Scheduled-task rows: delete rule, claiming due runs, and the log for work left by people who left the workspace.
Completion notice job: reads notice settings, queues email (held for quiet hours), and sends push.
Reads a person's and a schedule's notice settings; decides push and email per status.
Filters push devices by preferences and quiet hours, then sends to the push service and clears rejected tokens.
Reads quiet hours from the person's settings and returns when they end.
Mobile Daily brief: availability by plan and feature flag, create, pause, and time change.
Builds the Reflect recap for a range, after checking Memory.
Web break reminders and quiet-hours nudge, driven by local active time.
Web Time and focus settings page: break length, quiet hours, validation and save.

guide.area: 043 Image and visual understanding (image and visual understanding in the AI chat)
guide.what_it_is_for: A person attaches a picture (a photo, screenshot, chart, diagram, handwritten note or scan) and asks the assistant about it. The model reads the picture and answers, so the person does not have to describe it by hand. This matters because much real help starts from something seen on a screen or on paper, such as an error, a setup problem or a receipt.
guide.who_uses_it: Every chat user on a surface whose chosen model accepts images (the code checks a model flag named supports_vision in the CLI and the model metadata in the web API). The code I read has no plan gate on sending an image to a vision model. Developers use the same path through the web OpenAI-style chat endpoint (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions), which accepts image parts with a detail setting. Workspace admins: not found in the code I read. Paid plans only: not found for this area in the code I read.

features.name: Ask a question about one or more attached images
features.use: The person attaches one image (or several in one message) and asks a question. Screenshots are covered by the same path, since a captured or pasted screenshot is just an image file.
how_people_use_it: Click the attach control in the composer and pick one or more image files (web, desktop, mobile, VS Code, CLI).
Or paste an image into the composer (VS Code paste handler, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:7728).
Or drag an image file onto the composer (VS Code drop handler, webviewContent.ts:7575).
Type the question and send. CLI: stage an image with the image file option at launch or with the stage-image command (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:830-885).
how_it_should_work: Image types accepted: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (signature check in apps/web/lib/moderation/image-structure.ts:25-35). Other files are refused by the chat attachment rules (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/chat-attachments.ts:339-350).
Before the model sees the picture, the upload is checked (structure, credentials, and an external malware scanner when one is required). See the scanner rules below.
If the chosen model does not accept images, the CLI refuses with the message: the model does not accept images, switch to a vision model with /model first (tui_app.rs:853-856).
Empty state, waiting state and failure text for the web and mobile composers were not established in the code I read.

Plan limits: not found for image input in the code I read. The quota label 'image' seen at apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5621 is for image generation, not for reading images.
features.on_each_app: Web: the image is uploaded through the web chat path and the scanner rules apply; the brief says a live check on production is still pending. Desktop: same web-hosted chat (the Electron window shows the hosted web app), brief says live check pending. Mobile (Cloud): a captured or chosen image is uploaded through apps/mobile/services/api.ts uploadFile (line 651 area). Mobile (Local): the on-device text model cannot see pixels; the app runs on-device OCR and sends the recognised text with a note (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1245-1258). CLI: images are read from disk, resized or kept original, and sent as image blocks (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8383-8400). VS Code: the image is stored as a data URL attachment with type image (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2207-2214). Chrome extension: the brief marks it done; I did not open the extension's image code except that apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/userFileUpload.ts lists image types.

features.name: Read documents, charts, diagrams and handwriting in an image
features.use: The same attach-and-ask path is used when the picture is a document photo or scan, a chart, a diagram or handwritten notes. The code does not treat these differently; the model does the reading.
how_people_use_it: Attach the photo or scan with the attach control or paste.
Ask for the transcript, the trend in a chart, the structure of a diagram, or what the handwriting says.
how_it_should_work: Same rules as the single-image feature. There is no separate document-image branch for these in the code I read.

how_it_works.detail: The image comes in by the attach control, paste, drop, the mobile scan screen, the Library, or the CLI image option. Each surface reads the file bytes and a MIME type (image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp).
The chat attachment rule maps the file name and declared type to an allowed type. Anything else is refused. Unknown types with a text-like extension become text/plain.

On a phone in Local mode, the picture is run through the on-device text recogniser. The text is sent to the local text model with the note that the model cannot see pixels. If no text is found, that is said in the note.

The web server reads the bytes, checks the image structure (signature, size), looks for credential strings, and asks the external malware scanner if one is configured. If the scanner is required and missing, the upload is refused with scan_unavailable.

Each image part may carry a detail value. The server accepts auto, low, high or original. It then checks that the chosen model accepts that value; a model metadata list is used, with a default list of auto, low and high. Auto is always allowed.

how_it_works.step: Parse the wire format into content blocks
how_it_works.detail: The OpenAI-style chat body is turned into internal content blocks. An image part with a URL or a data URL becomes an image block with its source and detail.
Each provider adapter turns image blocks into its own request shape: an image URL part for chat-style APIs (base64 images become data URLs), or an input image part for the responses-style API.
The request then goes through the normal routing and model-choice code, which sends it to a provider route the account can use. Model choice and routing for images were not traced end to end.
The answer comes back as ordinary assistant text. Image-related answers have no separate display or annotation layer (see S43.11).

switches.name: UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL
switches.effect: Sets the external malware scanner endpoint. When set, uploads are sent to it. When unset and a scanner is required, uploads are refused with scan_unavailable.

switches.name: UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED
switches.effect: true forces a scanner requirement, false turns it off; when unset the scanner is required only when NODE_ENV is production.

switches.name: NODE_ENV
switches.effect: Decides the default for scanner requirement when UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED is unset; also controls a one-time warning in production.

switches.name: Model image detail values (imageInput.detailValues)

switches.name: Vision support flag (supports_vision)
switches.effect: Refuses image staging on a model without vision; also reported in CLI model listings.

switches.name: CLI image mode (ResizeToFit or Original)
switches.effect: Resize to fit the model bounds, or send the original file.

switches.name: Native OCR module (AGIVisionOCR)
switches.effect: Required for mobile scan and Local-mode image text; missing means an error asking for a rebuild.

switches.name: Composer attachment size limit (10 MB)

guide.what_it_is_for: The image-generation studio lets a signed-in person make a picture from a text prompt inside a normal chat, pick the image model, and then keep, change, reuse, download or share the result. Images are made on the Managed Cloud path only: the server runs the model, reserves usage, and stores the result in the Library. This matters because the same flow serves the web app, the mobile app and the CLI, so a fix in the server route changes all three.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-in users on a paid plan that includes image generation. The server code lists the plans in PRO_TIERS (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise); basic and free plans are excluded. The web composer also hides image mode for free-trial accounts. Workspace admins are affected by the organisation policy gate and the workspace spend cap that run before every generation. Developers and power users use the CLI, which calls the same route. I found no Local (on-device) or own-key (user's provider key) image path in the files I opened.

how_it_works.detail: The person turns on image mode, picks the model, aspect ratio, style, and transparency, then sends. The web send path builds the generation request from the composer state.
The client posts to /api/media/image/generate. Mobile and the CLI post to the same path; mobile adds an Idempotency-Key header and async:true so the server returns a job handle.

The route checks CSRF, the rate limit, the adult-eligibility gate for media-image, the managed-compute gate, the organisation policy gate, and the workspace spend cap, in that order. Each returns a refusal response when it fails.

how_it_works.detail: The managed flow loads the entitlement. No subscription gives 403 subscription_required. A plan without image_generation gives 403 plan_upgrade_required. Then the canUseImages capability is asserted.

guide.area: Image editor (area 45): edit, select, remix, transparency, versions and related image tools
guide.what_it_is_for: A person can change a picture they already have, or make a new one from a picture they own. They upload a photo or pick one from their library, describe the change in plain words, and get a new version back. The original stays available, so a bad edit costs nothing. The area matters because the image tools are the visible proof that the product can do what the leading chat assistants do with pictures.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user who is on a plan that includes image generation (the capability is named canUseImages and is granted to the PRO tiers). Free users get an upgrade prompt instead. Editing also needs a model whose catalog entry says it can edit (supports_edit). The code does not show a workspace-admin or developer-only path for this area. The CLI and the chat extension use a different, narrower path (see notes).

features.name: Attach a photo and describe a change
features.use: Turns an attached photo into the source image, then applies a typed instruction to it.
how_people_use_it: In the web or desktop chat, switch the composer to image mode.
Attach a photo with the paperclip or by drag and drop.
Pick an operation from the menu: Edit or Variation (Mask edit appears only after a mask is attached).
Type the change and press Send.
how_it_should_work: The photo becomes the source for the edit; the typed text is the instruction.
If the chosen model cannot edit, the composer shows a notice and does not send.
While the job runs, a generating card shows. On failure, a message says what went wrong and a retry is offered.
Mobile: the first attached photo is edited, up to four photos in total; the rest only guide the result.
Free plans are refused with an upgrade message.
features.on_each_app: Web and desktop (desktop shows the hosted web app): done. Mobile: done, but the edit is only the Edit operation with up to 4 photos; no mask or Variation. CLI and Chrome: missing (CLI can only generate new images).

features.name: Remix an earlier image
features.use: Starts a new edit from an image made earlier, in this chat or an older one.
how_people_use_it: Web: in the card of an image, choose Edit (opens the revision panel) for this chat's images. From the Library, choose Remix on an image row.
Mobile: open the Library, long-press or open the row action menu, choose Remix.
Type the change and send.
how_it_should_work: Remix loads the saved file, its original prompt and its aspect ratio into the composer in image mode.
An image from an old chat is reachable only through the Library.
If the file is too large to load, the Library shows a clear message and asks the person to add it from the device.
Only image files can be remixed; other files show an error.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (Library Remix plus the card's Edit). Mobile: the brief says missing, but the code has a Remix action in the Library (see things that look wrong). CLI and Chrome: missing.

features.name: Paint the area to change (mask and selection)
features.use: The person paints over the part of the picture that should change. Only the painted part is redrawn.
how_people_use_it: In the revision panel, press Select area and paint with the mouse or finger over the image.
Press Clear selection to remove the paint, or Cancel selection to leave the mode.
Composer alternative: press the Edit menu and choose Mask edit, which opens a dialog titled Select the area to change; paint, then press Use this area.
Or attach a PNG mask file with Add mask (it must be the same size as the image and have transparency).
how_it_should_work: The painted area shows as a semi-transparent tint over the image before sending.
Only the painted part is redrawn; the rest should stay the same. The UI warns that nearby content may also change.
The mask is a PNG where painted pixels are transparent. The server refuses a mask that is not a PNG, has no transparency, or is a different size, with a clear message, before any charge.
Brush size is fixed (about 5 percent of image width, minimum 8 pixels). There is no eraser, no undo, no brush size control and no invert.
Mobile does not offer painting.
features.on_each_app: Web: partly done. Select area, Clear selection and the composer Mask edit dialog work; brush size, eraser, invert and the overlay labels are missing. Desktop: the brief says done; the desktop app shows the hosted web app, so the web code applies (not separately checked). Mobile and CLI and Chrome: missing.

how_people_use_it: Not built. There is no click-to-comment control in the code.

Currently nothing exists to test.

features.use: Asks for an image with a see-through background (the subject on transparent), and keeps transparency through storage and download.

how_it_works.step: Pick the operation and attachments in the composer
how_it_works.detail: The composer lists three operations (Edit, Variation, Mask edit). Mask edit appears only after a mask is attached. A flag decides whether the image model can edit. In the send path, the source photo, optional mask and reference photos are read to base64 and an edit object is built.

The result card opens a revision panel. Describing a change, Variation, or Select area each build an edit request. The panel only offers editing when the model supports it; otherwise it generates a new image from the text.

how_it_works.step: Paint the mask in the browser
how_it_works.detail: A canvas sits over the image. Dragging paints strokes at a fixed width. On release, the painted pixels become transparent in an exported PNG, which is the area to change.
For a new aspect ratio, the browser draws the image centred on a larger canvas and marks the new border as the area to draw. Both are sent as PNG.

how_it_works.step: Send to the managed image route
how_it_works.detail: The client sends the request with an idempotency key. Before any work, the route checks the CSRF token, a rate limit, the age gate, the managed-compute gate, the organisation policy, the spend limit, and the canUseImages capability.

how_it_works.step: Check the source, mask and model on the server
how_it_works.detail: The source, mask and references are read (from inline bytes or stored assets) and their hashes saved. The mask must be a PNG with transparency and the same size as the source. A model whose catalog entry is not an editing API is refused before any charge.

how_it_works.step: Save a durable job and run it
how_it_works.detail: The job row keeps the plan (source, mask and reference asset ids, transparency flag) and the hashes. The executor reloads the stored images, so a retry must match what was charged.

The adapter sends a multipart form with the source, optional references and mask, plus the transparency setting. Every edit operation goes to the same edit endpoint; the operation name only changes the label of the model returned.

how_it_works.step: Show the result and keep the old one
how_it_works.detail: The page writes the new image URL into the message metadata and adds the previous image to imageVersions. The card shows a pager for earlier versions.

key_files.role: Result card and revision panel: Describe-a-change, Variation, Select area, Add mask, Aspect ratio, Clear selection, version pager.
Canvas where the person paints the area; exports the mask PNG (painted = transparent).

Mask dialog opened from the composer's Mask edit operation.
Shared client helpers: build the edit request, read files to base64, build the reframe (outpaint) padding.
HTTP entry for image generation; runs the gates and hands off to the managed generator.
Checks the edit request, the model's edit support and the mask, then creates the durable job.
Runs queued jobs; rebuilds the edit context from stored assets and checks the hashes.
Provider adapter: sends the multipart edit request and reads the result.
Server-side mask validation: PNG, has transparency, same size as the source.
Shared contract: the list of operations (generate, edit, inpaint, outpaint, variation) and which image API shapes accept edits.
Web page logic that regenerates an image in place and stores previous versions.
Mobile decision logic: checks gates, reference images and transparency, then builds the request.
Mobile runner: sends the generation, keeps edit retries for three recent failures.

guide.what_it_is_for: A person writes a text prompt, picks a video model and the clip's length, shape and size, and gets a generated video back in the chat. The clip can be watched, downloaded, shared (mobile) and retried after a failure, and the person sees a cost estimate and a progress bar while it is made. Video is a paid, server-run feature, so the server checks the person's plan, budget and admin policy before it starts any job.
guide.who_uses_it: Only signed-in users on the top two paid plan tiers. The code keys this to the plan capability video_generation, which lists max_15x and enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357). Users with no subscription get a subscription_required error, and lower plans get plan_upgrade_required (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:941-1001). Workspace admins affect it through the organization policy and model-policy gates (route.ts:917-931, 1181-1187) and the workspace spend limit (route.ts:935-936). A limited free video offer is also shown in the web composer (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1299-1305, 1347-1348). Video is managed-cloud only. No local or own-key video path was seen.

features.name: Write a prompt and pick the clip options
features.use: The main video flow. A person writes what the clip should show, picks which video model makes it, and sets the length, shape and resolution. The server only accepts combinations that the chosen model supports.
how_people_use_it: On web, switch the composer into video mode, type a prompt and press send. Video mode and image mode cannot be on at the same time (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1116-1123).
Open the video model menu and pick a model (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1413, 6549-6685 for the menus).
Open the aspect menu, the quality (resolution) menu and the duration menu. Each menu shows only the options the chosen model supports (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1421-1443).
On mobile, open the add-to-chat sheet, choose the video option, set the options and send (AddToChatSheet.tsx:214-219, 269-326). Mobile video is off in v1 (see things_that_look_wrong).
how_it_should_work: Before a job is started, the server checks the prompt, the model, the duration, resolution, aspect and audio choice against the model's video contract (route.ts:446-481, 1206-1219). An unsupported combination returns a validation error, not a silent change.
Default aspect is 16:9 and default resolution is 720p (route.ts:1206; managed-media.ts:197). Default duration is 4 seconds (managed-media.ts:196).
Prompts are limited to 2000 characters by the shared schema (managed-media.ts:195). The server also limits prompts for one provider to 1,000 characters (route.ts:1209-1211).
Pickers are hidden when a promotional (free offer) model is selected (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6549, 6602, 6656), so the options are fixed.

Empty state: when no video model is live or configured, the server returns a service-unavailable error (route.ts:389-411). The web composer offers video models only when the account can use video and the model is admitted (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1338-1353).
features.on_each_app: Web: done in the web composer (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1116-6685) with all four pickers and the send path. Desktop: the public desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so it has the same controls. Mobile: the add-to-chat sheet has the model, aspect, resolution and duration options (AddToChatSheet.tsx:214-326), but the video option is hidden in v1 by a feature flag. Chrome: not present.

features.name: Cost estimate
features.use: Shows a rough credit cost before the person sends a video, so they can see if it is more than their spendable credits.
how_people_use_it: Choose a model and options in the web composer. A small note reading About (amount) appears next to the controls (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6705).
Hover or focus the note to read the full wording. It is a role=note with the full text in aria-label (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:30-43).
how_it_should_work: The estimate comes from estimateVideoCredits for the chosen model, resolution, aspect and duration (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:24). If there is no estimate, nothing is shown (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:25).
If the estimate is more than the spendable credits now, the note turns to the warning colour and says so (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:28-31, 42).
The final cost is settled only on delivery, and a failed video costs nothing. The note says this (VideoCostEstimate.tsx:32).

On the server, the cost is computed per request from the model's pricing and the chosen resolution and audio (route.ts:485-520, 1223-1237), and the video-seconds allowance is checked before any job is created (route.ts:1238-1256).
features.on_each_app: Web: done in the web composer (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6705). Desktop: the public desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so it shows the same note. Mobile: the estimate is computed in AddToChatSheet.tsx:303-326 and shown in the sheet (AddToChatSheet.tsx:887, 1114-1145), but mobile video is off in v1. Chrome: not present.

features.name: Progress and stop
features.use: While a clip is being made, the person sees a progress bar and status text, and can press Stop to ask the server to cancel the job.
how_people_use_it: Send a video. The chat shows a placeholder with a progress bar (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:246-255).
Press Stop generating (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:257-271). The button reads Stopping while the request is sent, and it disappears once the server accepts the stop.
how_it_should_work: The client polls the status endpoint about every 5 seconds, and stops after 5 minutes (useMediaGeneration.ts:94-95, 639-669). Progress is shown as a percentage when the server reports one (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:65-67).
Stop sends the task id to the cancel endpoint (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:287-314). The server marks the job as cancel-requested (cancel route.ts:96-100).
For a provider that cannot stop a started video, the server records the request, and the result is not delivered and not charged. The message says the provider cannot stop it (cancel route.ts:56-57).
Only one provider has a server-side stop call. It is attempted once and the result is checked afterward (video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:465-490).
If the stop request fails, the placeholder shows an alert with a message and the stop button comes back (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:276-282, 313-314).
Terminal jobs (completed, failed, outcome unknown) cannot be cancelled. The server returns their current state (cancel route.ts:42-44, 94).
features.on_each_app: Web: done (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx, useMediaGeneration.ts). Desktop: same web code path. Mobile: progress is shown by VideoGenProgress.tsx:89-95 and polled in videogen.ts:109-163 with a shouldCancel check (videogen.ts:157-158). The mobile stop call is videogen.ts:124-126, and mobile library cancel is libraryClient.ts:184-187. Mobile video is off in v1. Chrome: not present.

features.name: Try again after a failure
features.use: Lets the person run a failed video again with the same settings and inputs.
how_people_use_it: On web, a failed video message shows a retry button when the server marks the failure as retryable (MessageBubble.tsx:3353-3363). Pressing it calls the chat's retry handler (WebChatPage.tsx:7761).

On mobile, a failed video in the chat shows a Retry video generation button (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:2570), and the library shows a Try again button when a job is retryable (MediaJobsSection.tsx:236-242).
how_it_should_work: The retry uses the original prompt and settings: the server stores them in the message metadata, and videoRetryInputs.ts:9-15 rebuilds the inputs.
The retry is only offered when the server marks the failure as retryable (MessageBubble.tsx:3353).
The retry must start a new job through the same generate route, so the same plan, budget and policy checks run again (route.ts:884-1001).
features.on_each_app: Web: done (WebChatPage.tsx:3192-3489 area, handleRetryVideo at 7761, videoRetryInputs.ts). Desktop: same web code. Mobile: the chat retry button exists (MessageBubble.tsx:2570) but mobile video is off in v1. The library Try again button sends video jobs to the image retry endpoint, which looks wrong (see things_that_look_wrong). Chrome: not present.

features.name: Clip library, playback, download and share
features.use: Finished clips can be found in one library, watched in the product, saved as a file, and (on mobile) sent to another app.
how_people_use_it: Open the library and choose the Videos filter (LibraryView.tsx:95, 111).

Press play on a clip in the library or in the chat. The web player is a video element with the test id library-video-player (LibraryView.tsx:1293-1295) and an in-chat video element (MessageBubble.tsx:3438).
Press Download video in the chat (MessageBubble.tsx:3419-3423), or Download in the library (library/index.tsx:450-451 on mobile).
On mobile, press share on a clip (GeneratedVideo.tsx:79, library/index.tsx:450-451).
how_it_should_work: Finished videos are served from the file route with a 256 MB cap for video (files route:46) and a check that the stored bytes match the signed-in person's asset (files route:258-286).
If the stored bytes are missing, the server returns Video bytes are not available (files route:260, 276).
Library lists are filtered to image and video items by MIME type (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:53, 125 excludes video from one query).
Share and download on mobile use the device file system and share sheet (library/index.tsx:450-456, GeneratedVideo.tsx:79).
Web share is not present. The brief says web share is missing, and no web share code was seen.
features.on_each_app: Web: play, download and the library are done (MessageBubble.tsx:3396-3454, LibraryView.tsx:327-328). Desktop: same web code and the shared library view. Mobile: play (VideoPlayerModal.tsx:15-20, GeneratedVideo.tsx:29), download and share (GeneratedVideo.tsx:52, 131; library/index.tsx:450-451). Web share is missing. Chrome: not present.

features.name: Start from an image or video
features.use: A person gives the model a starting image (first frame) or several reference images. Video-to-video is not built.
how_people_use_it: On web, attach one image and choose First frame, or attach several images and they are treated as references (ChatComposerNew.tsx:604-606, 1574, 6501-6519).
The chosen mode is sent as first_frame_image or reference_images (video-input-images.ts:37-50; schema managed-media.ts:209-215).
how_it_should_work: Accepted images are PNG, JPEG and WebP only (route.ts:754-758; video-input-images.ts:15-23).

A first frame allows one image. Reference images are limited by the model's declared maximum (managed-media.ts:176-188; video-input-images.ts:25-31). A model with no image input returns: cannot take input images (route.ts:794-798).
The image is checked against a hash denylist and a structure check; a match returns a 422 with a moderation rule id (route.ts:824-851).
If an image cannot be read, the server returns invalid_input_image and asks the person to attach it again (route.ts:808-818).
Both kinds cannot be sent together (managed-media.ts:222-224).
The input is only enabled when the model admission state is enabled (video-input-images.ts:29).
features.on_each_app: Web: partly built. First-frame and reference-image input exist (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6501-6519), but the brief lists them as missing. Video-to-video (S46.03) is not in the code. Desktop: same web code. Mobile: no input code for video (the mobile video request path has no first_frame or reference field). Chrome: not present.

features.name: Items that do not apply
features.use: Brief items marked not applicable to any app: camera motion, scene and action text, dialogue, a generated-audio switch, the job queue and save-to-project. Listed here so every brief item has a home.

how_it_works.step: 1. The person sets up the clip in the composer
how_it_works.detail: On web the composer keeps the video mode, model, aspect, resolution, duration and input-image choices as component state. Options come from the video catalog and the model's rules. On mobile the same choices live in a shared chat view store.

how_it_works.step: 2. Input images are read in the browser
how_it_works.detail: If images are attached, they are read as base64 for a first frame or as reference images. Only PNG, JPEG and WebP are accepted.
The web hook starts the generate call with the prompt, options and optional inputs, then records the task id. The mobile service sends the same request with a per-action idempotency key.

how_it_works.step: 4. The server checks the request and the person
how_it_works.detail: The generate route runs the rate limit, the age check, the managed-compute gate, the organization policy gate and the spend limit, then loads the subscription and checks the plan and the capability. A failed check returns a 403 or 503 with a code.

how_it_works.step: 5. The server picks and validates the model and provider
how_it_works.detail: A requested model must be an executable, live video model with a matching provider. Without a request, the server uses the routing slot's model. Provider keys must be set. The release policy then admits only the providers it allows. Duration, output size, audio and input-image counts are checked.

Input images are fetched, checked against a hash denylist and a structure check, and refused with a clear code if unreadable. The video-seconds allowance for the plan is checked. Cost is computed from the model pricing. Storage must be configured.

One job per candidate is written through the submit function, with idempotency keys. The route returns the job ids as queued. The job store and provider submission code are called from here but were not read.

The client polls the status endpoint every 5 seconds for up to 5 minutes, and reports progress. The web chat message carries the video status in its metadata. Mobile keeps the same fields on its chat message.
Stop calls the cancel endpoint. The server marks the job as cancel-requested and reconciles it once. Only the provider-specific path tries to stop the provider; others only stop delivery and billing.

how_it_works.step: 10. Finished clip is played, downloaded or shared
how_it_works.detail: The web file route streams the stored video bytes after an owner check. The chat bubble and the library show a video player and a download link. Mobile plays, downloads and shares the file through the device.

key_files.role: Server entry for a video request (POST at line 1869). Runs all plan, policy, model, input-image and budget checks, then creates the jobs.
Web composer: video mode, model, aspect, resolution and duration menus, input-image menu, cost note and send.
Web client hook: starts a video (startVideo, 570) and polls its status (watchVideo, 639).
Progress bar and the Stop generating button while a web video is made; calls the cancel endpoint.
Server cancel endpoint: records the cancel request, reconciles once and returns the cancellation state and message.
Shared video request schema (193-217) and input-image limits (176-188), used by the server and mobile.
Decides which paid video providers may be admitted. Only two of the three are admitted now.
Mobile client for video: start (with idempotency), status poll, cancel and the duration helper.
Mobile feature switch. videoGen is false in v1, which hides the mobile video option.
Shared library view for finished clips: Videos filter, inline video player and download, used across surfaces.
Serves the stored video bytes to the owner, with a 256 MB cap and an ownership check.
In-chat video result: the player, the Download video link and the Retry button for failed clips.

switches.name: Video plan capability
switches.effect: Only the top two paid tiers can start a video (max_15x and enterprise). Other plans get plan_upgrade_required.

switches.name: canUseVideoGeneration capability
switches.effect: Shows the video controls in the web composer and is asserted on the server before a job starts.

switches.name: Provider release policy
switches.effect: Only the listed providers may be admitted. Others are refused with a 503 while billing controls are finalized.

switches.name: Provider keys
switches.effect: A provider without its key is not configured and its models are not used.

switches.name: Routing slot for video
switches.effect: Chooses the default video model when the request does not name one.

switches.name: Model admission state
switches.effect: Input images are only allowed when the model's admission state is enabled. Promotional models show no pickers.

switches.name: Free video offer
switches.effect: A limited free video offer lets users without the plan see the controls with a limit.

switches.name: Rate limit, age gate and spend limit
switches.effect: Video requests are rate limited, need an age check, and stop when the workspace spend limit is reached.

switches.name: Mobile video feature flag
switches.effect: Hides the mobile video option in v1. The option also needs cloud mode and the video capability.

switches.name: Poll interval and timeout
switches.effect: How often and how long the client waits for a video.

switches.name: Input image limits
switches.effect: Maximum input images per model and provider.

switches.name: Video request ceiling
switches.effect: The maximum number of candidate clips per request.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the request schema and input-image limits (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts), used by the server route and mobile videogen.ts; the model catalog (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts) and the plan table (billing-catalog.ts); the library view (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx), which AGENTS.md section 5 says is shared by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code. Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so it runs the web code. Separate per app: the web composer and placeholder (ChatComposerNew.tsx, MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx, useMediaGeneration.ts), and the mobile composer, client and progress (AddToChatSheet.tsx, videogen.ts, VideoGenProgress.tsx, libraryClient.ts). There is also a second web library view at apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:42 that has its own cancel endpoint constant. Chrome and the CLI were not checked.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The brief marks the first-frame and reference-image inputs (S46.02, S46.04) as missing on web and desktop, but the web composer has a first-frame choice and a reference choice, and the server accepts both. Only video-to-video (S46.03) is absent from the code.

The brief marks mobile video as done, but the mobile video option is turned off in v1 (videoGen: false). The add-to-chat video option requires that flag, so the mobile video composer cannot show. The progress, cancel and share code still exists.
The library's Try again button for a video job calls the image retry endpoint. The image retry route only loads image jobs, so a video job retry likely fails. Not run; based on reading the code.

The brief says Cancel makes the job stop. For providers other than the one with a stop call, the server only stops delivery and billing; the provider keeps making the video. The server message says so.

The brief's line numbers do not match the code. For example ChatComposerNew.tsx:5081 and 5110 hold no video control (the controls are at 6501-6685 now), and model-catalog.ts:2304 is an image-model check (isExecutableImageModel), not a duration setting. The brief's route.ts:757 is the image MIME list (754-758), and the handler is at 1869.

The web model picker is built from the catalog with a live-status filter, not from the provider release policy. A model whose provider is not admitted may still be offered and then refused by the server with a 503. Not verified in the running app.

not_sure: Desktop: the brief says done. I assumed it runs the hosted web code (AGENTS.md section 5). I did not read any desktop-specific file.
Chrome extension, CLI and VS Code: not in the brief's status set. Not checked. The brief says Chrome is missing for every item.

Not opened: apps/web/app/api/media/video/status/route.ts, apps/web/lib/server/video-generation-jobs (job store), submitVideoCandidates (generate/route.ts from 1316), the provider output and webhook code, apps/web/features/media/services/media-api-service.ts, and the cost function (route.ts 485-520 was read only in part). Job table name and storage backend are therefore unverified.
Local (on-device) and own-key video: no path was seen. The route is the managed-cloud path only.
The request schema has a candidate count field n (managed-media.ts:207). The brief does not mention it, and no UI for it was found.

Frame rate, style presets, templates, characters, storyboards, remix, extend and segment regeneration: I checked the request schema and found no field for them. I did not search every UI file for these words, so a hidden or unfinished control could exist elsewhere.

Mobile stop button: the stop path exists in the service (videogen.ts:124-126, 157-158) and the chat turn (runVideoGenerationTurn.ts:43, 130-156), but no mobile stop control was located in the UI code read.
Web library: which of the two library views (packages/ui vs apps/web/features/library) the web app renders was not verified.
Plan naming: the code uses max_15x and enterprise. I did not map these to product plan names.
No tests, builds, installs or servers were run, as instructed. Everything above comes from reading the code. Nothing was checked at localhost.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is meant to let a person change a video after it is made. They could trim or join clips, extend a scene, ask in chat for a revised clip, keep one character looking the same across shots, add captions or sound, pick a thumbnail, see where a clip came from, and control who may use their likeness or remix their media. None of the 27 items exists as a working feature in any app. The brief marks 26 items "missing" and one, S47.11 (generated sound effects), "n/a" everywhere. The only video code in the repository is for making a clip from a prompt (area 46), plus one unapplied database draft for file history. Today a person can create a clip, but cannot edit it.
guide.who_uses_it: Intended: every signed-in person who makes video, plus anyone who wants to control their own likeness (avatar or cameo) and its reuse. Nothing in the code yet defines which plans get these features, and the audit note does not say. The existing video creation path is for signed-in users. The mobile app asks for cloud consent first, and the Chrome extension requires sign-in and reports plan-upgrade errors (apps/mobile/src/features/video/services/videogen.ts:94; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:100 and :14). Developers and QA are the only users of the audit note and the draft migration.

Preview the trimmed result, then save it as a new version

Plan limits: not defined in the code yet

Reorder them and confirm
For a continuation, choose Extend on a clip and write what happens next
how_it_should_work: A joined video plays the clips in the order shown
An extended shot starts from the last frame of the previous shot

Waiting state: progress shown while the video is built
Failure: the source clips are untouched and the user is told which step failed
Plan limits: not defined in the code yet

Type the change, for example a new style or a different background
Read the revised clip and keep it, or go back to the earlier one

Object or background changes only where the model supports them, and the app says so when it does not

Or attach a first frame, and a last frame where supported, in the video request

A first frame supplied by the user is the starting picture of the clip
A last frame is used only where the model supports it
Failure: an unsupported frame is refused with a message, not silently ignored
Plan limits: not defined in the code yet

Or choose Regenerate dialogue and edit the line

Regenerating dialogue keeps the picture unchanged

Sound effects (S47.11): brief says not applicable in every app, so no work is planned in the brief
features.on_each_app: S47.10 and S47.12 missing on all four apps. S47.11 is n/a on all four apps.

features.name: Captions
features.use: Create captions or subtitles for a clip, then correct them.

how_it_works.step: 1. The person asks for a video in the web chat, optionally with an image
how_it_works.detail: The chat page reads the kind of input image (first frame or reference) and sends it with the request.

how_it_works.step: 2. The web client builds the request fields
how_it_works.detail: A first frame becomes first_frame_image; reference images become reference_images.

how_it_works.step: 3. The shared request contract checks the input
how_it_works.detail: The contract allows a first_frame_image or reference_images, not both.

how_it_works.step: 4. The server route maps the input to the provider request
how_it_works.detail: The route turns the chosen input kind into the provider input and task type.

how_it_works.step: 5. The provider service sends frame images
how_it_works.detail: A first frame is sent with a first-frame marker; there is no code path for a last frame or for editing an existing clip.

how_it_works.step: 6. The mobile app starts a task and polls it
how_it_works.detail: It asks for cloud consent, sends an idempotency key so a retry does not bill twice, and then polls status every 5 seconds for up to 5 minutes.

how_it_works.step: 7. The Chrome extension starts a task with a prompt only
how_it_works.detail: It needs a signed-in token, maps plan-upgrade error codes, and checks the task id format.

how_it_works.step: 8. A finished clip is shown in the library, with a cancel action
how_it_works.detail: The mobile library lists video jobs and can cancel one. No edit, trim, caption or version action exists here.

how_it_works.step: 9. Stored history is only a draft
how_it_works.detail: The draft adds version and parent columns to media and artifact tables, a version history table and a lineage table. Its header says it is not applied, so nothing stored today supports S47.17 to S47.19.

guide.what_it_is_for: A person talks to the assistant out loud and hears it answer, inside a chat. The spoken turns land in the same transcript as typed turns, so the person can switch between talking and typing. It matters because it is the hands-free way to get work done, and it runs tools and approvals while the person is still talking.
guide.who_uses_it: Web and mobile live voice is gated by plan. The server checks the plan's allowVoice flag and returns a not-in-plan error otherwise (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:311-317). Plans with a free time allowance use that allowance; other plans use a budget check and a usage reservation (route.ts:346-373). Signed-in users only, since the route needs a user and a conversation (route.ts:246-262). Desktop uses the web code in its cloud window. The CLI has only push-to-talk speech-to-text, not live conversation (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-12). Workspace policy is checked through the managed-compute and training-opt-out gates (route.ts:290-340). Not verified: whether admin-only switches exist beyond those gates.

how_it_works.step: Person starts voice from a chat
how_it_works.detail: The chat page switches to voice mode when the voice session is active (WebChatPage.tsx:6671, 7201). On mobile the chat input's voice button starts a live session (ChatInput.tsx:1219, per brief). A new chat is created first if none exists (mobile voice.tsx:262-281).

how_it_works.step: Browser opens the microphone and the session
how_it_works.detail: The web session asks for the microphone with echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain control, then sends a WebRTC offer (a standard way to open a live audio link). Mute state is applied to the microphone track before and after the link opens.

The route checks the speech-provider key, the conversation id, the price table, the user's plan, the capability flag, the subscription access, the training opt-out and the Google user-data rule. Any failure returns a clear error code (403, 402, 503).
Plans with a free allowance get seconds from the free allowance. Other plans must fit a budget and a voice-minutes quota, then a usage reservation is made with a lease (ten minutes).

The route sends the offer to the realtime voice provider with the chosen voice, language, pace and reasoning. It blocks the browser from changing the backend model, tools or reasoning. Only mute and unmute are allowed from the browser.

how_it_works.step: Voice turns go into the chat and tools
how_it_works.detail: A finished spoken turn is sent as a normal chat message to the chosen model, and the reply is read back from the chat store. Tool output is trimmed before the voice model reads it. Approvals wait on screen.
Mute is sent to the realtime link. Pause ends the live link on web. Cancel-task ends pending delegations and tool work and tells the assistant the task stopped.
Ending closes the session on the server, which settles the usage. On web the session also ends when the page is hidden. On mobile the session ends when the app goes to background.

guide.what_it_is_for: A person speaks and the words land as text in the message box, so they can type less. The text can be checked and edited before it is sent. The same idea runs in the web app, the desktop app, the phone app, the command-line tool and the Chrome and VS Code extensions, but each app does the speech-to-text step in a different place. Most of the other items in the brief (meeting notes, speaker labels, timestamps, search, export of recordings) are not built yet.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user can dictate on web, desktop and CLI, subject to the dictation kill switch and the Voice setting. Web dictation is turned off in Local and own-key (BYOK) chats (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2052-2070). Free users get a monthly voice-minute allowance (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-51). Paid plans use managed usage reservations (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:596-604). Workspace organisations can be blocked by their policy and spend cap (route.ts:336-355). Developers can call the transcription API with an inference:write key (route.ts:294-299). On phones, dictation runs on the device and does not use the server at all (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:440-446). Whether a phone user must be signed in is not established (see not_sure).

features.name: Dictate into the message box
features.use: Lets a person speak a message instead of typing it. The text is added where the cursor is, ready to edit, or sent straight away on some apps.
how_people_use_it: Web and desktop: click the microphone button in the composer. Speak. Click the square stop button, or press Enter to stop and send. Press Escape or the X to discard.
Phone: tap the microphone to start, tap again to finish. Hold it to talk; releasing ends the recording. The first use shows an intro sheet.
Command line: press SPACE to start recording, then release SPACE or press ENTER to stop. Read the text, press ENTER to send, E to edit, R to re-record, ESC to discard.
Chrome extension: click the microphone to start; click again to stop. VS Code: the sidebar microphone records, then the text is added to the message.
how_it_should_work: Starts only after microphone permission is granted. Shows a live waveform while recording on web and desktop.
When recording ends, a spinner says Transcribing. Then the text is added to the end of the message field and the cursor moves to the end.
Empty result: web shows 'Nothing was heard in that recording. Try again.' Failures show a message with a Try again button (web) or an error note (phone).

Interim text (text that appears while the person is still speaking) is not in the brief as required (status n/a). The phone app does show a live transcript line while recording (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1976).
Undo of inserted text is not verified in any app (brief status 'unverified').

Limits: phone recording stops after 60 seconds (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:68). Command line and VS Code stop after 120 seconds (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:37; apps/extension-vscode/src/protocol/dictationLimits.ts MAX_DICTATION_MS). Web client sets no time limit that I found; the server caps the upload at 25 MB (route.ts:398-412).
features.on_each_app: Web: done, sends the recording to the server to transcribe. Desktop: done, same web code inside the desktop window; a global shortcut can also dictate into another app (see feature 'Desktop dictation into other apps'). Phone: done, on-device speech recognition, no upload, no retry. Command line: done, uploads the recording to the chosen backend and shows the text before anything is sent. Chrome extension: done, uses the browser's own speech recognition (no server); no discard control. VS Code: code exists for recording and upload (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:5779), but the brief says missing; needs a QA check.

features.name: Choose the dictation language
features.use: Sets the language the recognizer listens for, so speech in another language is transcribed correctly.
how_people_use_it: Web: Settings > Voice; the language follows the browser language by default.
Phone: Voice language screen; there are separate settings for the cloud and local chat modes.
Command line: a language argument is checked against a supported list (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:88-96).
Chrome extension: choice stored in the browser profile; VS Code: stored in editor settings.
how_it_should_work: Web sends only the main language code (for example 'de', not 'de-DE'), and drops a code it does not recognise so the server detects the language (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:213-217).

Phone uses the chosen language if set, else the device language (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/speechSettings.ts:17-31). On-device recognition needs the language model installed; if not, the user is told to install it (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:~321).
Unsupported command-line language stops with a list of supported languages.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (VoiceSection language state at apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.tsx:41-57). Desktop: done (same web code). Phone: done, per trust domain. Command line: done. Chrome extension: done (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/dictation-language.ts:14 uses sync storage). VS Code: done in code (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/dictationClient.ts:5).

features.name: Stop, discard and retry a recording
features.use: Lets a person end, throw away, or redo a recording without losing a long dictation.
how_people_use_it: Web and desktop: stop square ends and sends the audio; X discards; after a failure, Try again re-sends the same recording.
Command line: when transcription fails, press R to retry that recording, or any other key to drop it; ESC discards after the text is shown.
Phone: the X on the recording bar cancels (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1947).
how_it_should_work: Web keeps the failed recording in memory and retries it without re-recording, unless the failure was a plan or allowance refusal, in which case the recording is dropped (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:176, 186-213).
Discard drops the audio and inserts nothing (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:215-227).

Pause and resume are missing everywhere in the code I read. Recording duration is shown only in the command line, as whole seconds (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:762-771). Web, desktop and phone show no timer.
Phone has no retry: a failed transcription returns to idle with an error (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/VoiceInputButton.tsx:186-194).
features.on_each_app: Web: discard and retry done; pause and timer missing. Desktop: same as web. Phone: discard done; retry not found in code (brief says done, see things_that_look_wrong); pause and timer missing. Command line: retry, discard and timer done; pause missing. Chrome extension: no discard (stopping keeps the text); pause missing. VS Code: no pause or timer found.

features.name: Batch and file transcription
features.use: Turns a whole recording, or an uploaded audio file, into text in one request. This is the path the web and command-line apps use, and the one developers can call.
how_people_use_it: Apps: stop a recording and the whole clip is sent once (web, command line, VS Code).
Developers: send an audio file to the transcription API endpoint with a file field and an optional language (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts).
how_it_should_work: Accepted audio types are mpeg, mp4, m4a, wav, webm, ogg and flac; anything over 25 MB is refused with a 'file exceeds maximum size' message (route.ts:398-420).

The request is rate limited under the 'audio-transcription' limit (route.ts:294), must carry a valid sign-in or key (route.ts:297), and is refused when the dictation switch is off (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:18-26).

There is no end-user screen to upload an audio file in any app (S49.08 is missing in every app; API only). Phone file transcription (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:475-511) runs on the device only.
features.on_each_app: Web: batch done through the composer; file upload missing (no screen). Desktop: batch done (same web code). Phone: batch done on device; no file upload screen. Command line: batch done. Chrome extension: not applicable (browser speech). VS Code: batch done in code. API: both done.

features.use: A live spoken conversation where speech is transcribed as it is spoken and text appears while the person talks.
how_people_use_it: Web: the voice composer (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceComposer.tsx) with mute, type and end-session buttons.
Phone: the live voice bar with pause and an elapsed timer (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx).

Usage is counted against the same voice allowance and expired sessions are settled (route.ts:~598-640).
Command line has no streaming dictation.

features.use: Lets a person save a chat, including dictated messages, as a file, and delete chats. Audio download and separate recording retention are not built.
how_people_use_it: Web: conversation export dialog (apps/web/features/chat/components/dialogs/EnhancedExportDialog.tsx exists; not opened in detail).
Phone: conversation export sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ConversationExportSheet.tsx:96).

Deleting a chat removes its messages, which include the dictated text. There is no separate audio file to delete on web or phone because the audio is not kept.

It is shown once per install (apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:56, 134).

how_people_use_it: Turn on 'Dictate into the app you are using' in desktop settings (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:57, 380-384), grant accessibility access, then press the dictation shortcut while typing in another app. A small floating bar appears; press again to stop.

Text is cleaned: line breaks become spaces and invisible characters are removed (apps/desktop/electron/dictationElsewhere.ts:~50-75). Sessions stop after 10 minutes (dictationElsewhere.ts:45). Password and keychain windows are never typed into (dictationElsewhere.ts:17-27).
If typing fails, the text is copied to the clipboard and the person is notified (dictationElsewhere.ts deps copyText and notify).
