switches.name: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION
switches.effect: Turns cloud execution on when set to 1; without it, approvals and cloud session creation refuse with 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment'.

switches.name: E2B_API_KEY
switches.effect: Sandbox key. Its presence counts as enabled for the general check; cloud provisioning needs it plus the flag.

switches.name: Sandbox rate card (priceable check)
switches.effect: Cloud provisioning is ready only when the sandbox rate card declares a vCPU and memory rate pair.

switches.name: AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA (managed-compute beta gate)
switches.effect: Separate, broader managed-compute gate; the brief says it is on when unset.

switches.name: remote_control plan capability
switches.effect: Paid-plan check for Remote Control pairings; refusal is 403 with plan_upgrade_required, or 503 if the plan cannot be read.

switches.name: Screen-share switch (SCREEN_SHARE_CAPABILITY)
switches.effect: Remote Control is refused while this switch is closed; the file says the switch is defined in the feature registry.

switches.name: Workspace feature gate 'remote_control'
switches.effect: Workspace policy can refuse Remote Control for its members.

switches.name: SIGNALING_HTTP_URL and SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET
switches.effect: Both required for pairing; without them the claim returns 503 'Pairing is not configured'.

switches.name: NODE_ENV development (relay URL check)
switches.effect: Allows an insecure relay address in development only.

switches.name: Approval confirmation time limit
switches.effect: Two minutes for a native approval dialog on the computer before the allow is dropped.

switches.name: Insecure loopback relay (not packaged app)
switches.effect: Allows a non-secure local relay address only when the app is not packaged.

switches.name: Agent push preference
switches.effect: Turns activity pushes on or off per account.

switches.name: --yes flag on the hand-off command
switches.effect: Skips the confirmation prompt; without it and without a terminal, nothing moves.

guide.shared_code: Shared: packages/contracts/types/src/product-routes.ts (route prefixes for the web proxy and the desktop shell); packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/local-code-session-activity.ts (activity event schema); packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/remoteControlHost.ts (the remote-control host the desktop creates, apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts). The web server gates (apps/web/lib/e2b, apps/web/lib/feature-flags) are used by web API routes. Separate per app: web pages in apps/web/features/code and apps/web/app/api; the phone code in apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code and apps/mobile/src/features/companion; the desktop Electron runtime in apps/desktop/electron; the command line in apps/cli (Rust); the editor extension in apps/extension-vscode. The relay is a separate service in services/signaling-server.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The brief cites apps/web/app/code approvals route lines 139-140 for S68.11 (active control). The approvals route file ends at line 130, so those lines do not exist there.
The brief cites apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:124 for active-control attachment. Line 124 is an import line, not control code.

Brief marks web S68.11 (active control) as done, but its approval decisions are refused unless the cloud switch is on. The same switch is what the brief lists as off in production, and web S68.08 (pending approvals) is partial for that reason.
Approval listing (GET) has no cloud-switch check, while approval decisions (POST) do. A listed approval can be shown and then refused.
Brief marks phone S68.24 (start a session in an allowed folder) as missing, but the phone already has a start-session request that sends the task and folder to the computer.
Phone setup copy tells people to open Remote Control and pair a phone, while the brief says Remote Control is hidden in the first mobile release. The code that hides it was not found.

Phone pairing claim is a web route, but the brief lists the web pairing status as partial. Its unfinished note says the claim returns 503 until the website deploy is live-checked; the code returns 503 when the relay settings are missing.

not_sure: Whether Remote Control is hidden in the first mobile release (stated in the owner's notes and the brief). The hiding code was not found; only the copy that points to it was seen.
Which plan tiers include the remote_control capability. The check was read; the tier table was not opened.
The database table or store used for cloud sessions and approvals. Only the access wrapper was seen.

Where the relay keeps pairing codes (getSessionByCode in the signaling store) and how revocation works (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:95, apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts:1223, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/index.ts:206 were cited by the brief and not opened).

Whether the command line has any remote-folder start or pairing code (S68.22-S68.25 for the command line are marked missing in the brief; the command line's remote host files apps/cli/src/tui/remote_host.rs and apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs were cited but not opened).
The export file format and where it is written (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3887 and apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:375 were not opened).
The web, desktop and phone items marked missing (S68.05, S68.07, S68.12, S68.16, S68.18, S68.27) were taken from the brief and not checked in code, except where stated.
The sessions list and the desktop's stored approval state beyond memory (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:892 and the desktop-side pending store were not opened).
Whether a cloud session's history is the same across clients is taken from the brief; the server transcript read path was not followed.

The VS Code session-sheet and context-handoff code paths beyond the lines cited (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/context-handoff/index.ts:72-202 were partly read; webviewContent.ts and ChatStateManager.ts were not).
No tests, builds, installs or servers were run, as the task required. The work is read only from the project folder.

guide.what_it_is_for: A signed-in person opens the AGI Workforce web app in a browser, chats with the assistant, and can switch the composer to Work mode for multi-step runs that use tools. The area also covers the parts that make a browser app feel finished: links that open a conversation, a layout that fits phone, tablet and desktop, browser notifications for finished runs, export, and public share pages for people who are not signed in.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person using a browser (chat page at /chat and /chat/<id>). Work mode is paid-plan only: the composer hides it for free-trial accounts (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066) and the server refuses it below the plan tier (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1484-1500). Cloud code execution is on by default and can be switched off per account. Signed-out visitors see the marketing page at / (apps/web/proxy.ts, buildHomeResponse is only used for the signed-in path) and can open public share links (/share/[token], /shared-artifact/[token]). Browser notifications are per browser and per account. Workspace members can open organization-visible shares through the scoped database read (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:28-47). Workspace admins and developers are not identified in this area.

features.name: Chat page and Work mode
features.use: The main place to chat with the assistant in a browser. Work mode (labelled Work in the composer, with a translated label key composer.modeAgiWork) runs multi-step tasks with tools on paid plans.
how_people_use_it: Sign in, open the chat page, type in the composer and press the send control.
Use the Chat / Work mode toggle in the composer to switch mode (handler: ChatComposerNew.tsx:2806-2815).
Type a slash command such as /code (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3247-3253) to turn on cloud code execution for that message.
how_it_should_work: Work mode is offered only when the plan allows it (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066). A free-trial account never sees it.
The server refuses Work mode below the paid tier with error code agi_work_plan_required and the message that Work needs a paid plan (request-processor.ts:1484-1500).
Empty state: /chat is the new-chat surface. No conversation is saved until the first send (WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2358 comment).
Waiting state: the reply streams in. Tool activity shows as tool status updates (useChatStream.ts:3488-3500).
Offline: send is refused with the notice 'You are offline. Your draft is saved here and can be sent after you reconnect.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:717, 3588-3590).
Failure: send failures surface through the chat error state; the specific failure paths were not traced end to end.
features.on_each_app: Web only in the brief (status: web done). The brief gives no status for the other apps.

features.name: Responsive layout
features.use: One shell that adapts to phone, tablet and desktop widths so navigation does not cover the reading column on small screens.
how_people_use_it: Phone: tap the header control 'Open navigation' to open the drawer.
Portrait tablet: the sidebar stays as an icon rail; tap it to expand over the content.
Landscape tablet or wide desktop: the sidebar stays persistent; the collapse toggle hides it.
Rotate the device or resize the window; the reading position is kept.
how_it_should_work: Below 768px width: compact tier, navigation is a modal drawer (app-shell-layout.ts:24-48; WebAppShell.tsx:684-700).
768px to 1023px in portrait: icon rail that expands over the content. In landscape at that width: persistent sidebar.
1024px and wider: persistent sidebar.
The drawer closes after any navigation (WebAppShell.tsx effect on pathname, around line 210).
A manual collapse choice survives a resize to a wider window (WebAppShell.tsx:190-198 comment).
The first paint assumes a wide window so a mobile header does not flash (app-shell-layout.ts comment before the server layout constant).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief. The shell is in apps/web and is not shared with the other apps.

features.name: Links, history, refresh and other tabs
features.use: Every conversation has its own address, so links, Back and Forward, and reload all return to the same conversation. The unsent draft survives a reload.
how_people_use_it: Click a conversation in the sidebar; the address changes to /chat/<id>.
Send the first message in a new chat; the address changes to /chat/<id> after the send.
Press Back or Forward; press reload.
Open a copied /chat/<id> link in a new tab.
how_it_should_work: A new chat lives at /chat. After the first send, the page replaces the address with /chat/<id> (WebChatPage.tsx:5792 and 6711).
Opening /chat/<id> loads that conversation if it is not already in local state (WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2358 and the code below it).
Back and Forward use the router's history entries; the artifact panel listens for popstate to reopen the artifact named in the address (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:638).
Reload restores the conversation from the address and the draft from browser storage (composer-draft-storage.ts; ChatComposerNew.tsx:4157).

Several tabs: there is no live sync of messages between tabs. The open conversation is re-fetched when the tab regains focus or becomes visible, at most once per minimum gap (WebChatPage.tsx:2331-2339). The unread-count store does sync across tabs through storage events (unread-conversations-store.ts:63).
Failure when the address names a conversation that does not exist: not traced.
features.on_each_app: Web only. The brief marks the multi-tab item not applicable, but the code has a partial cross-tab refresh (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Drag, drop, paste and copy
features.use: Put files into a message by dropping or pasting them, paste text or code, and copy a message out.
how_people_use_it: Drag files over the browser window; a 'Drop files here' overlay appears; release to attach.
Paste with the keyboard shortcut for paste into the composer; text, code or files are handled.
Open the '+' menu and choose attach from clipboard (this reads the clipboard only on that click).
Click the copy control on a message; a 'Copied to clipboard' toast appears.
how_it_should_work: Drop: every dropped file goes to the attachment intake (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2301-2303, 2223), which enforces the file-count and size limits and names any file it refuses (use-attachments.ts:447-448).
The overlay shows 'Up to N files' from the per-plan limit (DragDropOverlay.tsx:113-115; ChatComposerNew.tsx:919-920).

Paste: a shared decision says whether the clipboard becomes text or an attachment (packages/platform/utils/src/composerPaste.ts:131). Long code pasted as text is fenced and can be undone (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2372-2396).
Copy: a message is copied as plain text, rich blocks flattened for assistant messages (MessageBubble.tsx:2273-2282).
Failure: a clipboard refusal on copy is not caught in the handler (see things_that_look_wrong).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief. The paste decision is shared with the other surfaces through the platform utilities package (composerPaste.ts).

features.name: Microphone, camera and screen access
features.use: Use the microphone for dictation or a live voice call, share the camera in voice mode, and capture the screen for a feedback report.
how_people_use_it: Click the microphone button in the composer; allow the browser prompt; speak; the transcript fills the composer.
Start voice mode; press 'Share your camera' to send camera frames with the call.
Open the feedback dialog and use the screen capture control to attach a picture of the screen.
how_it_should_work: The browser is asked for the microphone only when a feature needs it (voice-input-store.ts:280-288; live-voice-session.ts:480-486).

A refused microphone shows 'Microphone permission denied. Please allow access in your browser settings.' (voice-input-store.ts:451-452). Other errors have their own messages (voice-input-store.ts:454-466).
Recovery: after the refusal, a change of the browser's microphone permission to granted retries the live session automatically (use-voice-session.ts:903-925).

Camera: the request is made in the shared visual capture module with a user-facing or environment camera choice (packages/contracts/types/src/visual-session-capture.ts:77-91), used by apps/web/lib/visual/use-visual-session.ts:40. The camera control is hidden when the desktop host bridge is present (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:257-258).

Screen: the feedback dialog asks for one screen frame, draws it to a PNG, and stops the capture tracks (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:54-69). It is offered only when the browser supports it (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:94-96).
Failure states beyond the messages above were not traced.
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief. The brief marks screen sharing 'not applicable anywhere', but the web feedback dialog captures the screen (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Cloud code execution
features.use: Lets the assistant run code and create files in a cloud sandbox during a chat turn. A switch in Settings refuses it.
how_people_use_it: Type /code, or ask in words that clearly ask to run code or analyse data; the server can turn execution on for that turn (request-processor.ts:1003-1013).
Open Settings, then Capabilities, and turn 'Cloud code execution and file creation' off or on (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:108-121).
Turning code execution on also forces artifacts on (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:52, 142-151).
how_it_should_work: The setting is saved in the account's user settings under capabilities.cloudCodeExecution (code-execution-policy.ts:7-8, 33-36). An absent setting means enabled.

When the setting is off, the model is told that execution is disabled and the tool call is refused (tool-loop.ts:2814-2836). The code-runs route refuses with a forbidden error (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/code-runs/route.ts:106-110).
If the setting cannot be read, execution is refused, not allowed (code-execution-policy.ts:43-48).
Execution tools are offered only when the sandbox service is configured and the turn streams (lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-26; lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:258-269).
A platform kill switch named canUseCloudExecution also turns execution off (request-processor.ts:5236, 6417-6419).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief (web done). The Settings copy says the sandbox can reach only package registries and code hosting; this was not verified.

features.name: Cloud browser and desktop control
features.use: Intended to let the assistant drive a cloud browser, and let a browser tab control a paired desktop host. Neither exists on the web app as far as the code shows.
how_people_use_it: Not available from the web app. The Remote Control section in Settings renders nothing unless the desktop host bridge is present (RemoteControlSection.tsx:166).
how_it_should_work: Cloud browser: no code found by searching apps/web for cloud browser terms in features, lib and app.
Remote control: its gate is the screen share switch (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts header comment), and the server refuses pairing while that switch is closed.
Expected behaviour per the brief: a browser tab can send work to a paired desktop and see its screen. Not present on web.
features.on_each_app: Web missing per the brief. The desktop shell is the only surface where the remote-control UI renders, per the desktop-host gate.

features.name: Browser notifications
features.use: Get a system notification when an agent run or long task finishes, even with the tab closed. Clicking it opens the run.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, then Notifications, and turn on browser (web push) notifications; allow the browser prompt.
Turn the same switch off to remove this browser's subscription.
Click the notification to focus or open the run.
how_it_should_work: Enabling: the browser permission is requested first; a denied answer returns 'denied' (web-push-client.ts:168-186).
If the server has no key pair, the result is 'unavailable' and nothing is offered (web-push-client.ts:74-88; /api/web-push GET returns the public key).

If another account used this browser earlier, the server refuses to move the endpoint (403) and the client takes a fresh endpoint for this account (web-push-client.ts:120-150; apps/web/app/api/web-push/route.ts:84-99).

Sending: agent-run events call sendPushToUser (agent-notification-service.ts:140-170), which checks quiet hours (push-notification-service.ts:281-291) and then sends through the web push service (web-push-service.ts:346-389).
Clicking the notification focuses an open tab on the same path or opens a new window (public/sw.js:81-95).
Not offered in the desktop shell (web-push-client.ts:33-40).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief (web done).

features.name: Install and offline
features.use: Install the site as an app from the browser, and see a clear notice when the connection drops.
how_people_use_it: Use the browser's install or add-to-home-screen action (not run in this review).
Go offline and try to send; read the notice; reconnect and send the kept draft.
how_it_should_work: The site ships a web app manifest: name, standalone display, icons, start URL '/' (apps/web/app/manifest.ts:4-30).
For a signed-in visitor, '/' is rewritten to the chat root (apps/web/proxy.ts buildHomeResponse, CHAT_ROOT_PATH). A signed-out visitor keeps the marketing page.

Offline: the composer tracks the online state (ChatComposerNew.tsx:842), refuses to send with a notice, and keeps the draft (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3588-3590, 4806). The shared offline indicator is mounted in the app runtime (AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:25; OfflineIndicator.tsx:31).
The only service worker caches nothing and intercepts no fetches (public/sw.js:4-7), so there is no offline page and no read-only cache of old content.
The offline queue module is started by the indicator but only the code feature enqueues into it (features/code/hooks/use-local-session.ts:813). Chat does not use it.
features.on_each_app: Web only. The brief marks both items not applicable, while the code has an install manifest, an offline notice and an indicator.

features.name: Export and download
features.use: Export a conversation to a file, or download the artifacts of a conversation.
how_people_use_it: Open the chat header menu and choose Export (WebChatPage.tsx:7408; dialog at WebChatPage.tsx:7934).
Pick Markdown, PDF, Word (DOCX), HTML or JSON; optionally change the file name, include timestamps and, for Markdown, metadata; press download.
In the artifacts panel, use the download-all action (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:737-740).
how_it_should_work: The conversation is turned into the chosen format in the browser (EnhancedExportDialog.tsx:99-160; ChatExportService at features/chat/services/conversation-export.ts:83).
The default file name is the conversation title with non-letter and non-digit characters replaced by hyphens (EnhancedExportDialog.tsx:112-115).
Progress and result show as a toast for artifacts (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:737-740). Export failure messages were not traced.
Export covers the conversation text. Attachments and per-message files are not part of the export dialog.
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief (web done).

features.name: Browser checks and support message
features.use: Check that the browser has the features the app needs, and say so clearly when it does not.
how_people_use_it: Open the site in an old browser: a red-bordered alert line appears at the top.
Turn JavaScript off: a notice asks for JavaScript or a supported browser.
Use the microphone button in a browser without microphone support: a short hint appears for three seconds.
how_it_should_work: An inline script checks Object.hasOwn, structuredClone, Array.prototype.at, fetch and a lookbehind regular expression; if one is missing it un-hides the notice (app/layout.tsx:144-157; lib/browser-support.ts:1-11).
Supported browsers named in the notice: Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari (lib/browser-support.ts:1).
Voice input checks for the media API before starting and shows a hint if missing (VoiceInputButton.tsx:16, 26-30, 50-54).
Web push checks for service workers, the push API and Notification before offering the switch (web-push-client.ts:34-41).
The feedback dialog offers screen capture only when the display-capture call exists (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:94-96).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief (web done).

features.name: Public share and preview pages
features.use: A signed-out person opens a shared conversation or a published artifact from a link, and can report it.
how_people_use_it: Open /share/<token> for a shared conversation, or /shared-artifact/<token> for a published artifact.
Use the report link at the bottom of the page.
how_it_should_work: Public rows are read first; otherwise a signed-in viewer's scoped read may show organization-visible rows (share/[token]/page.tsx:28-47).
A malformed or expired shared conversation returns the standard not-found page (share/[token]/page.tsx:107-111).
A malformed or revoked published artifact shows an 'unavailable' page; an invite-only artifact shows an invite page (shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:69-77).
Link preview: the page title is the conversation or artifact title plus ' - AGI', with noindex (share/[token]/page.tsx generateMetadata).
The viewer shows 'Expires' with a relative time (SharedSessionViewer.tsx:93); system messages are removed from the shared view (share/[token]/page.tsx:50-53).
Both pages show the report link (ReportContentLink).
features.on_each_app: Web only per the brief (web done).

how_it_works.detail: A person opens /chat or /chat/<id>. The proxy stamps the real path in a header when it rewrites /agi-work to chat, and the chat page reads that header to start in Work mode. The chat itself is loaded only in the browser (no server rendering) through a dynamic import.
The shell reads the window size and orientation and chooses drawer, rail or persistent sidebar. It re-checks on resize and rotation.
Typing is saved as a draft in browser storage. Dropped files and pasted files go to the attachment intake, which applies per-plan limits and names refused files.

how_it_works.step: 4. Send is checked in the browser
how_it_works.detail: Sending checks for offline, for an empty message and for a pending slash command. It also warns once if the text looks like it holds a secret. Then the message goes to the streaming hook.
The streaming hook first checks whether the model is a local one; a local turn never reaches the server. Other turns are sent to the chat endpoint chosen for the model, with the owner's auth token.
The chat route checks auth, rate limit, subscription and managed compute, then takes a turn slot and dispatches the turn.

how_it_works.step: 7. Work mode and tools are set
how_it_works.detail: Work mode turns on web tools and code execution for the turn, unless the person excluded them. The plan is checked for Work. Code execution tools are added only when the sandbox is ready and the kill switch is on. The tool loop checks the user's own switch before running any code.
The browser reads the server-sent event stream, decodes frames, and updates the message, tool status, searching and code-running states.

how_it_works.step: 9. The address and history follow the conversation
how_it_works.detail: After the first send in a new chat, the address changes to /chat/<id>. Opening an address loads its conversation. Focus or visibility changes re-fetch the open conversation.
When an agent run or cloud code turn finishes, the server sends a push to the account's registered browsers; the service worker shows it and opens the run on click.

key_files.role: Route for /chat; reads the proxy header to start in Work mode.
Main chat page: URL loading, history, export and share dialogs, focus refresh, message actions.
Composer: send checks, Chat/Work toggle, drop, paste, attachments, drafts, offline refusal, slash commands.
Sends a turn to the chat endpoint and reads the streamed reply and tool status.
Server entry for one chat turn: auth, admission, dispatch.
Server work-mode setup, Work plan gate, code-execution tool choice, kill-switch check.
Checks the user's code-execution switch before any code tool runs.
Responsive shell: drawer, icon rail, persistent sidebar, scroll and focus handling.
Pure width and orientation rules for the shell (768px and 1024px breakpoints).
Keeps unsent drafts per conversation in browser local storage, with owner tracking across reloads.
Settings switch for cloud code execution and file creation.
Server read of the user's code-execution setting; refuses when the read fails.
Browser side of web push: support check, permission, subscribe, store, remove.
The only service worker: shows push notifications and opens the run on click; caches nothing.
Public page for a shared conversation: reads, expiry check, metadata, report link.

data_kept.what: Unsent composer drafts, keyed by owner and conversation (key prefix agi-composer-draft:v2:)
data_kept.where: Browser localStorage (composer-draft-storage.ts:1-5, 149-200)

data_kept.what: Current draft owner id and the list of previous owners
data_kept.where: Browser sessionStorage key agi-composer-draft:document-owner (composer-draft-storage.ts:5, 149-200)

data_kept.what: Whether this browser turned web push off
data_kept.where: Browser localStorage key agi.web-push.disabled (web-push-client.ts:8, 14-26)

data_kept.what: Cloud code execution setting, under capabilities.cloudCodeExecution
data_kept.where: Server table public.user_settings, JSON settings column (code-execution-policy.ts:7-8, 33-36)

data_kept.what: Web push subscriptions: endpoint, encryption keys, user agent, last seen time, owner user id
data_kept.where: Server table public.web_push_subscriptions (apps/web/app/api/web-push/route.ts:95-110)

data_kept.what: Push subscription held by the browser
data_kept.where: Browser push manager, created by web-push-client.ts:98-110

data_kept.what: Dictation audio, kept in memory until sent for transcription

guide.area: Area 70. Desktop application (the installed desktop app, Desktop only)
guide.what_it_is_for: The desktop app is an installed Mac and Windows program that opens the signed-in product in its own window. It adds things a browser tab cannot do well: a menu bar, a tray icon, system-wide shortcuts, a small quick-ask panel, local folders and shell commands, screen capture, computer control after permission, and control from a paired phone. These local powers touch the user's own files and screen, so each one is gated by approvals.
guide.who_uses_it: Per the brief, this area applies to the Desktop app only (the other five apps are n/a or not listed). In the code, the window, menus and shortcuts are for any signed-in user. Local folder and shell features need the user to approve a folder first. Phone control needs a paired phone. The code read here shows no plan gate on these features, so plan limits are unknown (see not_sure). No workspace admin role was seen in these files.

features.name: App window and lifecycle
features.use: The app runs as its own program with one window, one running copy, and a crash recovery path. On Mac, closing the window keeps the app running; clicking the Dock icon brings it back.
how_people_use_it: Open the app from Applications or the Dock.
Start the app a second time: the first window comes forward instead.
Click the close button on Mac: the app stays in the Dock.
Click the Dock icon to bring the window back.
On Windows or Linux, closing the last window quits the app unless the tray icon is present.
how_it_should_work: Only one copy runs. A second launch passes its link to the first copy and brings its window forward.
If the page crashes or stops responding for a long time, the app shows a recovery screen instead of a blank window.
On Mac, the app stays running with no window and reopens a window on activation.
Empty state: with no window open, the Dock or tray opens the main window.
Failure: a broken page shows the recovery screen; it does not silently stay blank.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only, done per the brief. Other apps: not listed in the brief.

features.name: Menu bar, Dock and tray icon
features.use: The app has a native menu bar with File, Edit, View, History, Window and Help. It also has a tray (menu bar) icon for quick actions that stays when the app is hidden.
how_people_use_it: Click a menu bar item such as New Chat, Quick Ask or Always on Top.
Click the tray icon to see Open, New Chat, running agents, shortcuts, Check for Updates and Quit.
Turn the tray icon off in preferences (Show in menu bar switch).
how_it_should_work: Each menu item runs a real action; items that are not ready are disabled, not silent.
The tray icon is shown when the preference is on, or while an agent runs, or while computer use is granted. It is removed when none of these is true.
Empty state: with the preference off and nothing running, there is no tray icon.
Limit: the tray cannot be turned off while an agent or computer use still needs it.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only, done per the brief.

features.name: Global shortcuts
features.use: System-wide keys (Quick Ask, New Chat, screenshot, window screenshot, voice, stop agents) work even when another app is in front. Quick Ask opens a small panel where the user types one prompt.
how_people_use_it: Press the Quick Ask shortcut in any app; type a prompt in the small panel; press Enter.
Press Escape or click away to hide the panel.
Change a shortcut in Settings or from the tray submenu Shortcuts; pick a preset or set it off.
how_it_should_work: A shortcut that another app already holds is reported as taken, and the user is told by a notification.
Two shortcuts with the same key are reported as duplicate.
Stop Agents can never be set off; the change is rolled back if it would leave no stop key.
Quick Ask: a prompt that needs a full conversation, an upgrade page or settings opens in the main window instead of the panel.
Failure: a shortcut that cannot register shows a warning once, not on every press.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only, done per the brief.

features.name: Window management
features.use: The user can keep a compact companion window beside other apps, keep a window always on top, open more windows, and move a conversation into its own window.
how_people_use_it: Choose Window > New Window, Open in New Window or Move Conversation to New Window.
Choose Window > Always on Top to toggle it.
Use Window > Move and Resize or Arrange items to tile windows.
Pop a panel (artifact, preview, side panel) out of the main window: not built.
how_it_should_work: Always on Top keeps the chosen window above others until turned off.
Each new window reopens its last size and place, and a zoomed frame is not saved as a larger size.
Detaching a panel into its own window is expected by the brief, but it is marked missing.
Empty state: with no conversation open, Move Conversation to New Window should not act on nothing.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only. Companion, Always on Top and multiple windows: done. Detachable panels: missing.

features.name: Screen capture and computer use
features.use: The user can send a screenshot of the whole screen or one window into the chat. The assistant can also see the screen and move the mouse or keyboard, but only after the user grants it.
how_people_use_it: Press the screenshot shortcut, or choose Screenshot to Chat from the menu, and the image lands in the chat composer.
Choose the window screenshot option to pick one window.
Grant computer use from the tray or menu, then watch the control bar.
Press Stop Computer Use, Take Over Screen Control, or Hand Back Screen Control.
how_it_should_work: Capture copies the image to the clipboard, pastes it into the chat, then clears the clipboard again if it still holds only the capture.
If the chat window is closed, the image stays on the clipboard and the user is told.
If screen recording permission is missing, the user sees a message naming the permission and asked to relaunch.
Computer use can be stopped at any time; take-over pauses the assistant so the user can act; hand-back resumes it.
Revoke removes the grant so the assistant must ask again.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only, done per the brief.

features.name: Local folders and files
features.use: The user approves folders on the computer. The assistant can then search their file names and contents, and create or change files inside them, after a permission prompt. The approval list can be reviewed and revoked.
how_people_use_it: Attach a folder: the system file dialog opens; pick the folder.
See approved folders in Settings > Capabilities or Local access; revoke one from there.
Ask the assistant to find or edit a file; approve the prompt when asked.
how_it_should_work: Choices come from the operating system dialog, not a web page.
A folder stays approved across launches until the user revokes it (brief status; storage not confirmed in code).
Search only covers approved folders.
Edits need a permission prompt before they happen.
Failure: if the approved folder no longer exists, the user is told to choose it again.
features.on_each_app: Desktop only, done per the brief.

features.name: Local shell commands
features.use: The assistant or the user can run a program inside an approved folder, with approval, a sandbox, and output shown as it streams.
how_people_use_it: Open the terminal for a folder and type commands yourself (only the user types into it).
Approve a command the assistant wants to run.
Watch the streamed output in the session.
how_it_should_work: Commands run only in an approved folder, and inside the same sandbox as agent commands.
The assistant cannot type into the user's terminal.
If the folder is no longer approved, the command is refused with a message to choose the folder again.

features.name: Phone remote control
features.use: The desktop app can host a session that a paired phone can watch and steer, including answering approval requests.
how_people_use_it: Turn on Remote Control in Desktop settings.
Pair the phone; confirm the pairing code on both devices.
On the phone, read sessions and answer approvals.
how_it_should_work: The phone is asked again before it connects.
If the computer is locked, remote control refuses.
If the service stops, the state shows as stopped, not connected.
Failure: a dropped connection is shown, and the phone can ask to refresh pairing.

features.name: Background work, launch at login and sleep
features.use: The user chooses whether the app starts at login, and can see and stop what it keeps running in the background. Sleep and wake handling is only partly present.
how_people_use_it: Turn on Launch at Login in the File menu or Desktop settings.
Open Background activity to see running work; stop it there.
Turn on keep-awake in settings to stop idle sleep while an agent runs.
how_it_should_work: Launch at login uses the operating system login item setting.
Background activity lists running work and lets the user stop each one.
Keep-awake stops idle sleep only; the display can still turn off and a closed lid still sleeps.

Sleep and wake: the brief says missing. The code only retries a page after the computer wakes and records a routine run that a sleep interrupted; it does not pause or resume agent work on sleep or lock.

how_it_works.detail: The app asks the operating system for a single-instance lock. If it already runs, the new copy quits. The first copy handles a second launch by delivering any deep link and bringing its window forward.

The main window loads the signed-in web product from the cloud origin. A window policy decides which links stay in the window and which open in the user's browser. Sign-in pages go through the browser.
If the page process crashes, or stays unresponsive for a set time, the app shows a recovery screen. A busy page that recovers does not trigger it.

The menu and tray call the same command functions. The tray is created or removed by a rule: preference on, or computer use granted, or an agent running. Global shortcuts are registered with the operating system and checked for taken or duplicate keys.
A small always-on-top window loads the web page for quick ask. It hides on blur or Escape. A navigation to a full page is handed to the main window.
The app captures the screen or one window, puts the image on the clipboard, focuses the chat composer, pastes, and clears the clipboard again if it still holds only the capture.

The page sends device steps (file, shell, browser, screen) to the desktop runtime. The runtime checks that the folder is approved and that any permission was given before it acts. Computer use has stop, take-over and hand-back controls.
The app reads screen, microphone and accessibility status from the operating system. It can ask for microphone access or open the matching system settings page.
The app sets a feed for the update server and waits for a download. Install quits and relaunches. Launch at login is a login item setting.

Auto-update feed, download state and install.

guide.area: Mobile application (AGI Mobile, the phone app for iOS and Android)
guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the phone version of AGI. A person chats with a model, attaches photos, files and shared content, speaks to the assistant, and gets alerts when a cloud task needs them. Local mode runs a downloaded model on the phone with no cloud. The area also covers the phone's own features: home screen widgets, Siri and Spotlight actions, app lock and storage controls. It matters because the phone is where many people use AGI most, and these features are what a phone user expects from a chat app.
guide.who_uses_it: Every person who opens the phone app. Local mode features (chat on the device, model downloads, storage) work without a cloud account as far as the code shows. Cloud features (cloud tasks, live voice, push alerts, sync) need a signed-in account that has accepted the terms and passed the adult-age check (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:527-534, 745-748). Some plan limits change what a paid or free plan may attach (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/photoSelectionLimit.ts:3-5). Purchases are not live in this build, so no one can buy a plan in the phone app yet (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6). Developers and the owner switch parts on and off through the feature flag file and build settings.

features.name: Moving around and screen layout
features.use: Move between chats, lists and settings. Phones get a slide-out drawer. Tablets get a drawer that stays open on the side. Full-screen pages such as the camera hide the drawer.
how_people_use_it: Swipe from the left edge to open the drawer, or tap the menu control.
Tap a chat, list item or settings row to open it.
Swipe from the left edge, or tap the back control, to return from a stack page.
On a tablet, the drawer stays visible beside the chat.
Rotate the phone: nothing changes, because phones stay in portrait.
how_it_should_work: The drawer is an overlay on phones and a fixed panel on wide screens (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts:5-6 sets 768 and 1024 points as the tablet and regular breakpoints).
Settings pages do not take the drawer's edge swipe, so the edge swipe means Back there (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:20-22).
Camera and scan pages cover the whole window and hide the drawer (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:23-25, 130-132).
The voice screen is always dark and turns the drawer swipe off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:26-28, 134).
Landscape: the code locks phones to portrait. Only tablets may rotate (see things_that_look_wrong).
Foldable adaptation: no code found for hinge or fold events (brief status: not applicable).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. The brief gives a status for the mobile app only. Phone and tablet differ by screen width, not by a separate build.

features.name: Writing a message in the composer
features.use: Type a message in a box that starts as one line and grows. Open a full-screen editor for long text. Send, and keep the chat and the box visible above the keyboard.
how_people_use_it: Tap the box and type. The box grows as lines wrap.
Tap the expand control in the top-right corner of the box to edit in a full-screen editor, then tap send there.
Tap the send control to send.
Open the keyboard: the chat and the box move up.
how_it_should_work: The box grows until 6 lines (apps/mobile/lib/constants.ts:25 MAX_INPUT_LINES = 6). It is also capped at 160 points high and then scrolls (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2107).
The expand control appears only when the text is multi-line (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2131-2151).
While a reply is still streaming, a new send is queued as a follow-up instead of being lost (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:945-960).
If the chat opened a different conversation during a send, the draft is handed to the new chat (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1040-1060).
Drafts are saved on the device so a draft survives leaving the screen (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:180-186).
Keyboard: iOS uses padding. Android screens use padding, and modals use height (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/chrome/keyboardSafeComposer.ts:17-20).
Failure: an attachment whose send failed carries a sendFailed flag so it can be sent again (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1004-1006).
Empty state: the send path only runs when there is text or an attachment (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:1525).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Message actions (tap buttons and long-press menu)
features.use: Act on one message: copy, read aloud, regenerate, rate, export, edit, resend, branch, delete.
how_people_use_it: Under a reply, tap copy, read aloud, regenerate, or the three-dot button.
Long-press a message to open the full action list.
Double-tap a reply to give it a thumbs up.
Tap Export in the menu to open the export sheet, which has share and copy.
how_it_should_work: Under a reply the tap row shows copy, read aloud (with a stop state while speaking), regenerate, and the three-dot button (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:3146-3196).
The long-press menu for a user message has Edit, Resend, Schedule as Task, Copy, Select Text and Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1640-1700, 1722).

The long-press menu for a reply has Retry, Retry with Another Model, Branch, Copy, Select Text, Export, Save as Document, Good and Bad Response, Report and Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1655-1722).
Retry and Edit ask before discarding unsaved answer edits (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:295-300).
Delete asks first: Delete message, with the warning that it cannot be recovered (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1609-1623).
While a reply is streaming, some actions are hidden or show Wait for response (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1629-1630).
Rating: a double-tap sends thumbs up only when the reply is not streaming and rating is wired (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:1625, 1632-1637).
Failure: copy shows a failed state icon (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:3154-3168).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. Share is not a tap button under the reply; it is in the Export sheet.

features.name: Attaching photos, camera, files and shared content
features.use: Add a photo taken now, photos from the library, files from the Files app or a storage provider, or content shared from another app. The attachment goes with the next message, or starts a new chat.
how_people_use_it: Open the attach sheet and choose Camera, Photos, Files or Paste image.
In the camera screen, take a photo, check it, add a question, and send. The default question is What do you see in this image?
In another app, choose Share and pick AGI Mobile. A preview opens with the shared text or files.
On a shared web page, tap Summarize this page or Ask about this page.
how_it_should_work: Camera photos are taken with metadata turned off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/camera.tsx:73-76), and library photos have metadata removed before use (apps/mobile/src/features/media/photo-picker.ts:26).
A camera send with no chat open starts a chat titled Vision Analysis (apps/mobile/app/(app)/camera.tsx:117) and asks the default question (apps/mobile/app/(app)/camera.tsx:126).
Photos: multiple selection, capped at the plan limit for one message (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1580-1587; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/photoSelectionLimit.ts:3-5).

Files: a system file picker that allows several files and copies them to the app cache (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1606-1610). The allowed types depend on the mode (apps/web... see services/docParser.ts:112 in apps/mobile).
Other limits: file size and count per message depend on the mode and plan (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:34-47).
Share text is cut to 100 KB, and a notice says it was cut (apps/mobile/src/features/share-preview/index.tsx:43, 55-59).
Shared content is wrapped in a tag so the model reads it as data (apps/mobile/src/features/share-preview/index.tsx:62-65).
Offline: in a cloud chat, attachments cannot be queued, so the user gets an alert and the draft stays (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:859-866).

Interrupted uploads: when the app leaves the foreground, an upload is marked as stopped in the background. The code shows this state, but no automatic resume was found (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadLifecycle.ts:52, 118-124).
Failure: a failed camera or library open shows an alert that offers Open Settings when permission is off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1535-1541).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. The share intake differs by platform: an Android share intent filter (apps/mobile/app.config.js:318-338) and an iOS share extension inbox (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:827-840).

features.name: Voice conversation
features.use: Talk to the assistant by voice. In a cloud chat, a live two-way session. In a local chat, a turn-based voice bar that uses on-device speech.
how_people_use_it: Tap the voice control in a chat, or open the voice screen from the widget or from settings.
Tap the orb to speak, or hold it in push-to-talk mode, and release to send.
Watch the phase text: Tap to speak, Listening, Thinking, Speaking.
To end, tap the stop or leave the screen.
how_it_should_work: The live two-way session runs only for cloud chats and a signed-in user (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21-28; apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1698-1712).
Local chats show the turn-based voice bar instead (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1708-1711).
Waiting: Thinking shows Sending to AGI Cloud or Answering on this device, depending on the model (apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx:88-95).
Timeouts: connection setup waits up to 10 seconds for network gathering, and a tool call times out after 20 seconds (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:30, 37, 179-196).
Failure: a microphone denial or a failed connection gives a specific message (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:171-176).
Plan gate: the voice button checks a capability named canUseVoice and shows an alert when it is off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1648, 1698-1700).
On older Android, the on-device speech check can stop the start without a message (see things_that_look_wrong).
Audio route selection (speaker, Bluetooth, headset): no code found (brief status: not applicable).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Push notifications
features.use: Get alerts when an agent, a research run, a scheduled task or a chat reply needs the person. Tap an alert to open the matching item.
how_people_use_it: Turn on notifications after the app shows its reason (the OS prompt runs once, from an explicit tap).
Tap an alert on the lock screen or in the notification list.
Open the notifications list from the app to see past alerts.
how_it_should_work: The OS prompt runs only from an explicit user action, not at launch (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:202-204, 204-221).
The phone gets an Expo push token and sends it, with a device id and preferences, to the server (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:257-263; apps/mobile/services/pushPreferenceSync.ts:29, 153).
The server stores the token in the device table. A device id already used by another account gets a refusal (apps/web/app/api/mobile/push-token/route.ts:42-48, 50-79).

The server sends pushes for agent events, research and task completion, approvals, schedules, chat replies and product updates (apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts:66-69; callers listed in apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts and schedule-notification-service.ts).
Priority: critical and high play a sound; normal shows without sound; low is silent (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:125-156).
Alerts for another account, or for a chat that is open in front, are hidden (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:97-115).
Tap routing: a tap opens the matching route from an allow list. The list drops a route whose feature is off (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:339-381).
Approval alerts open the companion screen. With companion off, they open the notifications list instead (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:414-418, 441-447).
Failure: a failed token send records device_token or server. The status then reads unregistered (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:172-178, 193-196, 266-274).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Cloud tasks, agent answers and approvals
features.use: Start a cloud task from the phone, follow it in the task list, answer an agent's question, approve or deny a pending action, and (where enabled) follow a coding session running elsewhere.
how_people_use_it: Open Tasks, tap start, write a goal (and optional constraints or deliverable), and start.
Open a task to see its status and output.
If the agent asks a question, type the answer in the sheet and submit.
If the agent wants to run an action, tap Approve or Deny. The run then resumes or stops.
Remote coding review: open a coding session, read its changed files and diffs, then steer or approve. Not reachable in this build (see below).
how_it_should_work: Starting: a goal is required. An empty goal shows Describe what this task should accomplish (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/startWork.ts:13, 44-52). The run is made in a new chat using the selected cloud model (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/startWork.ts:38-60).
The Tasks screen needs the cloudTasks flag, cloud mode and an unlocked account (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/CloudTasksScreen.tsx:423, 655).
Approve and Deny call the same resolve step with approved or rejected (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:424-437; apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/service.ts:64-70).
Answers: the sheet has a form that submits answers to the run (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:245, 459-460).

Waiting: a chat turn that is still running shows Waiting for the answer. It appears here when it is ready. After 150 seconds with no progress, it reports that the turn stopped on the server (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:17-22).
Notification buttons: the only action is Review, which opens the app (apps/mobile/services/notificationCategories.ts:11-17). The answer is typed in the app, not in the alert.

Remote coding review and remote approval: the code is behind two flags, companion and dispatch, and both are off (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:12, 16; apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:108-121).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Home screen, lock screen and OS shortcuts
features.use: Start AGI from the home screen, a control, Siri, Spotlight, or the app icon's shortcut menu.
how_people_use_it: Add the AGI Quick Actions widget to the home screen (iOS or Android). Tap New chat, Camera or Voice.
On iOS 18 or later, add the AGI control where the OS allows it (lock screen or Control Center).
Say a Siri phrase, or search in Spotlight, for Start Chat, Ask AGI, Summarize, Analyze Image, Transcribe, Translate, Scan or Set Reminder.
Long-press the app icon on Android for its shortcuts.
how_it_should_work: Widget buttons open deep links: agiworkforce://intent/chat, /camera and /voice (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift:6-8, 66-71). The app routes them in apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:202-225.
Voice from the widget opens the voice screen only when on-device speech is available. Otherwise it opens the chat tab (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:219-225).
Ask AGI does not open the app (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:11). Most other intents open the app.
The intents are wired into the iOS build (apps/mobile/native/ios/withAGINativeModulesIOS.cjs:42-44, 109-125).

Android shortcuts and the Android widget are registered in the build (apps/mobile/app.config.js:478-482; apps/mobile/native/android/withAGIShortcuts.cjs:9-15; apps/mobile/native/android/withAGIWidget.cjs:9-12).
Live Activity: no code found (brief status: missing).
Default digital assistant on Android: no assist or voice-command intent filter found (brief status: missing).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. iOS and Android differ: the iOS widget and control and the App Intents exist; the Android widget and shortcuts exist; Android default-assistant does not.

features.name: Local models and device storage
features.use: Download a model and chat with it on the device. See how much space AGI uses, and delete models, cache, or all local data.
how_people_use_it: In onboarding or the model picker, choose a model and tap Download. Turn on Download over cellular too if wanted.
In Settings, open Storage to see the total, the list of models, and Clear cache.
Tap the trash icon next to a model, confirm, and the model files are removed.
Tap Delete everything and confirm twice to wipe the device.
how_it_should_work: Model states: ready, download required, downloading, failed, unavailable, locked (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:56-57).

Downloads use Wi-Fi by default. The cellular switch is off unless the person turns it on (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:379, 521; apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:746-756).
Local chats cannot use cloud models. Sending shows a message that a separate cloud chat is needed (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2278).
Delete model: an alert warns the files can be downloaded again. A busy removal shows a specific message (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:239-285).
Clear cache: an alert says conversations and models are not affected (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:287-305).

Delete everything: two confirmations. It wipes conversations, memory, settings and models, signs out, and shows Wipe failed if it cannot finish (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/useEraseDeviceData.ts:9-44).
Storage totals show Measuring until read, and Try again on a failed read (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:112-139, 315-327).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Keeping your place after the app closes
features.use: Reopen AGI after the system closes it, and return to the same chat with its messages and draft.
how_people_use_it: Open the app after it was closed by the system or by the person. The last chat and its draft are back.
If a reply was still being written, the app checks the server and shows the result, or a waiting message.
how_it_should_work: Messages are kept in encrypted local storage: the local chat store and the cloud chat store (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:1729-1730; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatCloudMessageStore.ts:313-314).
Drafts are kept under a composer-draft key (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:5, 186).
When the store reloads, a reply that was still streaming is marked stopped (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:411-417, 1745).

The app then asks the server whether the turn finished. A finished answer is restored. A turn that stalls for 150 seconds is reported as stopped on the server (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:17-22).
So the phone does not keep writing an interrupted reply itself. It checks the server and shows what the server has.
features.on_each_app: Mobile only.

features.name: Buying plans and credits in the store
features.use: Buy a plan or credits through the App Store or Google Play, and restore earlier purchases.
how_people_use_it: Open Billing in settings and choose a plan or credits. Restore purchases with the restore control.
In this build, none of these steps is reachable.
how_it_should_work: The purchase logic exists: purchase, acknowledge, and restore (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/useMobileIap.ts:44-64, 199-277). It is wrapped in a hook that no screen mounts. Only tests import it (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/useMobileIap.ts:726).

The billing flag is off, so the billing service throws and the billing portal is hidden (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/service.ts:9; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:199).

The server product catalog returns no products unless the server flag is on (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-iap-catalog.ts:53-56), and product ids come from environment settings (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-iap-catalog.ts:42-45).
Store listings say version 1 sells nothing (apps/mobile/store-listing/REVIEWER-NOTES-IOS.md:253).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. Status: partial, as the brief says.

features.name: App lock and privacy controls
features.use: Lock the phone app with Face ID, a fingerprint or the device passcode. Hide the chat when the app is in the app switcher. Manage what the app may access.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, then Safety and Security, and turn on App Lock. The device passcode is asked first.
When the app returns from the background, the device unlock prompt appears.
Open Permissions to change camera, photos and microphone access.
how_it_should_work: Turning App Lock on first checks that a device lock is set up. If not, it says so and stays off (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/safety-security/index.tsx:37-57, 59-72).

While the app is not active, it is covered, and the cover is shown in the app switcher (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/hooks/useBiometricGate.ts:135-150). The overlay is drawn in the root layout (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:1020-1026).
The prompt appears only when the app is in front again, and a short switch of 1.5 seconds does not re-lock (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/hooks/useBiometricGate.ts:15-19, 119).
If the check fails, the app stays locked (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/hooks/useBiometricGate.ts:93-96).
Reset: Reset app lock and sign out is offered from the lock overlay (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:565-586).
Reduce sensitive content is a content filter, not a privacy control. It is forced on for minor mode (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/safety-security/index.tsx:82-94).
features.on_each_app: Mobile only. The cover on app switch works only when App Lock is on.

how_it_works.detail: The root layout starts the encrypted local storage, waits for sign-in state and the terms and age answers, and puts the App Lock overlay over the app. Cloud features wait for the answers.
A drawer wraps the screens. Some screens hide the drawer or switch off its edge swipe. Tablets get a fixed side panel by width.
The composer tracks the text height, offers the full-screen editor, and calls the send handler. While a reply streams, a send is queued.
The attach sheet calls the camera, library or file picker. Photos lose their metadata. Limits by plan and mode are applied.

how_it_works.step: Choose local or cloud for the send
how_it_works.detail: The send reads the conversation's mode. A local chat needs a local model. A cloud chat needs a signed-in account and a cloud model. A mismatch shows a message and stops.

how_it_works.step: Run a local model on the device
how_it_works.detail: Local models are downloaded and kept in the app's document folder. Downloads follow the Wi-Fi-first rule and the cellular switch. The runtime resolves the chosen local model before it answers.
The chat checks the mode, sign-in and device speech. In cloud mode it opens a live session with a server route that issues the session. Local mode gets the turn-based voice bar.
After the person taps Turn on, the app asks the OS for permission, gets an Expo push token, and sends it with its device id to the server. The server saves it in the device table.
Server services decide when to send. A push goes to the Expo push service, which delivers it to the phone. The phone shows it with a priority-based sound.

how_it_works.step: Open the right screen on tap
how_it_works.detail: A tapped alert is mapped to a route from an allow list. Routes whose feature is off are dropped. Approvals open the companion screen only when that feature is on.
Messages and drafts are written to encrypted storage. On reload, a streaming reply is marked stopped and the server is asked for the final answer.

key_files.role: Root layout: storage start, sign-in and terms gates, App Lock overlay, share and widget link intake, push and deep link handling.
Drawer and the list of screens, with the rules for which screens hide the drawer or switch off its swipe.
The composer: one-line growth, full-screen editor, send, queue while streaming, draft hand-off.
Message actions: tap row, long-press menu, delete confirmation, double-tap rating.
The chat screen: attach sheet (camera, photos, files, paste), voice entry, keyboard layout.
Send path that picks local or cloud by the chat's mode and checks the model and sign-in.
Push permission, token registration, how alerts show, and where a tapped alert opens.
Server route that saves a phone's push token and preferences, and refuses a device id held by another account.
The cloud live voice session: connection, timeouts, tool calls, errors.
Local model status and downloads, with the Wi-Fi default and cellular switch.
App Lock state: prompts on return, covers the app while away, fails closed.
The switches for this build (billing, companion, dispatch, cloud tasks and others).
Build settings: orientation, permissions, plugins, widget and intent wiring, production checks.
