guide.shared_code: Mobile logic lives in apps/mobile (features under apps/mobile/src/features, stores under apps/mobile/stores, services under apps/mobile/services). It is separate from the web and desktop apps. Shared packages used by this code: @agiworkforce/cloud-contracts (push route path, push account binding, used in apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts and pushPreferenceSync.ts); @agiworkforce/types (plan attachment limit in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/photoSelectionLimit.ts, and the store product definitions used by apps/web/lib/server/mobile-iap-catalog.ts); @agiworkforce/utils/voice (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useVoiceConversation.ts:4). Server code for mobile push is in apps/web/app/api/mobile/push-token and apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts. That service is also used by web push (apps/web/lib/services/web-push-service.ts:21), so it is shared between mobile and web. Native code is separate per platform: apps/mobile/native/ios and apps/mobile/native/android. Not checked: whether the chat UI is shared with other surfaces (packages/ui/unified-chat was not opened).

things_that_look_wrong.what: The brief says phones rotate to landscape and re-lay out the chat. The code keeps iPhone in portrait, and holds narrow Android screens in portrait. Only tablets can rotate. The brief's cited lines (app.config.js:73 and :91) are not orientation code.
The brief says purchases and restore are built. The purchase hook is not mounted in any screen. Only tests import it. The billing flag is also off.
The brief says remote approval and remote coding review are done. Both sit behind the companion and dispatch flags, which are both off, so they cannot be reached in this build.
The brief says home-screen widgets and lock-screen controls are missing. The code has an iOS widget with New chat, Camera and Voice buttons, an iOS control, and an Android widget.
The brief says Siri and Spotlight shortcuts are not applicable. The code has App Intents for eight actions, and the iOS build plugin copies them in.

The brief says cellular data preferences are not applicable. The code has a Wi-Fi-first default and a Download over cellular switch during onboarding. The error text in the native code points to a Settings path (Settings, Storage, Download over cellular), but no such control was found outside onboarding.
On older Android, the voice button returns silently when on-device speech is not available and the local mode check fails. The person gets no message.
Clear cache has no error handling. A failed delete is an unhandled promise error, and the total is then reset to zero anyway.

The brief lists share and rate among the tap targets under a reply. The tap row has copy, read aloud, regenerate and the three-dot button only. Share sits in the Export sheet, and rating is a double-tap or a menu item.
The privacy cover on app switch only works when App Lock is on. With App Lock off, the app is not covered in the app switcher.

After a restart, a reply that was still streaming is marked stopped locally. It is not continued by the phone. The app asks the server for the result, and shows a waiting or stopped message. This is weaker than the brief's wording about an in-flight reply.

Approval alerts are meant to open the approval screen, but with the companion flag off they open the notifications list. The alert's Review button also only opens the app; the answer is not typed in the alert.

Several brief line references do not match the code. S71.09 cites _layout.tsx:493 and :583, but the share listener is at :827-840. S71.32 cites _layout.tsx:726, which is background fetch registration; the lock overlay is at :1020-1026. S71.19 cites MessageBubble.tsx:1110, which is not restoration code.

not_sure: Whether the widget, the control, the App Intents and the Android widget actually appear and work on a device. Nothing was built or run, as the task required.
The numbers behind the plan attachment limits (defined in the shared types package, which was not opened).
What wipeAllLocalData in apps/mobile/services/dsarExport does beyond the in-memory reset, and which server data a wipe reaches.
How shared text and files are staged between the share extension and the app (apps/mobile/src/features/share-preview/sharedAttachments and iosShareInbox were not opened).
What writes to the SQLCipher database (expo-sqlite) in apps/mobile, if anything.
Tablet layout details in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.tsx and DrawerContent.tsx, which the brief cites. Those files were not opened.
Which server events call sendPushToUser beyond the callers found by search (agent, schedule, chat reply, product update, usage reset, video notice, web push). Not all callers were read.
Whether cloud chats keep their messages on the server during a phone restart. The server chat store was not opened.
What the empty states look like on each screen. Only the code paths named above were read.
Whether the composer send button is disabled when the box is empty. The code computes hasContent (ChatInput.tsx:1525), but the disabled prop was not confirmed.
Failure messages for a failed model download beyond installFailureMessage (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:71-76).

guide.area: 072 CLI and terminal application (`agi` command, apps/cli)
guide.what_it_is_for: The CLI is the `agi` command in a terminal. It gives a person an AI coding and task agent that works on the files in a folder, with a full-screen chat screen or a plain line mode. It can also run one prompt and exit, which lets scripts and CI use it, and it can resume, fork, and export saved sessions. It matters because the same agent can run on the user's own machine, on the user's own provider key, or on the managed cloud service.
guide.who_uses_it: Every terminal user who installs the binary, because local and own-key runs need no account (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-356 says account usage needs `agi login`). Cloud features need a signed-in account: account usage, cloud session attach, and `--auto` model routing (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:478 says `--auto` applies only to managed-cloud sessions). Scripts and CI jobs use the one-shot and exit-code features (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5122 area, the `exec` and `-p` paths). People who need a screen reader use plain or screen-reader mode (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:442-448). Developers change this area. The code does not show a paid-plan gate on most commands in this area; that is listed under not_sure.

features.name: Full-screen terminal chat screen
features.use: Opens the main chat screen when the user types `agi` in a terminal. The composer, transcript and overlays (pickers, dialogs) sit on one screen, and the user chooses a colour theme.
how_people_use_it: Type `agi` in a terminal to open the screen; type a message and press Enter to send it.
Press `/` to open the command palette (default key, keybindings.rs:48-57).
Type `/theme` to open the theme picker, or `/theme <name>` to set one directly.
Resize the terminal window; the screen redraws and the transcript stays.
how_it_should_work: Sending a message starts an agent turn; the transcript shows the reply and tool steps as they happen.
Theme choice is saved to the project config file (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6372-6390 calls persist_theme_project).
Resize: the main loop handles only key and paste events (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7283-7290). Each frame redraws at the current size, so layout follows the window; this was not run.
Empty state and waiting state were not traced in this read.
Failures show as chat system messages (e.g. `Model switch failed: ...`, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5553-5573).
Plain or screen-reader mode does not open this screen; the line mode runs instead (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8295).
features.on_each_app: CLI only. The brief gives a status only for the CLI (`cli done`). No other app is part of this item.

features.name: Keys, composer and @ file mentions
features.use: Lets the user type fast: up/down to recall earlier prompts, `@` to attach files, and global keys that can be changed in config.
how_people_use_it: Press Up or Down in an empty or single-line composer to walk back through earlier prompts.
Type `@` where a mention is allowed; a fuzzy file picker opens. Pick a file to insert its path.
Press Shift+Tab to change permission mode; Alt+P to cycle the model; Ctrl+L to redraw; Ctrl+D to quit.
Press Ctrl+C with an empty composer once to arm exit, and again within the window to quit (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3995-4012).
Add `[ui.keybindings]` to config.toml to rebind the global actions.
how_it_should_work: Prompt history is saved one line per prompt in history.txt in the config folder and loads on the next run (apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:15-18).

Ctrl+R reverse search is documented for the line mode (apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs:281-282, apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:1070). The full-screen screen has no Ctrl+R search; it uses Up and Down only (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4179-4200).
@ mentions: the path always goes to the model. File contents are inlined only when the folder is trusted (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:312-315 comment, expand_mentions at :315).

Config can rebind only the global actions: quit, cycle mode, cycle model, redraw, clear chat, clear input, open palette. Text editing and confirmation keys stay fixed (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:1-6).
Clear chat has no default key (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:48-57).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Saved sessions: list, resume, fork, export
features.use: Lets the user find an earlier conversation, continue it, branch it into a new one, or write it to a file.
how_people_use_it: In the screen, type `/history` (or `/sessions`) to open the session picker; `/resume` opens it too, or `/resume <id>` resumes one directly.

In a terminal shell, `agi history` lists sessions on this device; `agi history --cloud` lists account sessions; `agi resume [id] [--cloud]` resumes; `agi resume -c` or `agi -c` continues the newest session in this project.
`/fork` or `/branch` makes a new session from the current one. `agi fork <id>` and `agi session fork <id> --at-turn N` fork a saved one.
`/export [md|json|answer] [path]` writes the transcript to a file under the workspace root; with no path it shows the text in the chat.
how_it_should_work: Session data is stored under the config folder in managed_sessions and managed_session_metadata (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:205-235, 50).
`agi history` with no sessions prints `No sessions on this device.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7196 area).
Resume by cloud id: `resume_subcommand_target` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2505-2520) reads `--teleport` and `--cloud`.

Export writes only when the path is new or the user names it; the write fails loudly if the path exists (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs export path code, and apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4253-4262 pattern for memory export).
The brief says export also goes to the clipboard. The code has no clipboard write for /export (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6033-6043). See things_that_look_wrong.
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Model, effort and permission controls
features.use: Lets the user change the model, reasoning effort and approval rules during a session.
how_people_use_it: Type `/model` to open the model picker, or `/model <id>` to switch.
Type `/effort`, or `/effort low|medium|high|max` (short forms `l`, `m`, `h`).
Type `/permissions` (or `/perms`, `/approvals`) to see tabs for allow, ask, deny and session rules; `/permissions allow <rule>` adds one; `/permissions remove <rule>` removes one.
On the command line, `--mode default|plan|auto|bypassPermissions|dontAsk` and `--allowedTools` / `--disallowedTools` set the mode for one run.
how_it_should_work: `/model <id>` switches the model for the session; in local mode an unknown id falls through to a local switch (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5553-5573).
`/effort` sets the level for the session and also saves it as the project default (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6452-6470). The brief says it only changes the next request; the code does both.
Permission rule edits go through the permission store (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs permissions handler; apps/cli/src/cli_options.rs:12-25 modes).
`--auto` is refused together with `--model` or `--provider`, and applies only to managed-cloud sessions (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:474-478).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Context, usage and compaction
features.use: Shows how full the context window is, how much the session has cost, and lets the user shrink the conversation.
how_people_use_it: Type `/context` to see how much of the window the conversation uses.
Type `/usage` for session tokens and cost plus account allowance.
Type `/compact` or `/compact <focus text>` to summarise the conversation.
how_it_should_work: Context is computed from the message list against the model window (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:35-67).

`/usage` reads the account usage from the server endpoint `/api/usage` (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:15, 358-366). BYOK accounts get a local-only note instead (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-356).
`/compact` runs the summary and shows a receipt with before and after size (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7755-7768).
Without a signed-in account, usage shows a local-only line instead of account numbers.
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Tools, skills, plugins and background runs
features.use: Lets the user connect outside tools (MCP servers), turn skills and plugins on or off, and manage work that runs in the background.
how_people_use_it: `agi mcp add|list|get|enable|disable|allow|ask|block|unset|login|logout|remove` manages the MCP registry; `/mcp` in the screen shows connected tools.
`agi plugin list|install|info|login|configure|remove|enable|disable|update|digest` manages plugins; `/skills` and `/plugin` do the same in the screen.
`agi background start|list|logs|stop|rm|attach` runs a prompt that keeps going after the terminal closes; `/tasks` lists sub-agents and running work in the screen.
how_it_should_work: MCP registry lives at ~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:827-828 help text).
Plugin install checks a sha256 digest or a signature, and refuses an unsigned plugin when plugins.require_signed is set (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2017-2050 area).
Background run records are run.json and output.log (apps/cli/src/background.rs:6-7).
`/tasks` output comes from the sub-agent manager (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7733-7742, repl::tasks_for_display).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: One-shot and scripted runs with output formats
features.use: Runs one prompt to the end and exits. It prints plain text, one JSON object, or a stream of JSON events, and it reads the prompt and extra text from stdin or pipes.
how_people_use_it: `agi exec "<prompt>"` (alias `agi e`) or `agi -p "<prompt>"` runs once and exits.
`--raw` or `--print` prints only the reply text; `--output-format text|json|stream-json` (alias `--output`) picks the format; `--json` is one pretty JSON object.
`git diff | agi "explain"` pipes text in; `agi --stdin` or `agi - ` reads the prompt from stdin; `-f FILE` adds file context.
`--json-events` (alias for stream-json) prints NDJSON events.
how_it_should_work: Output mode is chosen in apps/cli/src/lib.rs:574-592 (JsonPretty, RawText, JsonLine, Text).

Stdin is read when the prompt is `-`, when `--stdin` is set, or when stdin is not a terminal (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8664-8672). Empty piped stdin prints `No input received from stdin.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8222-8223).
Piped text is wrapped as `<stdin>...</stdin>` and placed before the prompt; file context goes first (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8512-8550).
JSON result keys: response, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost, via_subscription, duration_ms, incomplete (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9415-9431).
A failure in JSON mode prints the error JSON to stderr, not stdout (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9455-9460). See things_that_look_wrong.
Stream events carry a `type` field; text deltas are `stream_event` with subtype `text_delta` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:10540-10546 test, sdk_io/protocol.rs:14-63).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Exit codes and CI automation
features.use: Lets CI and scripts tell failure classes apart, and run unattended with a spend cap and an approval policy.
how_people_use_it: Check the process exit status after `agi exec` or `agi -p`.
Set `--max-budget-usd <USD>` to stop when spend passes a limit.
Use `--auto-approve-plan` for headless plan runs, `--mode dontAsk` to avoid prompts, `--allowedTools` to allow named tools.
how_it_should_work: Exit codes: 1 generic failure, 65 data error, 69 unavailable (connection refused), 75 temporary (timeout), 76 client too old, 77 not permitted, 78 configuration. Code 2 is never used; it belongs to the argument parser (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:262-280).
A timeout or connection error from the HTTP layer maps to 75 or 69 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8829-8845).
A headless change that was refused exits 1 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8803).
Budget stop emits a `status_update` with reason `budget_exhausted` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9238-9250 area and the flag doc at :489-491).
Interrupt exits 130, which the brief's contract does not list (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8633-8637).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Plain and screen-reader output, no colour
features.use: Prints output one line at a time, without colour, spinners or full-screen redraws, for screen readers and logs.
how_people_use_it: Run `agi --plain` (or set AGI_PLAIN=1), or `agi --screen-reader` (or AGI_SCREEN_READER=1, or ui.screen_reader = true in config).
Set NO_COLOR=1 to remove colour.
how_it_should_work: Plain mode turns on from --plain, AGI_PLAIN, or screen reader mode (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5943-5951). It sets a global flag read by all output (apps/cli/src/output.rs:43-59).
Plain mode uses the line REPL instead of the full-screen screen (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8295).
Screen-reader mode labels each line `you:` or `agi:`, answers numbered menus by typing the number, and rings a bell when input is needed (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:442-448 doc).

NO_COLOR alone sets the colour level to none in one function (apps/cli/src/output.rs:91-108). That function has no caller outside its own tests, so NO_COLOR alone does not change the full-screen screen's colour. See things_that_look_wrong.
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Sign-in, settings, folders and environment
features.use: Signs the user in and out, shows auth status, sets the folder a run works in, and reads settings from a global file and a project file.
how_people_use_it: `agi login` signs in to the account; `agi login <provider>` stores that provider's API key; `agi logout [--all]` signs out; `agi auth-status` lists configured providers.
`/login` and `/logout` do the same in the screen.
`-C <path>` or `--repo <path>` runs against another folder; `--add-dir <DIR>` adds an extra folder; `/add-dir` does this in the screen.
`/config` shows the effective settings.
how_it_should_work: Global config is config.toml in ~/.agiworkforce, or in the folder named by AGIWORKFORCE_HOME, which must be absolute (apps/cli/src/config.rs:480-492, 1701-1713).

A project file at .agiworkforce/config.toml overrides the global one only when the folder is trusted and managed policy allows it (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6185-6189; apps/cli/src/config.rs:684-700, 826-844). A non-loopback provider URL in a project file needs consent (apps/cli/src/config.rs:684-687).

Environment variables AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL, AGIWORKFORCE_PROVIDER and AGIWORKFORCE_MAX_TOKENS override config. AGIWORKFORCE_API_BASE, AGI_PLAIN and AGI_SCREEN_READER are recorded so `/config` shows them (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1634-1670).
Credentials go to the OS keychain on macOS and Windows; on Linux they go to owner-only files (apps/cli/src/secure_store.rs:1-21; AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING forces files, secure_store.rs:14-17).
features.on_each_app: CLI only.

features.name: Install, update, diagnostics and shell completion
features.use: Installs the CLI with a script, checks for and installs new versions, checks the local setup, and prints shell completion scripts.
how_people_use_it: Run the installer: `curl -fsSL https://agiworkforce.com/install.sh | bash` (the script is apps/web/public/install.sh).
`agi update` compares this build with the newest release; `agi update --install` installs it after a prompt; `--check` exits non-zero when a newer release exists.
`agi doctor` prints a local setup report (use `--json` for JSON).
`agi completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script.
how_it_should_work: Install script verifies a signed checksum manifest with a public key pinned inside install.sh (apps/web/public/install.sh:31-34, 147-160).
With no published release the installer says so (apps/web/public/install.sh:133 and :151).
Update check reads /api/releases/cli/latest (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:26) and can be turned off with updates.check_on_startup (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:131).
Web surface status shows CLI as `Coming soon` (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:7).
features.on_each_app: CLI only. The installer is served by the web app; the brief marks the CLI partial until the owner publishes the first signed release.

features.name: Remote session attachment
features.use: Lets a terminal take over a session that runs elsewhere, such as a cloud coding session, and continue it here.
how_people_use_it: `agi resume --teleport [id]` checks out a cloud coding session's branch in this repository and continues it; without an id it lists this repository's open sessions.
`agi remote-control` (alias `rc`) lets the mobile app list, start, follow and steer sessions in this folder.
how_it_should_work: Teleport fetches and checks out the cloud session's working branch; it rejects an invalid branch name (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_teleport.rs:134 and validate_branch nearby).
Remote control hosts a developer session for this folder (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6659-6679).
features.on_each_app: CLI only. The mobile side is outside this area.

how_it_works.detail: The binary's main calls the library entry, which builds a multi-thread async runtime and runs the main routine. Special subcommands are handled before the runtime starts.
Clap reads all flags into one struct: prompt, --stdin, --raw, --output-format, --plain, --screen-reader, -C, --add-dir, --max-budget-usd, --auto, and so on. Subcommands live in a second enum.
Plain mode turns on from the flag, from AGI_PLAIN, or from screen-reader mode. The choice is stored in a global flag that every print call reads.
If the folder is trusted, the merged loader reads the global and project config files. If not, only the global file is read. Environment overrides are applied after the file.
A one-shot prompt (exec, -p, a prompt argument, or piped input) runs and exits. Plain mode or --no-tui runs the line REPL. Otherwise the full-screen screen opens.
Each key or paste event goes through the key handler. A line that starts with `/` goes to the slash-command handler; other text is sent as a turn after @ mentions are expanded.

how_it_works.step: Send the turn to the chosen provider path
how_it_works.detail: The session sends the turn to the local, own-key or managed-cloud route chosen by the config and the model. Cloud calls go to the account API base, which is https://agiworkforce.com/api by default.
Session records go under the config folder. Each prompt is appended to history.txt.
One-shot modes print text, a pretty JSON object, or stream events to stdout. A failure exits with the code for its class. Errors print to stderr.

key_files.role: Flag definitions (Cli struct), subcommand enum (Command), one-shot runs, JSON and stream output, exit-code mapping, and top-level dispatch.
Full-screen chat screen: event loop, key handling, slash-command dispatch (handle_slash), overlays, and status bar.
Line-mode slash commands and the display helpers for sessions, export, permissions and tasks, shared with the screen.
Global and project config layers, trust and consent gates, environment overrides, and project-level writes such as /effort and /theme.
Maps each error to an exit class and the exit code; builds the JSON error object.
Global plain-output flag, colour level detection, and the shared print helpers.
Default global key chords and the rules for user rebinding under [ui.keybindings].
Saved session store under the config folder (managed_sessions and metadata folders).
Account usage fetch from /api/usage and the local-only messages for BYOK and signed-out runs.
Newest-release check against /api/releases/cli/latest and the install-by-script path.
Installer script with the release public key pinned in it; checks the signed checksum manifest.
Checks out a cloud session's branch in the local repository for `agi resume --teleport`.

data_kept.what: Global settings (config.toml): model, provider, theme, effort, UI and keybinding settings, update checks
data_kept.where: config.toml in ~/.agiworkforce, or in AGIWORKFORCE_HOME (apps/cli/src/config.rs:480-492)

data_kept.what: Project settings (.agiworkforce/config.toml): project defaults written by /effort and /theme
data_kept.where: Repository folder, .agiworkforce/config.toml (apps/cli/src/config.rs:531-533; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1144, 1263)

data_kept.what: Prompt history, one line per prompt
data_kept.where: history.txt in the config folder (apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:15-18)

data_kept.what: Saved sessions and their metadata
data_kept.where: managed_sessions and managed_session_metadata folders in the config folder (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:205-235, 50; apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session_control.rs)

data_kept.what: Sign-in credentials and provider API keys
data_kept.where: OS keychain on macOS and Windows; owner-only auth.json in the config folder on Linux (apps/cli/src/secure_store.rs:1-21; apps/cli/src/auth.rs:89)

data_kept.what: Cached plan tier and plan model list
data_kept.where: cache/tier.toml and plan-models.toml in the config folder (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:50, 441)

data_kept.what: MCP server registry
data_kept.where: ~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:827-828 help text)

data_kept.what: Plugin settings
data_kept.where: plugin-settings.json, under the features/plugins settings module (apps/cli/src/features/plugins/settings.rs:13)

data_kept.what: Background run record and log
data_kept.where: run.json and output.log, written by the background module (apps/cli/src/background.rs:6-7); the exact folder was not traced

data_kept.what: Exported transcript files
data_kept.where: A path chosen by the user, resolved from the workspace root (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs, export_conversation_to_file)

data_kept.what: Git worktrees for sessions run with --worktree
data_kept.where: .agiworkforce/worktrees in the repository (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/worktree.rs:98)

switches.name: --plain flag and AGI_PLAIN environment variable
switches.effect: Turns on plain output and the line REPL instead of the full-screen screen; no colour, spinners or rules.

switches.name: --screen-reader flag, AGI_SCREEN_READER, ui.screen_reader in config
switches.effect: Plain output with labelled lines, typed menu answers and a bell for input.

switches.name: --no-tui flag
switches.effect: Runs the line REPL instead of the full-screen screen.

switches.name: NO_COLOR environment variable
switches.effect: Sets colour level to none in one function; the TUI icon set switches to ASCII.

switches.name: TERM=dumb
switches.effect: Uses ASCII icons.

switches.name: AGIWORKFORCE_HOME
switches.effect: Moves the config folder; must be an absolute path.

switches.name: AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL, AGIWORKFORCE_PROVIDER, AGIWORKFORCE_MAX_TOKENS
switches.effect: Override the default model, provider and token limit.

switches.name: AGIWORKFORCE_API_BASE
switches.effect: Changes the account API base for cloud calls; shown by /config.

switches.name: AGIWORKFORCE_JWT
switches.effect: Supplies the account token directly; checked before the auth store.

switches.name: AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING
switches.effect: Stores credentials in owner-only files instead of the OS keychain.

switches.name: Project trust and managed policy allow_project_config
switches.effect: Decides whether the project config file is read at all.

switches.name: Consent gate for non-loopback provider URLs in a project file
switches.effect: A project file cannot send prompts to a remote provider URL until the user consents.

switches.name: --auto flag
switches.effect: Automatic model routing; conflicts with --model and --provider; managed-cloud only.

switches.name: --max-budget-usd flag
switches.effect: Stops a run when spend passes the limit.

switches.name: --mode flag (default, plan, auto, bypassPermissions, dontAsk)
switches.effect: Sets the approval mode for the run.

switches.name: AGI_TEAM environment variable and --team flag
switches.effect: Turns team mode on.

switches.name: updates.check_on_startup config value
switches.effect: Turns the startup update check on or off.

switches.name: ui.keybindings table in config.toml
switches.effect: Rebinds the global keys; invalid or duplicate bindings are refused.

switches.name: Managed-cloud usage gate (BYOK accounts)
switches.effect: BYOK accounts see a local-only usage note instead of account usage.

guide.shared_code: Apps/cli is one Rust package, `agiworkforce-cli`, which builds the `agi` and `agiworkforce` binaries (apps/cli/Cargo.toml). It depends on these shared crates under crates/: agiworkforce-agent-core, agiworkforce-app-server, agiworkforce-llm, agiworkforce-model-registry, agiworkforce-mcp, agiworkforce-protocol, agiworkforce-sandbox-policy, agiworkforce-execpolicy, agiworkforce-command-registry, agiworkforce-utils-image, agiworkforce-worktree (apps/cli/Cargo.toml). The app-server module (`agi app-server`, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:860) is the same surface that IDE integrations use, so changes there reach other apps. Everything in apps/cli/src (the screen, line REPL, slash commands, config, sessions, exit codes) is CLI-only. The installer (apps/web/public/install.sh) and the surface status (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts) live in the web app. The account API the CLI calls is served from the web app under /api (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1020). Other apps do not run this code.

things_that_look_wrong.what: NO_COLOR does not remove colour from the full-screen screen. The brief says it does. The colour function that reads NO_COLOR has no caller outside its own tests, and the screen opens unless plain mode is on, so NO_COLOR alone changes only the icon set.
things_that_look_wrong.where: apps/cli/src/output.rs:91-108 (function at :95, no caller outside tests); apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5949-5951 and :8295 (plain mode is the only switch that opens the line REPL); apps/cli/src/tui/icons.rs:34

things_that_look_wrong.what: /export has no clipboard path. The brief says export goes to a file or the clipboard. With no path, the text is shown in the chat only.
Ctrl+R reverse history search is documented but not in the full-screen screen. The screen supports Up and Down only. The brief's item says `Up arrow / history search`.
A failed run in JSON output mode prints the error JSON to stderr, and stdout stays empty. The brief says the one JSON result carries the error state.
Interrupt exits with code 130, which is outside the documented exit contract (1, 65, 69, 75, 76, 77, 78).

Several brief line citations point at unrelated code. Examples: lib.rs:3181 is the cloud model chooser (the brief cites it for linear output); lib.rs:4784 is the models-set command (cited for piped input); tui_app.rs:3545 is inside the status bar (cited for /history); config.rs:339 is an update check helper (cited for config file support). guide.area: VS Code and IDE extension (brief area 73, 30 items, all listed as "vscode done" in the brief). All paths below are relative to ~/Desktop/agiworkforce.
guide.what_it_is_for: The VS Code extension puts the AI assistant inside the editor. A person can chat in a sidebar or an editor tab, and the chat can see the open file, the selected code, problems the editor reports, and the terminal output. Suggested changes come back as a diff the person reviews before anything is written to disk. It matters because the assistant can work on the code the person is already editing, without copy and paste.
guide.who_uses_it: Every VS Code user who installs the extension (activation at apps/extension-vscode/package.json:45-51). What works depends on how the person is connected. Local mode runs the AGI command-line tool on the device. Own-key mode uses the person's provider key. Cloud mode uses the managed service under the person's plan, and the model picker reads the plan tier (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:2000-2021). Workspace trust limits who can use risky features in a folder (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:53-77). The brief and code show no workspace-admin role for this area.

Run the command that opens the chat in an editor tab (agi-workforce.openChatInEditor, apps/extension-vscode/package.json:93).
Type a message in the composer and press Enter (Enter behaviour is a setting, see switches).
When an error shows, press the retry control (the message retryRuntime is handled at apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:1509).
how_it_should_work: The sidebar view is registered with retainContextWhenHidden true, so it keeps its state when hidden (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/chatSetup.ts:61-64).

how_it_works.detail: When the extension activates, it sets up analytics, providers, the local runtime pool (one CLI process per workspace folder), and the chat view. Each part is started inside a guarded boot step, so one failure does not stop the others.

The sidebar is a web page inside VS Code (a webview). It is registered with retainContextWhenHidden, so it keeps its state when hidden. The page sends messages to the host, and the host posts state back.
When the person sends, the host saves the open file if the setting asks for it, builds the turn with attachments and references, and checks the plan before sending.
The active file, selection, problems, terminal output and (in trusted folders) git changes are built into context items. Untitled files are flagged.

The extension sends a turn-start request to the AGI command-line tool over a JSON-lines connection (one JSON message per line). The tool is found from the agiWorkforce.cliPath setting. The turn result is streamed back.

The tier (Local, own key, or a Managed Cloud plan) comes from a cache that is refreshed on a timer. If no tier is known, the default is own key. The model list is grouped by boundary, and models the plan cannot reach are disabled.
Ghost-text suggestions are gated by the setting, by the credential check, by sensitive-file rules, and by the selected model route. Local routes are refused for this feature.

A suggested change is applied only in a trusted workspace and only if the document has not changed. Otherwise it opens in a new tab. A proposed change opens in the native diff, and the diff state drives the context keys for the diff shortcuts.
Errors are sorted into categories (for example rate limit, provider error) and a retry is offered when the failure is retryable. A permission refusal in an untrusted folder offers Manage Trust.

key_files.role: Entry point. Starts every part of the extension in order, registers commands, and reacts to settings changes (status bar, runtime restart).
Creates the sidebar chat view, the session tree, memory, cloud task, schedule, project and artifact providers.
The main chat controller (about 7,000 lines). Handles every message from the chat page, sends turns, builds the model list, handles session search, and handles trust and errors.
The HTML, CSS and script of the chat page. The brief's line references into this file point at styles, not behaviour (see things_that_look_wrong).
Starts the AGI command-line tool for a workspace and talks to it over JSON lines. Holds the start-turn call and the trust command constant.
Builds the context chips: active file, selection, problems, git changes, terminal output.
Applies a suggested edit to the document, with trust and version checks.
Opens a proposed change in the native diff and returns the reviewed text.
Manifest. Commands, menus, keybindings, settings with defaults, activation events, and the untrusted-workspace list.
Reads and caches the account plan tier (Local, own key, or a Managed Cloud plan).
Turns raw failures into a category, a headline and a retry flag.
The list of project instruction file names, the two-file cap, and the 8,192-character cap.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The update notice only says the extension was updated after the version changed. No check for an available update or a list of what changed was found. The brief says the extension tells users when an update is available and lets them update.

The brief cites extension.ts:310 for version-compatibility messaging. That line is part of the permission-restart refresh code. The real notice for a missing feature is announceMissingNativeChat, which covers only the native chat view, not a general unsupported-version or fork check.

Brief references point to the wrong lines. The status-bar reference extension.ts:221 is in the cloud session command. The diff-review reference ChatStateManager.ts:1002 is the reply-bookmark interface. The inline Tab reference package.json:1060 is a menu entry for Fix. The active-file reference ChatStateManager.ts:2650 is session search. The chat-view-loading references webviewContent.ts:2327 and 2715 are style rules.
Hunk-level accept and reject is listed as done, but the review code opened returns the whole reviewed text, with no per-hunk choice.

The local runtime pool is created during activation with a trust callback, but the manifest says the CLI runtime does not start until the folder is trusted. The code path that enforces this was not traced in full.

guide.what_it_is_for: The Chrome extension puts the assistant in a side panel next to the page a person is reading. The person can ask about the page, selected text or a YouTube video, attach other open tabs, and let the assistant act on a site after approving it. It matters because the assistant sees only what the person allows: each site needs Chrome host access and the person's approval before the extension reads it or drives it.
guide.who_uses_it: Every person who installs the Chrome extension. Chat is sent through a signed-in account and is shown only when the account's capability document allows it (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:13401, 13443). Voice, file upload, connectors, web search and browser control are each gated by plan capability (side_panel.ts:15242-15244, 9511, 11165). Free-plan accounts see an upgrade-only usage view (side_panel.ts:13224). Pairing with the desktop app needs a person running the desktop app on this computer, because the bridge address must be a local host (apps/extension/src/background/policy.ts:315-326). Organisation admins can set a site policy through managed storage, which the extension reads first (apps/extension/src/features/site-policy/store.ts:1-30). No developer-only surface was found in this area.

features.name: Site access and site permissions
features.use: The assistant asks Chrome for access to a site before reading or acting on it. The person chooses what each site may do and sets a default mode.
how_people_use_it: When the assistant needs a site that is not approved, a card appears in the chat with Allow once, Always (only for acting, not reading) and Decline (features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1417-1424).
In Options, set Browser control to Ask first, Auto, Full access or YOLO (features/options/site-permission-policy.ts:47-136).
In Options, approve a site for browser control (options.ts:1530-1550), and block sites in the Blocked sites section (features/options/blocked-sites-section.ts:31).
how_it_should_work: Before a read, the panel checks the blocked list, then asks Chrome for the site with a host permission request (side_panel.ts:7785-7830; the request itself is in features/options/site-allowlist.ts:86-96 and features/computer-use/browserControlConsent.ts:61).
Allow once records a temporary grant that is released after the task (side_panel.ts:7900-7925).
If Chrome refuses the grant, the page is not read and the person is told it was not granted (options.ts:1543-1550).
In YOLO mode no card is shown. The site must already be approved for browser control, or the panel says the site is unavailable without questions (side_panel.ts:7810-7833).
A site the org policy blocks is refused with the policy's reason (side_panel.ts:7800-7808, sitePolicyDenialMessage).

Permission modes: Ask first asks before each action; Auto acts and asks only before crucial actions (the default); Full access skips routine confirmations; YOLO runs routine actions on approved sites without questions (site-permission-policy.ts:9-22; computerUsePanel.ts:1139-1141).

features.name: Browser control (the assistant acts on a page)
features.use: Give the assistant a goal and let it drive the current tab. The person sees what it does and can stop it or take over.
how_people_use_it: Open the Computer use tab in the side panel, type a goal and start the task (side_panel.ts:14043-14051).
Watch the banner and the page indicator that names the page being driven (side_panel.ts:10857-10885; computerUsePanel.ts:1102-1135).
Press Stop to end the run, or Take over to pause the agent and drive the page, then Continue to hand it back (computerUsePanel.ts:1218-1233, 1337-1345).
A chat message can also start a browser task through the chat tool (side_panel.ts:7258-7380, startComposerBrowserTask).
how_it_should_work: Starting sends the goal and tab to the worker with AGI_START_COMPUTER_USE. The goal must not be empty and is limited to 4096 characters (background.ts:6232-6250).
The worker owns one run at a time with a lease; a second start is refused while one is active (background.ts:967-1010, computerUseRuns coordinator).

A run stops when its tab is closed (background.ts:tabs.onRemoved listener near 7735), when the tab leaves the approved page, when the account changes (background.ts:1330-1333), or when the worker is suspended (computerUsePanel.ts:829).
Take over lasts at most 15 minutes, then the run ends with a message (features/computer-use/runOwnership.ts:17; computerUsePanel.ts:825).
The agent can itself ask the person to take over (agentLoop.ts:1468, 1561, 1573).
Stop asks the worker to cancel with the run id (computerUsePanel.ts:1484-1525; background.ts:7148).
Unattended YOLO runs need the site already approved; otherwise the run is refused (side_panel.ts:7810-7833).

features.name: Desktop app pairing and connection status
features.use: Connect the extension to the AGI desktop app on the same computer, see whether it is connected, and reconnect.
how_people_use_it: Open the extension Options page, Destinations section, and find the desktop pairing rows (destinations.ts:110; desktop-pairing-rows.ts).

Paste the bridge token from the desktop app if one is set, or follow the code shown by the desktop app: pairing asks the desktop app for a request, the person types the code, and the extension confirms.
In the side panel, a notice Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected appears when the desktop is not connected, with a Reconnect button (side_panel.ts:15637-15648, 9851-9862).

Desktop side: the web app pairing page shows whether the extension is paired, and a link to install the extension (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPairingSection.tsx:120-150). Desktop bridge routes handle pair request and confirm (apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts:410-440).
how_it_should_work: Pairing works only with a local bridge: the address must be localhost or another allowed local host, otherwise the extension says Pairing is only supported with local desktop bridge (pairing.ts:318-332; policy.ts:315-326).
Pairing has phases: idle, requesting, awaiting code, confirming, paired, or error (pairing.ts:1-11).
A failed pairing shows the error text and stays in the error phase (pairing.ts:66-69).
The side panel only reads the status with GET_CONNECTION_STATUS, which may try to connect at most once on a worker start (background.ts:5074-5088).

Reconnect uses exponential back-off from 1 s up to 30 s, for at most 8 attempts; after that only a manual reconnect starts it again (features/native-bridge/reconnect.ts:1-17). Permanent errors such as host not found stop retries at once (reconnect.ts:10-17).
Unpair asks the desktop app to remove the pairing; if the desktop cannot be reached the pairing is kept and the person is asked to try again (background.ts:5114-5122).

how_it_works.step: Open the panel from the toolbar, a menu or a shortcut
how_it_works.detail: A toolbar click or a context-menu item calls openAssistantPanel, which opens the Chrome side panel for that tab. If the side panel is unavailable, a separate assistant window opens instead.

how_it_works.step: Hand selected text or a page request to the panel
how_it_works.detail: A context-menu item writes a pending request to chrome session storage. The side panel reads it when it opens and attaches the selection or page to the composer.

how_it_works.step: Read the page, asking Chrome for site access if needed
how_it_works.detail: The panel reads the visible tab text after checking the URL, the blocked list and loading state. If Chrome denies access, a card asks the person to allow once, always (for acting) or decline; the grant uses a Chrome host permission request.

how_it_works.step: Build and send the turn from the composer
how_it_works.detail: The composer text, attachments, page context, chat history, chosen model, thinking and web-search flags, and conversation id are gathered and sent to the worker as one message.

how_it_works.step: Worker accepts the message and checks the account
how_it_works.detail: The worker validates the owner and stream id, gets the sign-in context, and starts the chat through the managed chat handler. The request is checked for text length (32,000 characters) and model value.

how_it_works.step: Call the managed chat endpoint and stream the answer
how_it_works.detail: The chat client posts to the web app's chat-completions route on the gateway origin and reads a streamed response, with a 90 second default timeout and frame-size limits.
code: apps/extension/src/background.ts:1121 (CHAT_CHUNK message type seen; not read in full)

how_it_works.step: Run browser tools the model asks for
how_it_works.detail: When the model asks for a tool that touches a page, the worker hands it to the side panel, which runs the page read or browser task and returns the result.
The Computer use tab sends the goal and tab to the worker. The worker takes a lease on the run, checks the goal and tab, and the agent loop drives the page.

how_it_works.step: Show, pause and stop the run
how_it_works.detail: The panel shows the banner and the page indicator. Stop, Take over and Continue send messages that the worker uses to cancel, pause or resume the run.

how_it_works.step: Store the conversation on the device
how_it_works.detail: Each conversation, with its messages and sync state, is saved to chrome local storage under one key, with a cap on count, messages and size.

how_it_works.step: Keep the worker alive and recover after suspension
how_it_works.detail: The panel opens a port and sends a heartbeat every 20 seconds so Chrome does not stop the worker during a reply. If the port drops, the panel resumes a saved cloud run or ends the stream with an error.

key_files.role: Permissions, toolbar action, shortcuts, side panel page, and incognito setting (not allowed).
Service worker: toolbar and menu handlers, chat relay, browser-control runs, native link status, worker lifecycle (about 9,300 lines).
Side panel UI, composer, page capture, site-access requests, chat turns, conversations, tab mentions (about 16,800 lines).
Opens the side panel for a tab, or a fallback assistant window.
Browser-control panel: goal, mode select, Stop, Take over, Continue, status banner.
Agent loop that drives the page and the takeover tool.
Validates and streams a managed chat turn inside the worker.
HTTP client for the managed chat endpoint, models and usage, with size and time limits.
Stores conversations in chrome local storage with limits.
Pairing with the desktop app: code flow, pair token, revocation, local bridge check.
Options control for the default browser-control mode (Ask first, Auto, Full access, YOLO).
Microphone dictation with the first-use notice and error messages.

switches.name: Toolbar and side panel opening

switches.name: Keyboard shortcuts

switches.name: Incognito
switches.effect: Extension does not run in private windows; tabs in private windows are left out of the tab list.

switches.name: Browser-control default mode
switches.effect: Ask first, Auto (default), Full access, or YOLO. Changes whether a card appears and whether routine actions need questions.

switches.name: Free plan view
switches.effect: Free-plan usage screens show only an upgrade path.

switches.name: Attachment limit
switches.effect: At most 5 attachments (tabs and files) per message.

switches.name: Chat limits
switches.effect: Message up to 32,000 characters, up to 100 messages of history, 90 second default timeout.

guide.what_it_is_for: Each AI model in AGI Workforce has a row in one catalog that says what it can read and write (text, pictures, PDFs, audio, video), what it can make (pictures, video), its size limits, its reasoning levels, its cache, its data-retention and region rules, and whether it is current or retired. The apps and the server read that one catalog, so a person only sees models that can do the job they asked for, and a request that a model cannot serve is refused with a clear message instead of failing later. This matters because the same model list is shown on six apps and the API, and one wrong capability would break a turn on all of them.
guide.who_uses_it: Every person who opens the model picker or sends a chat or media request on any of the six apps (Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code extension, Chrome extension). The list shown depends on the plan tier, on the training opt-out setting (a privacy setting that hides models that may train on inputs), and on the developer region rule. Paid plans get the higher-tier models; the code gates by plan in the catalog and in auto routing. Image, video and voice generation also need a feature flag (the code checks canUseImages for images) and can be stopped by a workspace admin's organization policy or spend limit. Developers using the managed chat API get the registry's limits and error codes. Mobile on-device models use a separate local list.

features.name: Text chat input and output
features.use: Lets a person chat with a model that reads text and writes text. Every chat task is routed only to models with both flags.
how_people_use_it: Web: open the model picker in the composer, pick a model, type a message and send.
Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so the same steps apply as Web (not verified in a desktop file).
Mobile: open the model picker sheet, tap a model row, type and send.
CLI: run the chat command, or pick a model with the model list command (apps/cli/src/provider.rs prints the list).
VS Code and Chrome: open the model picker in the chat panel and choose a model.
API: send a chat completion request with a model id.
QA: test this feature on one app at a time, on localhost.
how_it_should_work: Only models that accept text are admitted for chat, on every surface that sends chat.
A model that cannot produce text is never listed as a chat model.
Empty state, waiting state and failure states for the picker were not established from the code read (see not_sure).
On failure of a route, auto routing tries other routes for the same model; it never swaps in a different model silently (auto.ts comment near line 1100 says never a model substitution).
features.on_each_app: All six apps and the API are marked done. The shared catalog and auto routing decide admission on all of them. Web shows a text-only label when no capability chips apply (ModelCatalogue.tsx:310). The CLI prints context and output sizes only (provider.rs:250-265), not input types.

(request-processor.ts:5099-5108). It is refused, not rerouted.

how_it_works.detail: Each model is one row in a curated file. A row holds its name, provider, model type, input and output types (inputModalities, outputModalities), limits, prices, reasoning levels (supportedEfforts), cache policy, lifecycle stage and an optional capabilitiesOverride block of yes/no flags. Changes go in this file, then the catalog is regenerated (AGENTS.md section 4).

how_it_works.step: 2. Compile into one capability record per model
how_it_works.detail: The compiler turns each row into a fixed list of capability names. Input and output types decide textInput, imageInput, audioInput, videoInput, textOutput, imageOutput, audioOutput and videoOutput. The yes/no flags (vision, tools, json, thinking, search, and so on) map to functionCalling, structuredOutput, reasoning, webSearch, codeExecution, computerUse, agentic, promptCaching. capabilitiesOverride, when present, replaces the base flags.

Code never reads the raw file. It calls typed functions: getModelMetadataById finds a row, isModelLive checks the lifecycle, resolveMaxOutputTokens caps output, getRoutingSlotModel returns the model in a named slot such as voice transcription.

how_it_works.step: 4. Picker list per plan on the server
how_it_works.detail: The web catalogue endpoint resolves the viewer's plan and training opt-out, builds the list, drops models that may train when the viewer opted out, and returns the rows with a private 15-second cache header. Each row keeps only the picker capability flags (imageInput, reasoning, functionCalling, webSearch, codeExecution, imageOutput, videoOutput, audioInput, audioOutput).

The web picker shows a chip for each capability (Vision, Reasoning, Tools, Search, Code execution, Image out, Video out, Audio in, Audio out), the context ceiling, the output ceiling and the release date. A model with no chips shows Text only.

how_it_works.step: 6. Auto routing admits or refuses a model
how_it_works.detail: When the person picks Auto, the router checks each model: it must be live, not deprecated, allowed by the plan tier, allowed by organization policy and region, and must have every capability the task needs (for example textInput and textOutput for chat). Routes are then ranked by health, credential, cost and default route. Retention and cache class also affect the ranking.

how_it_works.step: 7. Server checks each managed chat turn
how_it_works.detail: Before the request is sent, the server refuses a turn with pictures for a model that cannot read them, refuses too many pictures for the route, refuses unsupported sampling parameters, and refuses a message that is too long. Older chat history is compacted to fit the window first. Response formats are kept only when the model and the route allow them.

Video generation checks the duration, size, ratio and audio choice against the model's video block. Image generation counts pictures by image API family, refuses an edit for a family that cannot edit, and checks the feature flag, organization policy and spend limit first.
Dictation, read-aloud and live voice each read a named slot from the catalog and refuse if the slot model is not live or has the wrong type. Dictation is behind a kill switch and a privacy check.

how_it_works.step: 10. Each client applies its own view
how_it_works.detail: Mobile builds its own filters (Images, Files, Economy) and a client-side picture count check. VS Code warns when a switch loses tools, pictures or context. Chrome builds its own capability filter from a fixed list with no audio entry. Mobile on-device models come from a separate local list.

key_files.role: Source of truth: one row per model with input and output types, limits, reasoning levels, cache, lifecycle and capability flags.
Compiles the catalog into the capability names and the per-model capability record (lines 1537-1643).
Typed lookups every surface and server route uses (getModelMetadataById, isModelLive, resolveMaxOutputTokens, getRoutingSlotModel).
Auto routing: admits models by lifecycle, plan, policy, region, required capabilities; ranks routes by retention and cache class.
Picker rules: current-model filter and the capability list the picker can filter on.
Builds the per-plan picker list served to apps; keeps only the picker capability flags.
Managed chat turn checks: picture refusal, picture count, unsupported parameters, message too long, compaction.
Picture count lookup (model row first, then route) and native PDF admission.
Which request parameters a model and route accept (sampling rejection, parameter lists).
Web model picker card: capability chips, context and output ceilings, Text only fallback.
Image generation: picture count by image API family, edit refusal, plan and spend checks.
Mobile picker filters (Images, Files, Economy) built on the registry.
Rust mirror of the capability enum (IntrinsicCapability at line 79) and the harness picture-limit lookup used by the CLI.
Per-route settings: picture count, PDF types and page limits, response formats, and which features each route implements.

switches.name: AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED
switches.effect: Turns chat history compaction on or off. On unless the value is 0, false or off.

switches.name: Plan tier and minimum tier per model
switches.effect: Chooses which models the picker lists and which models Auto may use; a model above the plan is locked or refused.

switches.name: Training opt-out
switches.effect: Hides models that may train on inputs when the viewer has opted out.

switches.name: Zero data retention
switches.effect: Requests that need no retention are sent only to routes that keep no data.

switches.name: canUseImages feature flag
switches.effect: Blocks image generation for accounts without the capability.

switches.name: Organization policy, spend limit and managed compute gates
switches.effect: Workspace admin rules can block a model or a provider, or stop spending, before a media or chat job starts.

switches.name: Dictation kill switch
switches.effect: Turns dictation off through the capability gate.

switches.name: Routing slots voice_transcription, voice_speech, voice_live
switches.effect: Name the model each voice feature uses; the slot must be live and the right type.

switches.name: Speed-first routing profile
switches.effect: When the request asks for the speed profile, Auto uses the speed-first slots.

switches.name: Fast mode toggle and workspace block
switches.effect: Shows and sends fast mode for models with a fast tier; a workspace can turn it off.

switches.name: Developer-surface plan capability (VS Code)
switches.effect: Turns the developer model options on or off for the plan.

switches.name: Plan attachment byte limit (web)
switches.effect: Caps the size of attached files and pictures by plan.

switches.name: Per-route picture and PDF limits
switches.effect: Sets the picture count and PDF page limits that apply when a model row has none.

guide.shared_code: Shared across apps and server: the catalog file (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog), the compiler (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs), the typed lookups (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts), auto routing and picker rules (packages/ai/routing/src), and the Rust mirror (crates/agiworkforce-model-registry). The VS Code extension imports the routing package (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:29). The web catalogue and the managed chat, media and voice routes are server code used by the web app and the API. The public Desktop shows the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so it shares the web code. Separate per app: Mobile has its own picker filters, its own on-device model list and its own client-side picture count check (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts). The CLI has its own Rust catalog reader (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs) and its own streaming code. Chrome has its own picker in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts with a fixed label list.

guide.area: 078 UI gating and adaptation components (feature gating, plan checks, model-matched controls, and the explanations shown when something is blocked)
guide.what_it_is_for: This area decides what a person can see and use right now. It checks the plan, the selected model, the workspace policy, the region, the account and the connected devices, then shows the control, hides it, or shows it disabled with a reason. It also tells the person what would unlock the feature (a plan, a connection, another model, a permission), so a blocked feature is not a dead end. Without it, a free user would see controls that fail, and a model that cannot read a file would silently drop it.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user, on every surface, since the checks run for everyone. Paid-plan users see the plan allowance and paid model options. Workspace owners and admins set the policies and role-only controls. Developers and QA use the same code paths; there is no separate admin screen for the gating logic itself. Signed-out or unsupported-region users see the restricted states described in the features below.

features.name: Who may use what, and where it runs
features.use: Decides whether a feature, model or route is allowed for this user on this surface. It combines the plan, workspace policy, role, region and age or eligibility rules. It also lets the user pick where a request runs: on the device with a local model, with the user's own provider key, or on the managed cloud.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker or processing-path choice on the composer and pick Local, own key or Cloud (desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code).
Open workspace settings (owner or admin) to set feature switches, model policy and retention.
On web, open Privacy settings to turn the US-only routing option on or off.
On sign-up, accept the terms; on mobile, enter an age at first run.
how_it_should_work: Every gated feature is checked again on the server for each route that runs a model, not only in the UI.
If a plan or policy blocks a model, the UI hides or disables it and the server refuses it with a reason.
Empty or unknown state: a capability the server does not mention stays as the build shipped it (mobile), so an unreachable server does not disable working features.
Failure: a failed read of training opt-out or region data falls back to the stricter routing (the server logs a warning and routes only to models that keep inputs out of training).
Limits by plan: the plan decides the model roster (see the managed auto-routing mapping), and free users get the free model and region rules.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done (processing-path choice is in the desktop runtime). Mobile: done, with the capability document kept on device and refreshed from the server. CLI: done, mapping plan to routing tier. VS Code: done for model picker and tier revalidation. Chrome: done for the gating checks (routing and processing-path choice is listed as not applicable in the brief for chrome). Required-connection and age-gate rows differ by app (see other features).

features.name: Model-matched composer controls
features.use: Shows the composer controls that the chosen model supports: effort, thinking, sampling options, media duration/size/aspect, and which file types are accepted. Unsupported values are removed or corrected before the request is sent. When a model change would strand attachments, the person chooses to keep them by switching model or to remove them.
how_people_use_it: Pick a model in the composer picker; the effort slider, thinking toggle or media settings appear, change or disappear.
Attach a file; the accepted types depend on the model, and an unsupported type is refused with a message naming a model that can read it.
Switch model with attachments already in the composer; a prompt asks to keep them (switch model) or remove them.
On CLI, pick a model in the model picker; the TUI shows only the options that model accepts.
how_it_should_work: The option list is generated from the model catalog, not typed into each screen.
Unsupported effort levels and sampling values must not be sent to the provider; the server strips or corrects them.
Attachments the model cannot read are refused before upload, with a clear message.
VS Code and Chrome do not gate attachment types (brief status missing for VS Code and Chrome attachment types).
Limits by plan: media generation options depend on the media model and the plan.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (composer footer and new composer). Desktop: done (shares web composer). Mobile: done (effort slider, row-level model options; attachment-preservation choice missing). CLI: done for model options and sampling; attachment types done; attachment-preservation choice missing. VS Code: effort and sampling done; attachment types and media settings missing. Chrome: effort done; attachment types missing; attachment-preservation choice missing. Server: done for the reasoning and sampling checks.

features.name: Hidden and disabled controls
features.use: Hides controls that cannot apply here (for example a desktop-only control on the web), and shows restricted controls greyed out with the reason, so the person can discover what they would unlock.
how_people_use_it: Open the composer footer or model picker; a restricted option is visible but disabled, with a lock or reason text.
Use a surface where a control does not apply; the control is absent rather than shown broken.
how_it_should_work: A control is either hidden (cannot ever apply in this context) or disabled with a reason (applies, but this plan or policy blocks it). It must never be clickable and then fail silently.
Empty state: a model list with nothing allowed shows the upgrade or policy reason, not a blank list.
Failure: a disabled control must name the reason; the reason text comes from the plan or policy decision.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (composer footer disabled states). Desktop: done. Mobile: done (model row shows the disabled state and reason). CLI: done (TUI hides irrelevant controls; model catalog shows disabled reasons). VS Code: done (model picker constants). Chrome: done.

features.name: Plan allowance shown to the user
features.use: Shows how much of the plan allowance remains, read from the server, so the person knows before a limit stops them.
how_people_use_it: On web, open Settings and the Usage section to see the remaining allowance.
On mobile, open Settings and the cloud usage screen.
In the CLI, run the usage summary; in VS Code, the sidebar shows usage.
how_it_should_work: The number comes from the server summary, not from a local counter.
Empty or failed read: show that usage is unavailable rather than a zero that looks real (the brief marks all apps done; the failure text was not opened).
Limit by plan: the allowance differs per plan tier.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: done. Each reads the same server summary through its own client.

features.name: Why something is blocked, and what unlocks it
features.use: Explains a block in plain words: the feature is unsupported here, it is only temporarily unavailable, which plan unlocks it, or which other model can do the task.
how_people_use_it: Send a request the model cannot do (for example an image generation request on a text model); read the message and pick another model.
Open the paywall or upgrade sheet on mobile; read which plan unlocks the feature.
In the CLI or VS Code, the error text names the plan or model to choose.
how_it_should_work: Unsupported (permanent for this model or plan) and temporarily unavailable (retry later) must produce different messages.
The message names a plan or a model where it can.
Server refusal messages are fixed strings; the server returns them so every surface shows the same reason.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (composer message on blocked send). Desktop: done. Mobile: done (paywall sheet and image-generation resolver). CLI: done (error mapping). VS Code: done (error presentation). Chrome: done (per brief). API: done (per brief).

features.name: Connections, devices and runtimes
features.use: Detects that a feature needs an account connection, a paired device (desktop or phone), or a runtime (sandbox, local model, CLI); says which one is missing and gives a way to connect it or to continue the work on the other device.
how_people_use_it: On web, open a plugin page; a checklist shows which connector is missing and a connect action.
On web, open a code session; the rail shows whether a paired desktop is online; choose Continue on desktop.
On mobile, open the companion screen; the pairing status shows connected or not.
In the CLI or VS Code, the Continue action is offered for cloud sessions (CLI and VS Code have Continue on another device).
how_it_should_work: Detection happens before the person relies on the device: the paired-device hook fetches the device list when no desktop host is present.
If no device is paired, the action is hidden or disabled with the reason, not a silent failure.
A sandbox or local runtime that is not available blocks the feature with a message, not a blank panel.
Continue-on-another-device opens a deep link or runs the handoff; the handoff contract is shared.
features.on_each_app: Web: done for connector checklist, paired device and runtime checks. Desktop: done for device and runtime. Mobile: done for device (companion pairing) and runtime (model row); connector detection and connect-account explanation missing. CLI: done for runtime and continue-on-another-device; required-connection detection missing. VS Code: done for runtime and continue; required-connection detection missing. Chrome: done for device (browser tools dialog) and continue; runtime per brief not listed.

features.name: Permission explanations
features.use: Explains what a permission is for before or when the app asks for it (microphone for dictation, site access, agent autonomy in the extension and CLI).
how_people_use_it: Click the dictation button; the app explains that the microphone is used for voice input before the system prompt.
On mobile, open Settings and the permissions list; each permission has a description.
In VS Code, an agent mode consent prompt explains the autonomy being granted.
In Chrome, the side panel asks for site access with a reason.
how_it_should_work: The explanation appears before or at the moment of the system permission request, never after a denial.
A denied permission shows how to grant it later in settings.
The explanation text is part of the permission definition, not written per screen.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: done (each with its own permission registry or consent screen).

features.name: Live refresh after a change
features.use: Updates gated controls after a plan, policy, connection or device change, without reinstalling or restarting.
how_people_use_it: Upgrade the plan or connect a device in one window; the controls in other windows or the open app update without a restart.
On mobile, the capability refresh runs when the app is in use; on VS Code, the tier is revalidated on account change.
how_it_should_work: Changes are picked up on the next refresh of the capability document (mobile) or the tier revalidation (VS Code) or the billing query (web).
A failed refresh keeps the last answer, so a working feature is not disabled by a network error.
A server switch-off takes effect on the next refresh with no store release.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (billing query refresh). Desktop: done. Mobile: done (remote capability refresh). CLI: done (tier cache). VS Code: done (tier revalidation listener). Chrome: done.

On web sign-up, the page posts the terms version and surface to the terms endpoint. A 409 means the terms version is outdated and the user must reload. The mobile age gate stores a verdict on the device.

The CLI maps each plan tier to a managed routing tier. Tiers without developer-surface access fail closed.
