guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the server side of "who you are and what you may touch". It maps each sign-in to one account, checks the account's state on every request, keeps track of signed-in sessions and devices, and lets a workspace admin manage members, roles, invitations, enterprise sign-in and service keys. It also covers pairing a phone or second device, account recovery, account export and deletion, and the rules that stop support staff from reading customer data without a recorded reason and a second approver. Without it, a locked, suspended or removed person could keep working, and there would be no audit trail of who was let in.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person (sign-in, account status, sessions, devices, profile, preferences, terms, pairing, personal API keys, export and deletion). Workspace owners and admins (members, roles, groups, invitations, workspace policy, SSO, SCIM, service principals, workspace deletion). Enterprise identity providers push users in through SCIM and SSO. Support staff use recovery and the support-access grant flow. Developers use personal API keys. The brief marks every item "platform done" and shows no per-app differences; the code confirms the server side only.

features.name: Sign-in and account standing
features.use: Turns a verified sign-in into one AGI account and blocks any request from an account that is locked, recovering, suspended, banned, scheduled for deletion, or deleted.
how_people_use_it: Sign in through the hosted identity provider (the only provider the code can select).
If the account is locked or suspended, the API returns a denial with a recovery or appeal path instead of the data.
No direct control: the check runs on every request.
how_it_should_work: Every request resolves its identity to one account id; a cached answer is used first, otherwise the database is read, and a new identity row is linked if none exists (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:180-212).
An erased account is refused as erased, not as unknown.

Denial reasons: locked, recovery, suspended, deleted. A lockout points to password reset, a suspension points to the appeal page, and deletion has no recovery path (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).
An account with a scheduled deletion is still allowed, so the person can cancel it while signed in (account-status.ts:68-70).
Failure: if the account-status lookup takes longer than its deadline, the workspace binding fails rather than passing the request (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:225-229).
No plan limits seen.
features.on_each_app: Server only, in the web app's API layer. Desktop, mobile, CLI and extension reach it through the same API. The brief marks it done on the platform; no per-app behaviour is recorded.

features.name: Sessions and device sign-in credentials
features.use: Lets a person see which sessions and devices are signed in, end some or all of them, and keep device sign-in alive safely with rotating refresh tokens.
how_people_use_it: Open the sessions list (GET /api/settings/sessions) and see active sessions.
Sign out everything else (DELETE /api/settings/sessions revokes all other sessions, per the handler at apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:189-199).
Open the device list (GET /api/settings/devices), rename a device (PATCH /api/settings/devices/{deviceId}), unlink a device (DELETE on the same route), or stop remote work on it (POST).
A device keeps itself registered by sending heartbeats (POST /api/devices/heartbeat).
how_it_should_work: Session listing returns a bounded page with a truncation flag and a count of sessions that ended by lifetime rules (sessions/route.ts:178-186).
Revoking all sessions is rate-limited and needs a CSRF token and a step-up check before it runs (sessions/route.ts:189-198).

Device refresh rotates a token each time. A token used a second time is a replay: the whole family is marked compromised and revoked, and a compromise record is written (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:305-328).
A device refresh is withheld with a terms error (403) until current terms are accepted, or an age-review error until an adult decision exists (device/refresh/route.ts:257-279).
Heartbeat never turns remote work back on by itself; only pairing again turns it on (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:21-23).
Failure: a provider rate limit makes the bulk session revoke wait and retry, up to a fixed attempt limit (apps/web/lib/server/session-revocation.ts:127-139), then reports what failed.
Developer tokens are revoked by writing their id into a revoked list (apps/web/lib/server/developer-token.ts:135-144).
features.on_each_app: Web server endpoints are shared. The mobile store and the CLI remote-control module call the pairing and device flow (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts:960-994; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:180-201). Desktop and the others are not traced in this brief.

features.name: Account recovery through support
features.use: Lets a locked-out person ask for help when they lost their password, email or second factor. A support person checks the account and restores access.
how_people_use_it: Submit a recovery request (POST /api/support/recovery) with the account email, a reply address, what was lost (password, email or second factor) and details.
Support staff open the ticket and choose an action (POST /api/support/staff/tickets/{ticketId}/recovery) to remove the second factor or add a new sign-in email.
how_it_should_work: A request for an unknown email, or for a deleted account, does nothing visible, so the form does not reveal which accounts exist (apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts:39-49).
If the account has advanced security enrolled, the request is logged as an event instead of a ticket (recovery.ts:51-59).
Otherwise a ticket is opened and the requester gets a receipt email (recovery.ts:69-98).
Staff may only act on a recovery ticket that is still open, and never on an account with advanced security enrolled; that account's owner must use a recovery key (recovery.ts:116-126).
Each change emits a security event (recovery.ts:139-144).
Failure: a ticket error returns a validation message to staff; a missing ticket returns not found (staff recovery route).
Plan limits: none seen.
features.on_each_app: Web server and staff tooling only. The brief marks it done on the platform.

features.name: Profile, preferences, terms and consent
features.use: Stores the person's name, photo and work details; stores their settings in named groups that every app can read and write with version checks; and records which Terms version they accepted and their consents.
how_people_use_it: Read or change the profile through GET and PATCH /api/me.
Read or save settings through GET and PUT /api/settings/preferences, sending a namespace and either a patch or a full value.
Accept current terms through the login-complete or welcome page, which redirects a person who has not accepted (apps/web/lib/server/require-current-terms.ts:8-16).
how_it_should_work: Preferences cannot write the namespaces that have their own endpoint; the request is refused with a validation error naming the endpoint (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts:202-209).
A version clash returns a conflict response with the current value (preferences/route.ts:220).
Reading a settings namespace that fails returns an empty object and logs a warning, not an error (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:58-61).
Profile reads throw on failure rather than reporting no profile, so a failed read cannot overwrite a profile (user-identity.ts:90-93).
Terms: a person whose accepted version is not the current one must accept again before pages load (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts:65-68).
Consent records are written with the current notice version for each purpose (apps/web/lib/server/consent-records.ts:95-115).
Failure: a write error is logged and turned into a generic 'Failed to save settings' error (preferences/route.ts:213-218).
features.on_each_app: Shared server endpoints for every app. The brief does not record per-app UI.

features.name: Workspaces (personal and team)
features.use: A person has a personal workspace and may belong to team workspaces. They choose which one is active, and data is scoped to it. Admins create, rename or schedule deletion of a team workspace.
how_people_use_it: List workspaces (GET /api/settings/workspaces) and switch the active one (PUT with a workspace id, or the personal selector).
Or send the workspace selector as a request header; the header wins over the saved choice (apps/web/lib/services/active-workspace-service.ts:68-84).

Admins create, change or delete the organization (POST, PATCH, DELETE /api/settings/organization). Deleting schedules erasure after a cooling period and can be cancelled (POST /api/settings/organization/deletion/cancel).
how_it_should_work: A selector that is not a valid id is refused with a validation error; a workspace the person is not a member of is refused as forbidden (active-workspace-service.ts:68-78).
The chosen workspace is saved on the person's settings row and kept in a cache; a change clears the cache (active-workspace-service.ts:196-214).
Deleting a workspace returns a message saying what will be erased and when, and the date it is scheduled for (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:572-576).
Ownership transfer is a separate route (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/transfer-ownership/route.ts:132).
Failure: an unreadable policy denies the request rather than allowing it (see the policy feature).
Plan limits: seats come from the organization's licensed seat count (apps/web/lib/services/organization-seat-service.ts:33-54).
features.on_each_app: Shared server endpoints. The workspace console UI is in apps/web/features/workspace-console. Other apps' behaviour is not traced.

features.name: Members, invitations, groups and roles
features.use: Admins invite people, change or remove members, group them, and give roles with permissions. Nobody can hand out more permissions than they hold.
how_people_use_it: Invite by email (POST /api/settings/organization/invitations); accept through the invitation link (POST /api/settings/team/invitations/accept).
Change a member's role (PATCH /api/settings/team/{memberId}, memberId in the form organizationId:userId) or remove them (DELETE on the same route).
Create or rename groups and set their members (groups routes); create roles (POST /api/settings/organization/roles).
The additional-roles card in the workspace console lists and changes role holders (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceRoles.tsx:487-542).
how_it_should_work: Invitation tokens are random and only their SHA-256 hash is stored; invitations expire, can be resent a limited number of times, and can be revoked (apps/web/lib/services/organization-invitation-service.ts:17-42).
Role changes and removals need team admin access and a CSRF token; removal then cuts off the member's live credentials (see the cut-off feature below).

A permission a role carries must be held by the actor; otherwise the request is refused as forbidden (apps/web/lib/services/organization-permission-service.ts:95-108, which calls assertPermissionsWithinActor).
Only the primary owner can hold certain permissions; the refusal says so (organization-role-service.ts:86-99 is for the role-level check).
Failure: a failed members read shows an error line in the card (WorkspaceRoles.tsx:542-546).
Plan limits: not verified in this area.
features.on_each_app: Web workspace console and server endpoints. Other apps are not traced.

features.name: Workspace policy enforcement
features.use: Applies each workspace's rules (feature access, second-factor requirement, IP allow-list, retention, product analytics) to a person's requests, scoped to the workspace they are using.
how_people_use_it: Admins set the policy through the policy and posture routes under /api/settings/organization.
The person does not act directly; a request that the policy forbids is refused.
how_it_should_work: An unreadable workspace or policy is not treated as 'no policy'. Each read is retried once; then the request is denied with 'workspace_policy_unavailable', except a purchase that depends only on a billing hold (organization-policy-gate.ts:190-197).
A request against a workspace the person cannot access is denied with an explicit decision (organization-policy-gate.ts:211-224).
If the second-factor requirement is unknown, the request fails (organization-policy-gate.ts:490-496).
Product analytics are blocked if any governing workspace forbids them (organization-policy-gate.ts:501-513).
Failure: an unreadable billing hold denies a purchase.
features.on_each_app: Server-side gate used by web routes. The brief marks it done on the platform.

features.name: Enterprise sign-in and directory sync
features.use: Lets an admin connect the company identity provider (SAML or OIDC), verify the company's email domain, and have users created, updated or turned off from the company directory.
how_people_use_it: Admin lists, creates or deletes SSO connections (GET, POST, DELETE /api/admin/sso).
The customer's directory calls the SCIM endpoints (GET and POST /api/scim/v2/Users; a bearer token is checked first, apps/web/lib/server/scim/scim-auth.ts:26).
how_it_should_work: Connections are created in the hosted identity provider with the domain and attribute mapping; the SAML form is set to refuse IdP-first sign-in (apps/web/lib/server/sso/clerk-enterprise-connections.ts:157-168).
A user signing in from a verified domain is created or joined with the connection's default role when just-in-time provisioning is on (apps/web/lib/server/sso/jit-provisioning.ts:39-60).
Only the email domain (or a subdomain of it) matches a connection (jit-provisioning.ts:28-37).
SCIM user lists are filtered and paged; a create returns 201 with a location header (apps/web/app/api/scim/v2/Users/route.ts:23-56).
Failure: SCIM errors are returned as SCIM error responses through scimResponse; the exact error shapes were not traced.
features.on_each_app: Server-side admin and directory endpoints. The brief marks them done on the platform.

features.name: Service accounts and API keys
features.use: Service accounts are non-person principals with limited scopes, used by workspace automation. Personal API keys are issued to a person, hashed, can expire, and can be rotated or revoked. S89.21 (personal access tokens) is not applicable: no such service exists.
how_people_use_it: Admin lists and disables or enables service principals (GET and PATCH /api/settings/organization/service-principals).
A person creates, lists or rotates an API key (GET and POST /api/settings/api-keys; the create step needs a step-up check first).
Revoke or delete a key through the API-key routes.
how_it_should_work: A service principal cannot perform an action that acts for a person (service-principal.ts:87-95).
A service principal may only use scopes it was given; a call outside them is refused naming the missing scope (service-principal.ts:97-110).
A new service principal's scopes are capped at a ceiling; scopes above the ceiling are refused (service-principal.ts:112-119).
Each person may have at most 20 active keys; going over returns a validation error (apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:26, 105-109).
Creating a key requires a step-up check and a rate limit (api-keys/route.ts:111-120).
A key is stored with a hash and a short prefix (api-key-service.ts:216-217).
Rotation locks the old key row and refuses a key whose project or metadata changed (api-key-service.ts:145-172).
Failure: a project that does not exist or is archived is refused (api-key-service.ts:135-140).
features.on_each_app: Web server endpoints. The brief lists no per-app UI. S89.21 is not applicable on any app.

features.name: Pairing a second device
features.use: Links a phone or another desktop to a signed-in desktop or account with a short code, so the second device can use remote control.
how_people_use_it: The desktop or account creates a code and shows it as a QR code (POST /api/pair/initiate returns qrData 'agiw:<code>').
The phone scans or types the code and claims it (POST /api/pair/claim), which sends the account id to the relay.
The phone app then connects using the pairing secret it was given (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts:960-994).
how_it_should_work: Initiating needs a signed-in person, a CSRF token, a rate limit, and a current remote-control standing check (pair/initiate/route.ts:47-66).
If the relay URL or its secret is missing, the request returns 503 'Pairing is not configured' rather than working without the relay (pair/initiate/route.ts:69-80).
Relay URLs must be secure, except localhost in development (pair/initiate/route.ts:72).
Claim sends the account id to the relay, and the relay rejects a rotation that does not match the stored account id (services/signaling-server/src/db.ts:170-177).
A pairing expires; the relay sweeps expired pairings about an hour after they expire, so the maximum age is eight days (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:425-435).
Desktop-side pairing codes are 8 characters and relay codes 12 characters (packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts:50-60).
Failure: an unreachable relay during claim is logged and reported (pair/claim route).
features.on_each_app: Web server (pair routes), relay service (services/signaling-server), mobile app (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts), and the CLI remote-control module (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:190-201, which checks the server address). Desktop uses the same contract types.

features.name: Deleting and exporting account data
features.use: Produces the person's data export and erases the account (or an organization) across every store, except data held by a legal hold, and records what was kept.
how_people_use_it: Export through GET and POST /api/user/export and the archive routes.
Request deletion through GET and DELETE /api/user/delete-account.
Workspace deletion through DELETE /api/settings/organization, cancelled from /api/settings/organization/deletion/cancel.
A scheduled job (purge-deleted-accounts and purge-deleted-organizations cron routes) completes the erasure after the cooling period.
how_it_should_work: Account erasure deletes stored files (knowledge objects, avatars, media) and their backup copies, and leaves a tombstone row (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:770-820, 860-869).
Organization erasure is blocked when the workspace has an active legal hold; data is kept and the report says so (apps/web/lib/server/organization-erasure.ts:285-306).
If the billing hold cannot be read, the erasure keeps the organization and says why (organization-erasure.ts:309-318).
Each store's retention is listed in a deletion manifest, which states the deletion path for each store (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:425-459).
Failure: each store reports success or failure; untracked knowledge ledger rows block the erasure until settled (account-erasure.ts:847-857).
features.on_each_app: Server-side only. The brief marks it done on the platform.

features.name: Support staff access to customer data
features.use: Lets support staff read customer data only through a grant that has a reason, a ticket reference, a limited window and a second operator's approval. Every read is logged.
how_people_use_it: A staff member requests a grant with a reason, ticket reference, purpose and scopes (POST /api/admin/support-access, apps/web/app/api/admin/support-access/route.ts:141-166).
A second operator approves or denies it (route action 'approve' or 'deny', route.ts:185-189).
List grants and events with GET /api/admin/support-access.
how_it_should_work: Approval by the requester is refused: 'the requester cannot approve their own access' (apps/web/lib/server/support-access-service.ts:489-491).
The window defaults to one hour and can be at most eight hours (support-access-service.ts:58-59, 214-226).
Expired grants are moved to an expired state in the trail (support-access-service.ts:598-625).
Each event is written to a hash chain, so edits can be detected (support-access-service.ts:342-369).
Every grant creation writes an audit event (route.ts:167-181), and each data read is also recorded (apps/web/lib/server/admin-data-access.ts:24-50).
Failure: a read the grant does not allow is refused by the access check (support-access-service.ts:705) before any data is read.
features.on_each_app: Server-side admin tooling only.

how_it_works.detail: A request's identity is verified by the one identity provider the app selects. The verified subject is looked up (cache first, then the database) and mapped to an AGI account id. A new identity link is created when none exists.
Every API request calls the account check. Locked, recovering, suspended, banned, deleted and scheduled-deletion states are decided in one function, and a denial carries a reason and a recovery path.

The active workspace is taken from a request header if present, otherwise from a cache, otherwise from the saved setting. A header that is malformed or names a workspace the person is not in is refused.

A member's permissions are read from their role and group roles. A grant cannot exceed the actor's own permissions. Each workspace policy is read with a retry, and an unreadable policy denies the request.

A removal deletes the membership row first, then revokes the member's workspace-issued sessions, device refresh families, mobile intent tokens, and API keys. Failures are returned as warnings and recorded in the audit event.
A device exchanges its refresh token for a new one. Terms and age checks can withhold the new token. A replayed token marks the whole family compromised and revokes it.

A device heartbeat upserts its row (surface, OS, version, capabilities) and never re-enables remote work. The settings list reads the registry with a live-credential flag; rename and unlink are separate routes.

The web server checks the person's remote-control standing and the relay settings, then asks the relay for a pairing code. The phone claims it, and the relay checks the account id before rotating credentials.

Account erasure removes stored files and backup copies, then leaves a tombstone. Organization erasure stops for an active legal hold or unreadable billing state. A deletion manifest states the path for each store.

A staff request creates a pending grant with a reason and a ticket reference. A second operator approves it with a time window capped at eight hours. Each read is recorded in the workspace trail and in a hash-chained support log.

key_files.role: Runs the account-state check and workspace binding on each authenticated request.
Single decision table for locked, recovering, suspended, deleted and scheduled-deletion accounts.
Maps a verified sign-in to an AGI account id, with cache and identity-link creation.
Chooses the identity provider from the environment; only the hosted provider is implemented.
Cuts off a removed member's sessions, device tokens, API keys and shared connectors.
Remove-member and change-role endpoints for team members.
Applies workspace policy (MFA, IP, analytics, retention, billing hold) and denies when a policy cannot be read.
Rotating device refresh with replay detection and terms and age gating.
Starts a pairing through the relay after standing and configuration checks.
Erases account data and stored files, including backup copies.
Support access grants: request, second-operator approval, time window, hash-chained trail.

data_kept.what: Profile row: display name, avatar, accepted Terms version, acceptance time and surface, account status
data_kept.where: Neon database table public.profiles (apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts:40-42; apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts:56-58; apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:96-98)

data_kept.what: Per-person settings, one JSON object with namespaces (identity fields, workspace selection, preferences)
data_kept.where: Database table public.user_settings, column settings (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:50; apps/web/lib/services/active-workspace-service.ts:196-210)

data_kept.what: Identity link from the provider subject to the AGI account
data_kept.where: Database table named in a query constant in apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts (table name not opened)

data_kept.what: Device rows: surface, OS, versions, capabilities, last seen, remote-work flag, credential family id
data_kept.where: Database table public.device_registrations (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:24-40; settings/devices route.ts:67-81)

data_kept.what: Device refresh tokens and token families, with revoked, used and compromised markers
data_kept.where: Database tables device_refresh_tokens and device_refresh_token_families (apps/web/lib/server/refresh-token-family.ts:95-124)

data_kept.what: Revoked developer tokens by id until expiry
data_kept.where: Database table revoked_jwts (apps/web/lib/server/developer-token.ts:136-142)

data_kept.what: Personal API keys: name, scopes, hash, short prefix, expiry, project id
data_kept.where: Database table api_keys (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:216-217)

data_kept.what: Organization and membership: members, roles, group roles, seats, owner, invitations (token hash only, status, expiry)
data_kept.where: Database tables organizations, organization_members, organization_roles, organization_group_roles (apps/web/lib/services/organization-role-service.ts:75-80; organization-seat-service.ts:37-43); invitation columns at organization-invitation-service.ts:44-46

data_kept.what: Consent decisions, with the subject email stored only as a hash
data_kept.where: Database table consent_records (apps/web/lib/server/consent-records.ts:95-99)

data_kept.where: Via recordAuditEvent (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/[memberId]/route.ts:71-87) and emitIdentitySecurityEvent (recovery.ts:51-57)

data_kept.what: Sessions and sign-in credentials
data_kept.where: Held by the external hosted identity provider, not in this repository (apps/web/lib/server/session-revocation.ts:137-143 calls it)

switches.name: AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER
switches.effect: Chooses the identity provider. Only the hosted provider exists; any other value throws a configuration error.

switches.name: SIGNALING_HTTP_URL and SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET
switches.effect: Both required for pairing; without them pairing returns 503. A localhost URL is allowed only in development.

switches.name: Developer mode check (NODE_ENV)
switches.effect: Allows a non-HTTPS relay URL in development only.

switches.name: MAX_ACTIVE_API_KEYS
switches.effect: Caps active personal API keys at 20.

switches.name: DEFAULT_SUPPORT_ACCESS_TTL_MS and MAX_SUPPORT_ACCESS_TTL_MS
switches.effect: Default support grant window one hour, maximum eight hours.

switches.name: CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION
switches.effect: The Terms version a person must have accepted; a change forces re-acceptance on every gated page and device refresh.

switches.name: Workspace policy (MFA, IP allow-list, product analytics, retention, billing hold)
switches.effect: Set per workspace by admins; applied to every request scoped to that workspace.

switches.name: Seat count
switches.effect: Licensed seats limit how many members a workspace can hold.

switches.name: jit_provisioning_enabled and jit_default_role on an SSO connection
switches.effect: Whether a verified-domain sign-in creates a member, and at which role.

switches.name: Remote-work flag on a device
switches.effect: Set by pairing, cleared by stop-remote-work; a heartbeat never sets it.

switches.name: ORGANIZATION_DELETION_COOLING_PERIOD_DAYS
switches.effect: Days between a workspace deletion request and its erasure; the value was not opened.

switches.name: Plan tier and entitlement
switches.effect: Plan name, billing owner, and seat type are reported to the client; feature gating by plan was not traced in full.

guide.shared_code: Shared across apps: the identity adapter package (packages/platform/identity, used by the web server); the cloud contracts package (@agiworkforce/cloud-contracts) for device heartbeat and rename request shapes (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:5-8; apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts:5); and the pairing contract file packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts, which its comment says is shared by desktop and mobile. Separate per app: the mobile pairing store (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts), the CLI remote-control module (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs), and the signaling relay, which is its own deployable (services/signaling-server) and repeats some constants (deletion-manifest.ts:425-431). The server services in apps/web/lib are used only by the web API routes.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The Should says blocks use until current Terms are accepted, but mustAcceptTerms returns false when the acceptance read fails and logs 'letting the account through'. A database fault therefore admits an account that may not have accepted current Terms.

The Should lists four identity adapters (password, social, passkey, SSO) behind one interface. The factory has one case, the hosted provider; password is a method on the interface, and no passkey or social adapter was found.
Brief line reference for S89.06 cites team/[memberId]/route.ts:301 for the remove route, but the file has 162 lines; the DELETE and PATCH exports are at lines 156-157.
Brief line reference for S89.22 cites packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts:189, but the file has 124 lines. The code-length constants are at lines 50-60.
Brief item S89.10 says the organization service transfers ownership, but the organization route file has no transfer handler; transfer is a separate route.

Account recovery does not restore access for an account with advanced account security on; the owner must use a recovery key. This is a deliberate limit that the brief's Should ('regain access when password, email or second factor is lost') does not mention.
Session listing stops after a fixed number of pages, and the code notes that more sessions may still be live when the limit is reached.

not_sure: Whether the hosted identity provider implements password, social, passkey and SSO sign-in as the Should describes; those flows live outside this repository.
Whether recovery verifies the requester automatically; the code shows a staff person acts on the ticket, but the staff check steps were not read.
The table names used in the identity-link and support-access queries were not all opened, and row-level security was not checked.
The value of ORGANIZATION_DELETION_COOLING_PERIOD_DAYS and the exact plan gates for seats and workspace features were not established.
The bodies of the group, role-mapping, SCIM auth and token service routes were only partly read; the error shapes returned on failure were not traced.
Per-app behaviour: the brief gives no per-app status beyond 'platform done', and desktop, Chrome extension and VS Code extension code for these features was not opened.
The pair/claim route, the signaling relay's claim logic and the CLI remote-control flow were only partly read.
The user-facing delete-account and export routes were located but not read in full, so their interaction with the erasure coordinator is unverified.
No builds, tests or servers were run, as the task was read-only; claims are from code reading only.

guide.area: Conversation and synchronization components (brief area 90, items S90.01 to S90.23)
guide.what_it_is_for: This area keeps a person's chats safe and the same on every device. Conversations, messages, edits, forks, drafts and artifacts are saved on the server, and changes made on one device reach the others through a sync protocol. It also streams answers live, lets a dropped answer resume, shares a chat by link, searches and exports chats, and sends notifications when a run finishes. Without it, a chat would live in one browser or phone and disappear when that device is lost.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user of a surface that calls the managed (Cloud) chat API. The server code shows no plan gate on the sync routes themselves. Free users are limited by a daily allowance on new conversations and message writes (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:576; apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:519). Workspace administrators can turn cloud sync off per surface (apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-evaluator.ts:329-339). Anyone with a share link can read a shared chat without signing in (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:72). Mobile syncs only in Cloud app mode (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:97-107). Developers reach the same routes through the API and the CLI.

features.name: Saved conversations and messages
features.use: Stores each chat and each turn (question or answer) on the server, so the history can be listed, opened and added to from any device.
how_people_use_it: Send a message in a chat. The message is saved to that chat.
Open the chat list. Scroll down to load older chats.
Open a chat. Scroll up to load older messages.
how_it_should_work: A new chat is created with POST to the conversations route; the list is read with GET and a cursor. The first page of the list is read by offset, not by cursor (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:104-107), so the brief's keyset paging applies only to later pages.
Deleting a chat is a soft delete: deleted_at is set and the row stays (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:40-48). A deleted chat is not listed or opened.
Empty state, waiting state and failure text for the list are in the web and mobile screens, which I did not open.
Temporary chats are not stored: a draft or title is refused for them (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:223).
On a free plan, creating a chat or writing messages counts against the daily allowance; when it is spent, the server refuses the write (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:576).
features.on_each_app: The brief gives one status for all apps: platform done. The server routes are shared. The mobile app reads and writes these routes through apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts. The web app's use of the list and message routes was not traced in full.

features.name: Versions, branches and forks
features.use: Keeps every edited or regenerated answer as a sibling of the original, lets the person pick which one is visible, and lets a person fork a chat from one message into a new chat.
how_people_use_it: Edit a question, or ask for another answer. Each new answer becomes another version of that turn.
Use the version control on a turn to move between versions.
Use the branch or fork action on a message to start a new chat from that point.
how_it_should_work: Messages form a tree: parent_id names the message a row answers or replaces. Rows that share a parent are versions of one another (apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:37).
The visible path is recorded on the conversation as active_leaf_message_id, set through the conversation update route (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:382).

A fork creates a new conversation and copies messages into it; the source and copied ids are mapped in conversation_branch_messages (apps/web/db/neon/0078_conversation_branching_runtime.sql:25-30). Forks also count against the free daily allowance (apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:208).
A fork that is retried with the same request returns the same branch rather than making a second one (apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:57, findIdempotentBranch).
Deleting a message with children needs an explicit choice; a message with children cannot be removed by cascade (apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:30-33).
features.on_each_app: Platform status only. The branch list route is apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/branches/route.ts. The app screens that show version paging were not opened.

features.name: Pin, star, archive and chat settings
features.use: Lets a person pin a chat to the top, star it, archive it, and change its title, model, project or temporary flag. Each change is saved to the server.
how_people_use_it: Pin, star or archive a chat from its menu.
Rename a chat or change its model or project from the chat settings.
Turn on temporary mode for a chat so it is not kept.
how_it_should_work: Pin, star and archive are columns on web_conversations (apps/web/db/neon/0059_conversation_star_archive.sql:22) and are written by the update route (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:369-400).
Each update can carry an expected version. If the stored version differs, the route answers with a conflict status 409 (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:260-266 and 388).
A pinned chat sorts first in the list (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:124).
A temporary chat cannot be moved into a project; the server refuses that change (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:312-314).
features.on_each_app: Platform status only. The web and mobile controls were not opened.

features.name: Automatic chat titles
features.use: Gives a new chat a short title after its first question, so the sidebar is readable without typing a name.
how_people_use_it: Send the first question in a new chat. The title appears in the sidebar shortly after the answer starts or finishes.
Rename the chat yourself to replace the automatic title.
how_it_should_work: A short title is first cut from the first question on the server, at the time the question is saved (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:169-171; apps/web/lib/chat-title.ts:21-26).

A model then writes a better title in the background. The title is saved only if the current title is still the one it replaces, so a title the person set is never overwritten (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/generate-title.ts:335-346).
If the title step fails, the chat keeps its cut title and a warning is logged (generate-title.ts:353-358). The request that saved the message does not wait for the title (generate-title.ts:368-377).
Title generation counts against the daily allowance under the feature name conversation_title (generate-title.ts:54).
features.on_each_app: Platform status only.

features.name: Composer drafts
features.use: Keeps an unsent message for each chat, so a half-written message is still there after a reload or on another device.
how_people_use_it: Type in the composer, then leave or close the chat.
Reopen the chat, on the same device or another, and the unsent text is back.
how_it_should_work: The draft is saved on the chat row as draft and draft_updated_at (apps/web/db/neon/0219_conversation_drafts.sql:28-30).
A draft write does not change the chat's updated_at or server_version, so typing does not move the chat to the top of the list (apps/web/db/neon/0219_conversation_drafts.sql:14-17).
The newer draft wins between two devices, using draft_updated_at (apps/web/db/neon/0219_conversation_drafts.sql:10-12).
Saves are queued per chat in the browser and retried; a failed save is not shown as saved (apps/web/features/chat/services/conversation-draft.ts:120-137).
Temporary chats never store a draft (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:223).
A draft is not sent to the model; it is only text kept on the chat.
features.on_each_app: Web: the composer hook is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1495. Mobile and other apps: not verified.

features.name: Search, export and import
features.use: Finds words in chat titles and messages, saves a chat as a file, and brings text from a file into the user's memory.
how_people_use_it: Type in the search box. Results show matching chats and messages, with a short snippet.
Open the export dialog from a chat, choose Markdown, JSON, HTML, PDF or DOCX, and download the file.
Paste text or a list into the memory import, preview the items, then commit them.
how_it_should_work: Search runs a text match over titles and message content. Indexes exist for these columns (apps/web/db/neon/0101_sync_and_search_indexes.sql:82-88). A query shorter than three characters falls back to a scan, which is allowed only because of rate limits (0101 lines 78-81).
Temporary chats and deleted messages are excluded from search (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:375-377). Archived chats are excluded unless includeArchived is true (route.ts:378).

Export is built in the browser. It removes expiring links, replacing them with a placeholder (apps/web/features/chat/services/conversation-export.ts:31-36 and 61-67). PDF and DOCX are made in the browser (apps/web/features/chat/services/document-export-service.ts:30-43).

Import is a two-step route: a dry run returns a preview, then a commit writes the items (apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:55 and 107). The items are written to user memory, not to chats (apps/web/lib/memory/import-store.ts:63).
Limits: import text has a size cap, and large batches are refused with an error (packages/contracts/types/src/memory-import.ts:83-85).
features.on_each_app: Web: search, export and import routes and dialogs. Mobile, desktop, CLI and extension: not verified for these features.

features.name: Sharing a chat by link
features.use: Makes a frozen, cleaned copy of a chat that anyone with the link can read, and lets the owner change who can read it or cancel it.
how_people_use_it: Open a saved chat and choose Share. Pick how long the link lasts. Copy the link.
Change the visibility of the link (for example, public or workspace only) from the share list.
Revoke a link to stop it working.
how_it_should_work: Only a chat saved to the account can be shared. An unsaved chat is refused with a message to turn on sync first (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:203-204).
Share creation checks that the stored chat matches the snapshot being shared; if the chat has unsaved changes, the share is refused (route.ts:206 and 328).
The expiry is set in days (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:80 and 56).
The shared copy strips local file paths and tool-call paths (route.ts:100-125).
Visibility changes are a PATCH on the share token (apps/web/app/api/share/[token]/route.ts:168). Revoke is a DELETE (route.ts:100). Both write an audit event.
An expired link shows as not available (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:78-80).
features.on_each_app: Web only in the code I opened. Other apps were not checked.

features.name: Live answer stream and resume
features.use: Streams each answer to the screen as it is written. If the connection drops, the screen picks up where it stopped without showing the same text twice.
how_people_use_it: Send a message and watch the answer appear word by word.
Close the laptop lid or lose the network mid-answer. When the connection returns, the answer finishes on the screen.
how_it_should_work: The server sends each event as a server-sent event (a one-way stream over HTTP). Every few seconds with no output, it sends a keep-alive line so middle boxes do not drop the connection (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/sse-heartbeat.ts:6 and 29-40).

Each event is wrapped in an envelope with a schema version and a sequence number. The schema is checked on the server and on the client (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/agent-events.ts:321-341).
Each event is saved to the run's event journal in batches (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:841-845).

A resume request names the last sequence and character count the client has shown. The server sends only the rest of the saved answer (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/resume/stream/route.ts:66-83).
Resume is refused with a not found error if the turn does not exist for the caller (route.ts:72), and with an invalid-cursor error if the cursor is malformed (route.ts:60).
A gap in sequence numbers stops the client from settling the answer until the missing part is replayed (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3241-3285).
features.on_each_app: Web: apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts. Desktop: apps/desktop/src-tauri is not the reader; the reader is apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:1240. VS Code and extension read the same envelope (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:1308; apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:28). Mobile and CLI: not verified.

features.name: Attempt record for each answer
features.use: Records every try at an answer (first try, retry, regenerate), with its outcome and its provider and model, so failed and cancelled tries can be seen later.
how_people_use_it: No direct action. A person sees the result as an answer, a retry or an error message in the chat.
how_it_should_work: Each managed request has a row in managed_usage_requests. Migration 0329 adds conversation_id, attempt_outcome (completed, failed or cancelled) and attempt_error_class (apps/web/db/neon/0329_managed_usage_attempt_record.sql:24-33).
The conversation id is written when the request is reserved for a conversation the person owns (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:661-662).
The outcome is written once, by the first finalization (managed-usage-request-service.ts:681-682; apps/web/lib/services/free-trial-service.ts:798 and 903).
If the outcome cannot be written, a warning is logged (managed-usage-request-service.ts:688).
features.on_each_app: Server only. Shown to users only through their usage and history screens, which I did not open.

features.name: Sync between devices
features.use: Keeps chats, messages and artifacts the same on every device. A change made offline is queued and sent when the connection returns. A delete reaches the other devices and stays deleted.
how_people_use_it: Make a change on the phone, then open the web app or the CLI. The change is there.
Go offline, make edits, then come back online. The app sends the queued changes and shows the server copy if a conflict is found.
Delete a chat on one device. It disappears from the others.
how_it_should_work: Each device pulls changes since its last cursor and pushes its own changes with a base version. The server applies a change when the base version matches, treats an identical repeat as done, and returns a conflict with the server copy otherwise (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:235-259; 310-320; 334-355).

Every change, including a soft delete, gets a new server_version from a sequence through a trigger (apps/web/db/neon/0038_cloud_sync_versioning.sql:50-62). Deletes are sent as tombstones (packages/client/sync/src/conversations.ts:52-55).

A delete pushed by a device is not re-created by a later push of the same chat: the server only applies a push when the row is not deleted or the push is also a delete (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:629 and 833).

The pull returns at most 500 chats, 1000 messages and 500 artifacts per call (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:54-56). The cursor is moved to the lowest version that was not fully returned (route.ts:974-1000).

Protocol version: a push that declares a version the server cannot read is refused with 426 (update required) when it is too old, and with a validation error when it is too new (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:940-947; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/sync.ts:33-43).

The mobile app syncs every 30 seconds while active and again when it comes back to the foreground (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1068-1077). Its queue of changes is kept on the phone (apps/mobile/stores/chat/cloudSyncStateStore.ts:88-96).

The CLI records server versions after each push and pull (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs:343-364). Its handshake reads the 426 status and the minimum version header (apps/cli/src/cloud/handshake.rs:31-60).
A sync push is refused for a temporary chat on mobile (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1088-1094).
features.on_each_app: Mobile (cloudSyncEngine.ts) and CLI (cloud/chat.rs) are shown in the code. The browser extension pulls with the conversations scope (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts:865). Web and desktop sync code was not traced. Mobile syncs only in Cloud mode.

features.name: Notifications when a run finishes
features.use: When a background run (a task or a research job) changes state, the person sees it in the notification feed and, if allowed, on the phone or in the browser.
how_people_use_it: Start a long run and leave the app. A push appears on the phone or in the browser when it finishes or needs attention.
Open the notifications feed in the app to see the same event, and tap it to open the run.
how_it_should_work: One event is written to the notification feed first (apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:153-161). Finished or failed runs use a dedupe key so the same final event is not stored twice (line 160).

Then the push is sent to the phone transport and the browser transport (apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:163-177; apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts:281-297 and 362-369).
A phone that turned off this kind of alert does not get the push. The phone switch is separate from the browser switch (agent-notification-service.ts:146-149).
Quiet hours defer the push until they end (push-notification-service.ts:300-326).
Phone tokens that the push service reports as not registered are removed (push-notification-service.ts:208-211 and 135-147).
If a push fails, the failure is logged and the feed item is still kept (agent-notification-service.ts:180-182).
features.on_each_app: Mobile push and web push are in the code. Desktop, CLI and extension were not traced for receiving pushes.

features.name: Opening a link to a chat or item
features.use: A stable link opens the right chat, run, schedule, file or artifact, even from an email or another device.
how_people_use_it: Open a link of the form /open/<type>/<id>. If you are not signed in, you are sent to the sign-in page and then returned to the link.
how_it_should_work: The link is validated; a malformed id or unknown type returns not found (apps/web/app/open/[target]/[id]/page.tsx:28-31).
A signed-out visitor is redirected to sign-in, with the link kept as the return address (page.tsx:33-36).
The resolver checks ownership. A chat that is temporary is reported as not found; a deleted chat is reported as deleted (apps/web/lib/services/product-link-resolver.ts:88-90).
A link to something that exists for another account is reported as unauthorized rather than not found (product-link-resolver.ts:41-43).
States shown to the person are ready (redirect), not found, deleted, expired or unauthorized (apps/web/features/notifications/components/ProductLinkUnavailable.tsx:26-68).
features.on_each_app: Web route only in the code I opened. The link format is shared from packages/contracts/types/src/product-links.ts:45-66.

how_it_works.step: Send a message and save it
how_it_works.detail: The person sends a message. The server saves the turn on the chat, links it to its parent message, and, for the first question, cuts a short title and schedules a model title in the background.

how_it_works.step: Stream the answer and journal it
how_it_works.detail: The model route streams the answer as server-sent events with keep-alive lines. Each event is an envelope with a sequence number. The events are saved to the run's journal in batches.

how_it_works.step: Read the stream on the client
how_it_works.detail: The web client decodes each event, checks its envelope, and shows it. A gap in sequence numbers pauses settlement until the missing events are replayed.
If the connection drops, the client posts its cursor (sequence and character count). The server reads the saved answer, cuts off what the client has, and streams the rest.

how_it_works.step: Check the sync gate and protocol version
how_it_works.detail: A sync push or pull first checks the workspace policy for cloud sync and, for a push, the protocol version. A too-old push gets 426; a too-new one gets a validation error.

how_it_works.step: Apply pushed changes with a base version
how_it_works.detail: The push route checks the project belongs to the active workspace, checks the free allowance, then applies each conversation, message and artifact only where its base version matches. Other rows come back as conflicts with the server copy.

A device asks for changes after its cursor. The server returns chats, messages and artifacts, deletions included as tombstones. The client applies them and keeps local edits that are still waiting to be sent.

how_it_works.step: Store the row and its version
how_it_works.detail: The database gives every change a new version number from a sequence. Soft deletes set deleted_at and also get a version, so they reach other devices.

key_files.role: Server side of cross-device sync: pull by cursor, push with base versions, conflicts, sync gate and free allowance.
Sync protocol version (2, minimum 2), the too-old and too-new rules, and the wire schemas for sync deltas.
Read, update (pin, star, archive, title, model, project, active leaf, draft) and soft-delete one chat; version check and 409 conflict.
Saves a turn, sets the provisional title on the first question, and schedules the model title.
Builds the envelope for each stream event with a sequence number and the event id.
Event journal for runs: appends envelopes in batches, reads state, archives and restores runs.
Browser client that reads the stream, checks sequence gaps and calls resume.
Browser side of draft saves: per-chat queue, retries, revision check between devices.
Phone sync engine: push and pull loop, conflict handling, dirty queue, runs only in Cloud mode.
Shared client code that applies conversation deltas and tombstones to a local store.
Creates, lists, refreshes and revokes shares; verifies the snapshot matches the stored chat.
Turns a link (chat, run, research, schedule, file, artifact) into a ready address or a not-found, deleted, expired or unauthorized state.

data_kept.what: Chats: title, model, project, pinned, starred, archived, temporary flag, active leaf message, draft, draft time, version, deleted time, instructions
data_kept.where: Postgres table public.web_conversations (apps/web/db/neon/0001_mvp_chat.sql:3; 0059; 0078; 0038; 0219)

data_kept.what: Messages: role, content, model, provider, tokens, metadata, parent id, deleted time
data_kept.where: Postgres table public.web_messages (apps/web/db/neon/0001_mvp_chat.sql:15; apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:37)

data_kept.what: Artifact versions
data_kept.where: Postgres table web_artifact_versions, written by the sync push (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:366-374)

data_kept.what: Branch links: forked chat and mapping of copied messages
data_kept.where: Postgres tables conversation_branches and conversation_branch_messages (apps/web/db/neon/0078_conversation_branching_runtime.sql:20-30)

data_kept.what: Generation attempt record: conversation id, outcome, error class
data_kept.where: Postgres table public.managed_usage_requests (apps/web/db/neon/0329_managed_usage_attempt_record.sql:24-33)

data_kept.what: Run event journal: envelopes for each run
data_kept.where: Postgres tables cloud_agent_runs and cloud_agent_events (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1118-1125)

data_kept.what: Shared chat snapshots, personal and workspace
data_kept.where: Postgres tables shared_sessions and organization_shared_sessions (apps/web/db/neon/0051_shared_sessions.sql:1; apps/web/db/neon/0186_organization_shared_sessions.sql:86)

data_kept.what: Imported memory items (from the memory import route)
data_kept.where: Postgres table user_memories (apps/web/lib/memory/import-store.ts:63)

data_kept.what: Phone: sync cursor, last sync time, queue of changed chats and messages
data_kept.where: Phone storage (MMKV) under the key cloud-sync-state (apps/mobile/stores/chat/cloudSyncStateStore.ts:88-96)

data_kept.what: Browser: unsent composer text on the unsaved surface, per the migration comment
data_kept.where: Browser sessionStorage and a zustand map (apps/web/db/neon/0219_conversation_drafts.sql:5-8; the code path was not opened)

data_kept.what: Notification feed items and push device tokens
data_kept.where: Recorded through recordNotification and read from the push token store (apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:153; apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts:113)

switches.name: Cloud chat feature flag (mobile)
switches.effect: When false, the phone never runs the managed sync and hides cloud chat screens.

switches.name: App mode is Cloud
switches.effect: Mobile sync runs only when the app is in Cloud mode and an account is signed in.

switches.name: Workspace policy for chat sync, per surface
switches.effect: An administrator can turn cloud sync off for one surface; the server refuses sync with an organization policy error.

switches.name: Free daily allowance
switches.effect: Free users are limited on new chats and message writes per day; a spent allowance refuses the write.

switches.name: Sync protocol version
switches.effect: Sets the version this server speaks (2) and the oldest one it still accepts (2). Pushes from older clients get 426; newer ones get a validation error.

switches.name: Pull page sizes
switches.effect: Caps how many chats, messages and artifacts one pull returns.

switches.name: Mobile sync interval
switches.effect: The phone syncs every 30 seconds while active, and on return to the foreground.

switches.name: Stream keep-alive interval
switches.effect: How often a keep-alive line is sent on a quiet stream (2 seconds, checked at most every 5 seconds).

switches.name: Share link lifetime
switches.effect: Sets how many days a share link lasts.

switches.name: Notification preference for phone pushes
switches.effect: The phone's own switch decides whether phone pushes are sent for run events. The browser has its own switch.

switches.name: Push transports
switches.effect: Chooses which push transports a message is sent through (phone, browser). Both are on by default.

switches.name: Temporary chat
switches.effect: A temporary chat is not stored as a draft, is not synced on mobile, cannot be shared, and resolves to not found in links.

guide.shared_code: Shared between apps: the sync wire schemas, protocol version and refusal messages (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/sync.ts); the stream envelope schema and parser (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/agent-events.ts, used by the web, desktop, VS Code and browser-extension clients); the conversation delta apply and tombstone code (packages/client/sync/src/conversations.ts); product link format and parser (packages/contracts/types/src/product-links.ts); memory import parser (packages/contracts/types/src/memory-import.ts). Separate per app: the phone sync engine and its storage (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts, apps/mobile/stores/chat/cloudSyncStateStore.ts); the CLI sync state and handshake (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs, apps/cli/src/cloud/handshake.rs); the browser composer draft and stream hook (apps/web/features/chat/services/conversation-draft.ts, apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts); the browser-extension conversation sync (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts). All server routes live only in apps/web.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The draft migration header says it is NOT YET APPLIED and waits for approval. The brief and the audit register say it is applied. One of the two is stale; the header should be corrected once the state is confirmed.

Brief item S90.22 says chat history from another product can be imported as conversations. The import route only parses text into memory items and writes them to user_memories. No code I opened creates a conversation.
Brief item S90.23 says the server refuses too-old or too-new clients. Only the push route checks the protocol version. The pull route does not call the check.
The first page of the conversation list is read by offset, not by the keyset cursor. Only later pages use the keyset cursor. The brief says keyset paging.
The unauthorized state of a deep link reveals whether an id exists for another account, because it checks the table without the owner's scope.
Brief item S90.15 describes a sequence cursor over the event journal. The resume route reads the saved message text and cuts it by character count; it does not read the journal.

not_sure: I did not run anything. This is a reading of the code only; no tests, builds or servers were run, and no localhost checks were done.
Whether the web, desktop and CLI apps run the sync loop; I traced only the phone sync engine, the CLI pull and push functions, and the extension scope.
Whether desktop Local and own-key chats are ever synced to the server. The sync code I read works only on saved chats, and I did not follow the desktop code to see which chats it saves.
Whether the search, export, share, deep link and notification features appear in the mobile, desktop, CLI or extension apps.
The exact screen text for empty, waiting and failure states. I did not open any screen component except where named above.
Whether migration 0219 is applied on the production database. The file says it is not, the audit register says it is.
How the sidebar sorts pinned chats within the same page, and how the keyset sort key is built (conversations/route.ts:124 uses a '1' or '0' prefix; I did not read the helper that builds the rest).
Which generation attempt rows are written for each provider path. I confirmed the finalization calls but did not walk every caller of the reserve function.
The brief's line numbers for some items (for example S90.03 at messages/route.ts:71) point to query code that is not the version store itself; I used the code I opened instead.
Whether the web push transport delivers to every browser that registered. I saw the send path (push-notification-service.ts:362-369) but not the browser subscription code.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the server side that turns a chat, agent or coding request into a call to one AI model. It picks the model and the route to it, sends the request in each provider's own format, handles slow, failed or overloaded calls, and records what happened. A person gets answers from the right model without knowing which provider served them, and the account is charged for usage that is measured here.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user who sends a chat or agent turn reaches this code, on whatever plan they have. Some parts apply only to some plans: model access is checked against the plan tier, and free-tier turns take a separate path. Operators see cache, cost and rollout numbers in admin views. Developers change the catalog, adapters and routing. The brief does not say which parts are limited to paid plans beyond those checks.

features.name: Model catalog, providers and lifecycle
features.use: One list of models, providers, routes and capabilities that every surface and the server read. It also records whether a model is new, old, being retired, and what replaces it.
how_people_use_it: A person does not touch this directly.
They see the models the catalog allows in the model picker, and a retired model is replaced by its successor under the catalog rules.
A developer edits the curated catalog file, then runs the sync command to regenerate the shared catalog.
how_it_should_work: Every model ID comes from the generated catalog; no surface keeps its own copy.
Aliases resolve to one canonical model ID.
Lifecycle stage, deprecation and replacement are enforced by routing, not only shown in text.
Plan limits come from the same catalog (access checks use the plan tier).
features.on_each_app: The brief gives one status for each item (done) and no per-app status. The catalog is shared code read by every surface (see shared_code).

features.name: Automatic and chosen model routing
features.use: Turns Auto or a named model into one model and one route. It also classifies the task so Auto can pick a suitable model.
how_people_use_it: Leave the model on Auto and send a message; the server picks the model.
Or choose a model in the picker; the server must use that model, not a different one.
For cloud coding sessions, the chosen model is shown and sent with each agent turn.
how_it_should_work: An explicitly chosen model is never silently replaced (S91.23 Should). A model that cannot do the job must be refused with a clear message, not swapped.
Auto picks from models the plan allows and that are not over the price limit for the request.
If the plan does not include the model, the server returns a 'not available on your plan' error with the needed plan name.
Empty or unknown model names are rejected with a validation error.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status. The web Cloud Code page and mobile Cloud Code session screen both choose the agent model in the client. The VS Code extension's continue-in-cloud action also resolves it. The client code in each case is the place where the chosen model is replaced (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Provider calls and request translation
features.use: Sends one request to the chosen provider in that provider's own format. Covers the coordinator, a common adapter interface, credentials, message and attachment format, tool schemas and structured output.
how_people_use_it: A person sends a message, optionally with an image or document attached, or asks for a tool to run.
The person does not choose the wire format; the server translates it.
how_it_should_work: Each provider has one adapter built by a factory; the coordinator never talks to a provider directly.
The server picks the provider key from the deployment's environment; a key that a turn already reserved for free-trial spend is used in its place.
Provider base URLs from the environment are checked against an allow-list; a bad one is ignored with a warning.
Images and documents are converted into each provider's format; tool schemas are made strict where the provider needs it.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status. Calls are made only on the server, so every app uses the same path through the chat endpoint.

features.name: Streaming, cancellation and time limits
features.use: Turns each provider's stream into one chunk format. Stops the provider call when the person cancels, and stops calls that wait too long.
how_people_use_it: A person watches the answer appear word by word.
They press stop; the provider call ends.
If the model is silent too long, the answer shows a time-out instead of waiting forever.
how_it_should_work: The first chunk is checked before streaming starts; an error in it is mapped to a normal error and sent back.
A stream that goes quiet for 90 seconds is stopped; a warning is raised at half that time.
The first token must arrive within a per-call deadline that is bounded by the turn's remaining budget.
Client cancellation reaches the provider call through the request signal.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status. Each app shows the stream it receives from the same endpoint.

features.name: Retries, fallback and provider errors
features.use: When a call fails, it is classified, retried if safe, or moved to another model or route. Route health is recorded so bad routes are avoided next time.
how_people_use_it: Usually invisible. A person may see a slightly longer wait, or a message that the answer came from a backup model.
Failed or refused turns are refunded in usage.
how_it_should_work: Errors are classified by category; only some categories are retried or fall back.
Retries use backoff up to a 32 second cap; up to 10 retries, with at most 3 for overload.
Fallback tries at most 4 routes in a plan, same-model alternatives first, then a different model.
Outcomes of each route are recorded so health can feed back into routing.
Failed or refused turns release their usage reservation.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status. Fallback is a server decision, so every app behaves the same.

features.name: Context fitting and token counting
features.use: Estimates tokens before sending and trims or compacts old content to fit the model's context window.
how_people_use_it: A long chat keeps working; old turns may be shortened behind the scenes.
A very long single message may be refused rather than cut.
how_it_should_work: Policy and format system messages are never cut; the latest user message is never cut.
If the content still does not fit, the overflow is reported instead of silently sent.
Dense scripts (for example CJK) are counted at about one token per character, not the usual Latin estimate.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status.

features.name: Usage, cost and telemetry
features.use: Reads input, output, cache and reasoning token counts from each provider response, and records spans, cost, route, latency and outcome for each call.
how_people_use_it: A person sees usage in their account or plan meters (not read in this brief).
Operators see the numbers in admin views.
how_it_should_work: Every call produces usage numbers; a call that fails must still record its outcome.
Telemetry names the model, route, provider and error code.
Managed usage is marked as started before the provider call so a crash cannot double-bill.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status.

features.name: Prompt versions and prompt caching
features.use: Keeps prompts in a versioned registry and reuses cached prompt parts where the route supports it. Shows cache hit rates to operators.
how_people_use_it: A person does not see this directly; faster and cheaper repeat turns are the visible result.
Operators read cache numbers per route, model and tenant in the costs panel.
how_it_should_work: A prompt is resolved by id and version; a staged rollout can select a newer version for a share of requests.
Caching is off for private (temporary) turns; the temporary chat flag stops saving.
Cache hits and cache tokens are reported per route.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status.

features.name: Model evaluation and rollout gate
features.use: Scores models and cohorts from recent results and raises alerts for cost or quality problems before a rollout widens.
how_people_use_it: People do not use this. Operators read the alerts and benchmark records.
A scheduled job runs it on a fixed window.
how_it_should_work: The scheduled job must pass the cron authorisation check or it is refused with 401.
Each window writes benchmark rows per model, cohort and slot.
Alerts are sent once per claim key; if the claim store is down, the alert is sent anyway.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives no per-app status. It is server-only.

features.name: Batch and deferred inference
features.use: Intended to submit and track batch or deferred model jobs.
how_people_use_it: Not available. No screen or endpoint for it was found.
how_it_should_work: Per the brief, status is missing; nothing is built to satisfy the Should.
features.on_each_app: Missing on all apps; the brief status is 'platform missing'.

how_it_works.step: Request enters the chat endpoint and takes a slot
how_it_works.detail: The chat endpoint admits the turn through a concurrency slot, then runs the turn body. The slot is released on every exit path.
The agent route checks managed compute access and then whether the model is on the plan. Cloud Code agent turns pick their model with the agent-model resolver.
Connector and capability switches are read per turn. Operator kill switches and the account's policy decide what the product overview lists as on or off.

how_it_works.step: Usage reservation marked before the provider call
how_it_works.detail: Managed usage is marked as started before any provider or tool call. If marking fails, the reservation is refunded and the turn stops.

A factory builds the adapter for the chosen provider, with cache settings for that provider. A free-trial promotion can supply its own credential. Server keys come from environment variables; base URLs are checked against an allow-list.

how_it_works.step: Stream started and first chunk checked
how_it_works.detail: The first chunk is read before streaming to the person. An error there is mapped and thrown; metadata such as request ID and model is put on the span.
The stream is wrapped in an idle watchdog that stops after 90 seconds of silence. The first token must arrive before a deadline set from the turn's time left.

how_it_works.step: Failure: retry, fallback or give up, then record outcome
how_it_works.detail: Retries use exponential backoff from 500 ms to 32 s. A fallback re-targets the same messages to another model; the auto-router builds up to 4 fallback routes. Outcomes are recorded for route health. Failed usage is refunded.
Before a request goes out, content is measured and trimmed. Policy system messages and the latest user message are protected from cutting.

how_it_works.step: Benchmarks and alerts on a schedule
how_it_works.detail: A scheduled job reads cohort metrics for a time window, writes benchmark rows, detects cost and quality alerts, and de-duplicates alerts through a key-value store.

key_files.role: Chat endpoint: admits turns through a concurrency slot, runs the turn body, marks usage before the provider call, records route outcomes.
Builds the provider adapter per provider, sets prompt-cache settings, checks the first stream chunk and maps errors.
Resolves server-side provider keys and base URLs from environment values and builds the adapter.
Auto routing: builds the fallback plan (max 4 routes) and checks price and eligibility.
Re-targets a turn to a fallback model and builds the failover attempt view.
Retry loop with backoff, overload limit and fallback decision.
Stream idle watchdog (90 s default, warning at half).
Chooses the model for cloud coding agent turns; this is where a selected model can be replaced.
Context budget: protects policy and latest user messages from trimming, reports overflow.
Writes rollout benchmark rows and raises cost and quality alerts with de-duplication.

data_kept.where: Database table public.model_rollout_benchmarks (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:226-236)

data_kept.where: Key-value store via getKeyValueStore (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:60-70)

data_kept.what: Routing decision traces, purged after expiry
data_kept.where: Purged by purgeExpiredRoutingTraces called from apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts (store not read)

data_kept.where: Managed usage billing store, written through markManagedUsageProviderStarted (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:529-534); store not read

data_kept.what: Provider keys and base URLs
data_kept.where: Deployment environment variables read through getOptionalEnv (apps/web/lib/services/provider-adapter-service.ts:117-131); not stored by this code
