data_kept.where: In code: apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-registry.ts (resolvePrompt)

switches.name: Plan model access
switches.effect: A model not in the plan is refused with model_not_available; agent turns check the same rule.

switches.name: Managed compute access gate
switches.effect: Blocks cloud turns for accounts that lack access, before any model call.

switches.name: Operator kill switch
switches.effect: Turns off product capabilities per flag subject; unreadable state lists capabilities as shipped.

switches.name: Temporary chat flag
switches.effect: A temporary chat is not saved and does not reach prompt caching.

switches.name: Provider key and base URL environment values
switches.effect: Choose which key a provider call uses and where it goes; a bad base URL is ignored.

switches.name: Prompt canary traffic fraction
switches.effect: Share of requests that get a staged prompt version.

switches.name: Rollout evaluation window
switches.effect: Time window used by the scheduled evaluation.

switches.name: Cron authorisation
switches.effect: Only authorised scheduled calls run the rollout evaluation; others get 401.

switches.name: Cloud Code agent routing slot
switches.effect: Fixed routing slot used to pick the coding model for agent turns.

switches.name: Stream idle timeout
switches.effect: Stream stops after this many ms of silence (default 90 000).

switches.name: Retry limits
switches.effect: Maximum retries, overload retries, base delay and backoff cap.

switches.name: Fallback limits
switches.effect: Maximum fallback routes (4) and same-model fallbacks before a model is substituted (2).

switches.name: Anthropic-style prompt cache config
switches.effect: Turns prompt caching on or off and sets its retention for one provider.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the model catalog and contract types (packages/contracts/types/src, including cloud-code-agent-model.ts, which the web, mobile and VS Code code all import); routing (packages/ai/routing); provider runtime (packages/ai/provider-runtime: retry, watchdog); provider protocol (packages/ai/provider-protocol). The server chat endpoint under apps/web/app/api/llm is the one place provider calls are made, so every app reaches inference through it. Separate per app: the UI that chooses and sends the model (web Cloud Code page apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx, mobile apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx, VS Code apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/continueInCloud.ts). The brief lists server items only.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Selected model is silently replaced for Cloud Code agent turns, which the brief's S91.23 says must never happen. The resolver returns a different model when the selected one has no tool support, and the web page sends that resolved model to the agent endpoint.
Mobile Cloud Code session screen uses the same resolver, so the same replacement happens there.
Resolver's final fallback returns the plan's default chat model without checking that it can run agents. The candidate list is filtered for tool support, but the fallback is not.

Batch and deferred inference coordinator is missing (S91.30). A search of the chat endpoint, routing and provider code found no such coordinator; the batch-named code that exists is for other features.
things_that_look_wrong.where: apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions (no coordinator found); apps/web/lib/services/free-lane/runtime-state-service.ts:360 and apps/web/app/api/cron/sweep-chat-file-intakes/route.ts:43 are unrelated batch code

not_sure: Local and own-key paths: the brief covers Cloud only; I did not establish how Local or own-key turns reach these modules.
Client model picker code (how Auto and explicit choices are stored and shown): not read.

Catalog files named in the brief (model-catalog.ts lines 89, 124, 130, 1340, 1367, 1394, 1594, 1632; compile.mjs; lifecycle-stages.mjs) were not opened, so the statements about the catalog are from the brief, not from the code I read.
Retry-After ceiling and per-model same-route retry budget (S91.26): I saw the retry constants and loop but not the Retry-After handling.
Route health store (packages/ai/routing/src/route-health-store.ts) and how its data feeds routing: not read.
Telemetry Should (spans, usage, cost, route, latency, outcome) was checked only by the brief's paths; I did not open span.ts, cpst-telemetry.ts or the routing trace service.
Cache diagnostics panel (OperatorCostsPanel.tsx) and its data: not read.
Whether the user sees a notice when a model is replaced in the cloud agent flow (CloudCodePage.tsx around line 2818): not established.
Where the usage numbers reach a person's plan meter: outside this brief.
Temporary-chat behaviour beyond the flag at request-processor.ts:2340: not traced.
No builds, tests, servers or installs were run; this is code reading only, so no localhost or single-surface testing was done.

guide.what_it_is_for: When the assistant needs outside help, it asks for a tool: search the web, read a file, act on a connected account, or run code. This area is the machinery that decides which tools the model may see, checks each request, asks the person first when the action is risky, runs the tool, keeps a record, and stops cleanly when a run is cancelled, paused or out of budget. It matters because a wrong tool call can send a message, change data or leak private content, so every call passes through the same checks.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person who uses hosted chat with tools turned on (the tool list depends on their tool access mode and connected accounts). Scheduled runs use the same gate but run unattended. Workspace admins affect it only through an organization policy that can block autonomous approvals (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts). Developers use the Rust agent engine and local named agents in the CLI. Plan-based limits were not established from the code I read.

features.name: Tool list, risk labels and tool search
features.use: Declares each tool and its risk properties, and offers the model only the tools that fit the current turn. Less relevant tools stay hidden behind a tool directory that the model can query.
how_people_use_it: The person does not pick tools directly; they type a request and the model decides.
Connected accounts with many tools are trimmed to the most relevant ones for each turn.
The model can ask for the hidden tools by name or keyword and they are added to the next step.
how_it_should_work: Every platform tool has one declared entry: action class (read, write, delete, execute, external_send), reversible, untrusted content, and egress path.
Tools that are not declared are treated as the riskiest kind (an irreversible write that can leave the trust boundary), so they ask first.
Deferred tool schemas load on demand into the next step only.
Empty state: no connector tools means only the built-in tools are offered.
Failure: an unknown tool name is refused with a message, not run.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives only a platform status (done). The registry and loop are in the web server code, which the hosted chat route uses. Desktop, mobile, extension and CLI behaviour was not established from the files I read.

features.name: Checking tool arguments and reading tool calls
features.use: Turns the raw tool call from any model stream into one internal shape (id, name, arguments), then checks the arguments against the tool's declared schema before anything runs.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to do by the person. A bad call shows up as a tool error in the activity list.
how_it_should_work: Every call is parsed into id, qualified name and arguments.
Arguments are checked against the declared schema before execution; an invalid call is refused with a reason that goes back to the model.
Arguments that are not valid JSON still run on the raw text, but are flagged as malformed so the system can count it.
Argument text is capped at 256 KB per call.
features.on_each_app: Web server path only in the files read. Other apps not established.

features.name: Running tools in a turn
features.use: Runs the model, then its tool calls, then the model again, until the answer is done or a limit is hit. Read-only calls can run side by side; anything that changes state runs one at a time. Cancelling stops the stream and the tools in flight.
how_people_use_it: Send a message in chat; the answer shows each tool step as it runs.
Press stop (or cancel the run) to end the turn.
Approve or reject calls that need it (see approvals feature).
how_it_should_work: The loop repeats until the model is finished or the step limit is reached. At the limit the run pauses with a checkpoint and continues only if a resume raises the limit.
Up to 4 read-only calls run at once in the main loop; the research loop allows 3.
Any call that is not declared read-only, and every undeclared connector tool, runs one at a time.
Each result is capped in size and wrapped as untrusted data; a tool error is wrapped too and marked as an error.
Cancel: the model stream and in-flight tools are stopped and the turn is settled as cancelled.
A turn is treated as empty, blocked, cancelled or cut off by one shared set of checks.
Dependency-aware ordering: not applicable (no code found).
Empty state: a turn with no text and no tool output counts as an empty turn.
Failure: a timed-out tool returns a timeout message to the model; an empty provider step can trigger a failover to another route.
features.on_each_app: The brief gives platform status only. The Rust agent engine in the CLI has its own turn loop and cancellation; mobile, desktop, extension and VS Code behaviour was not established.

features.name: Large tool results
features.use: When a tool returns more than the model should read at once, the full result is stored once under a short reference id, and the model reads it in pages through a reader tool.
how_people_use_it: The model fetches a stored result by id when it needs more; the person sees a notice that the result was shortened.
how_it_should_work: Stored results expire after 24 hours.
Results are read in pages of about 40,000 characters; at most 10 results are listed.
Secret-looking content is checked by a policy before storage.
Empty state: no stored results means the reader tool is not offered.
Failure: a missing reference is reported as not found.
features.on_each_app: Web server path. Other apps not established.

features.name: Approvals and pauses
features.use: Decides for each tool call whether to run it, ask the person, or refuse it. A risky call pauses the run and waits for an answer, which can come from another device.
how_people_use_it: In chat, a tool card shows approve and reject buttons for each waiting call.
Approve or reject each call; the run then continues.
Saved per-tool levels (allow, ask, deny) are set in connector permissions; the account policy sets the default.
how_it_should_work: Rules are checked in a fixed order: a saved deny always wins; a saved allow is used unless the lethal-trifecta rule applies (untrusted content, a reachable private source and an outbound path together); the account policy then decides allow or ask.
Unattended runs (scheduled) turn an escalation into a refusal unless the run is set to pause.
Pending requests are stored with the exact calls and messages, so a decision on another device can resume the run.
A decision applies only to the calls it was made for; stale or mismatched decisions are refused.
Each decision is recorded per call, and the checkpoint is claimed under a short lease.
Failure: a checkpoint that does not match the event history is refused.
features.on_each_app: Chat UI wiring is in the shared chat components (MessageBubble and the stream hook). Other apps' approval UIs were not checked.

features.name: Receipts, retries and outcome checks
features.use: Leaves a record of each tool action, stops a risky call from running twice when a step is retried, and for some external writes, checks the outside system to learn whether the write actually landed.
how_people_use_it: The person reads activity records (connector call log is exposed by the connectors calls endpoint).
how_it_should_work: Platform tool actions are written to the audit log (success, failure or denied).
Connector calls are written to a call-event table with outcome and duration; the write is not awaited and cannot fail the call, so a log row can be lost without an error.
Calls that are not safe to retry are remembered under a key for 15 minutes by default, so a retry does not run them again.
For GitHub comment and review writes, if the outcome is unknown, the system checks GitHub and records whether the write landed.
Failure: if the outcome cannot be checked, the message says so.
Empty state: no connector calls means an empty call list.
features.on_each_app: Web server path. The reconciliation covers GitHub writes only in the code I read.

features.name: Durable runs and recovery
features.use: Stores each agent run, its plan steps, its checkpoints and its tool results, so a run survives a dropped connection and a crash can be settled rather than left hanging.
how_people_use_it: Start a longer task in the agent mode; close the tab and come back later (the run continues on the server).
how_it_should_work: Runs are stored with state, events and a lease.
Plans and steps are stored and updated as the run goes.
A checkpoint holds messages, pending calls and the request; a run can resume from it.
A reaper sweep settles runs whose invocation has ended, so they do not hang forever.
Failure: an orphaned run is marked abandoned with a reason.
features.on_each_app: Platform server. Client reconnection on each app not established.

features.name: Budgets and loop limits
features.use: Stops a run that spends too much, uses too many tool calls, runs too long, or repeats the same call again and again.
how_people_use_it: The person sees a message that the run was stopped and why.
how_it_should_work: Defaults per run: spend 20 dollars (in micro-dollars), 500 tool calls, 6 hours wall clock.
The same call made 5 times in a row stops the run.
The spend check happens before each provider operation; the code does not reserve the amount up front.
Each refusal is recorded with its code.
Failure: a refused operation returns a stop message and the run ends.
features.on_each_app: Platform server only.

features.name: Scheduled unattended runs
features.use: Runs scheduled agent tasks on time without a person present.
how_people_use_it: Create a schedule with the create-schedule tool, or in the app's schedule screen (screen not checked).
how_it_should_work: A cron endpoint with a secret check claims due runs in waves of 10 and stops at a sweep budget of 55 seconds.
Tools run only if the unattended gate allows them; anything that would need asking is refused.
Low-power cron skip can pause the sweep.
features.on_each_app: Platform server only.

features.name: Agent definitions and subagents
features.use: Named agents are instruction files a developer keeps in a project or user folder and runs from the CLI. Hosted agent definitions and subagents are not built.
how_people_use_it: In the CLI, type /agents to list agents, or /agents create <name> to create one.
how_it_should_work: Project agents override global agents with the same name.
The hosted execute endpoint answers that the feature is retired.
Subagents: not applicable (no coordinator found).
features.on_each_app: CLI only for definitions. Hosted platform has no store (partial).

how_it_works.detail: The provider stream is read and each tool call is turned into one shape (id, name, arguments). Arguments over 256 KB are capped.
Only the schemas that match the turn are sent; the rest are listed in a directory tool. When the model asks for a deferred tool, its schema is added for the next step.
Arguments are checked against the declared schema. A problem produces a refusal message that goes back to the model.

The gate walks a fixed rank table: saved deny, device step, lethal-trifecta escalation, saved allow, saved ask, account default read-only, manual mode ask, trifecta, then allow. Unattended escalations become a deny.

how_it_works.step: Pause for a person when needed
how_it_works.detail: The pending calls and the messages are saved as a server checkpoint before the approval request is shown. The run then waits. The checkpoint table holds state pending, resuming, resolved or failed.

A decision from chat or another device is sent to the approve or resume routes. The server checks that it matches the stored calls, claims the checkpoint, and runs only the approved calls with their stored arguments.

Approved calls go to the dispatcher, which routes by category (search, fetch, sandbox, office, skills, connectors, device steps, caller-owned). Retry-unsafe calls go through the idempotency guard. Read-only batches run up to 4 at once.
Errors are wrapped as untrusted content and capped at 4,000 characters. Each platform action is written to the audit log; connector calls are logged to the call-event table without blocking the call.

how_it_works.step: Store big results and trim history
how_it_works.detail: Large results are stored under a reference in the key-value store for 24 hours. The history sent to the model is trimmed to about 200,000 characters, keeping the most recent results.
The loop runs while steps are below the limit (10 for chat, 100 for agent mode, 20 for caller-owned runs by default). At the limit it pauses. Cancel stops the stream and in-flight tools.
Runs, plans, budgets and checkpoints are stored in the database. Budget checks run before each provider operation. A cron reaper settles runs whose invocation ended.

key_files.role: The main loop (runToolLoop at line 3833): streams, runs tools, pauses for approval, resumes, and enforces limits. About 8,000 lines; most behaviour lives here.
The web tool registry: declared risk properties per platform tool and per connector tool, plus parallel-safety and retry-safety lookups.
The approval rank table and resolveToolCallGate, which return allow, ask or deny for one call.
Loads the person's approval policy from user settings, and the organization check that can block autonomous approvals.
Chooses which tool schemas to send each turn and expands deferred ones on request.
Remembers retry-unsafe calls under a key so a retried step does not run them twice.
Stores large tool results under a reference for 24 hours and serves them in pages.
The deep-research loop: its own plan, search, gate and completion checks, using the same gate.
Stores run state, approval decisions and checkpoint resume; matches decisions to the exact pending calls.
Per-run budget defaults and the checks for spend, tool calls, time and repeated calls.
Settles runs whose worker stopped, so they do not hang.
Decides whether a scheduled run may run a tool without asking.
Connector tool execution, including the GitHub write reconciliation that checks the outcome after an unknown result.
The Rust turn engine used by the CLI (run_turn and cancellation).

switches.name: Per-person tool approval policy (ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous)
switches.effect: Sets the default allow or ask for read-only and other calls. Default is ask_every_time; the cloud account default is autonomous.

switches.name: Organization permits autonomous approvals
switches.effect: If any governing organization forbids it, an autonomous setting falls back to ask every time.

switches.name: Approval mode of the loop
switches.effect: manual (default) pauses for approval; auto runs calls without asking.

switches.name: Saved per-tool level (allow, ask, deny)
switches.effect: Overrides the account default for that tool; deny always wins.

switches.name: Step limit per turn
switches.effect: 10 for chat, 100 for agent mode, 20 for caller-owned runs; the caller can set its own value.

switches.name: Time limit for a loop
switches.effect: Maximum duration of a tool loop; the constant CHAT_TOOL_LOOP_BUDGET_MS is used but its value was not located.

switches.name: Parallel tool cap in the main loop
switches.effect: Up to 4 read-only calls at once.

switches.name: Parallel tool cap in research
switches.effect: Up to 3 at once by default.

switches.name: Research limits
switches.effect: Iterations 6, searches 12, time 4 minutes by default; set through environment reads.

switches.name: Idempotency window
switches.effect: How long a retry-unsafe call is remembered (default 15 minutes, minimum 1 second).

switches.name: Run budget defaults
switches.effect: Spend 20 dollars, 500 tool calls, 6 hours; repeat threshold 5 identical calls.

switches.name: Time-to-first-token targets
switches.effect: Targets for the provider first-token timing (2.5 s target, 5 s breach by default).

switches.name: Cron authentication and low-power skip
switches.effect: Cron sweeps reject requests without the secret, and can skip work when low-power mode is set.

switches.name: Connector health gate
switches.effect: A connector with a streak of failures is held back for a while.

switches.name: Code-execution availability
switches.effect: Turns sandboxed code execution on or off for a turn.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the tool metadata and gate logic are web server code in apps/web and are imported by the connector permissions route, the unattended gate and the voice tool runner (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tool-runner.ts:394). Argument validation comes from the shared package packages/ai/provider-protocol. Approval policy types come from packages/contracts/types. Tool protocol types are generated from the Rust crate crates/agiworkforce-protocol into packages/contracts/types/src/generated/protocol. Separate per app: the CLI turn engine is Rust (crates/agiworkforce-agent-core, with runaway.rs mirrored in cloud-agent-budget.ts). The hosted loop is TypeScript. Desktop, mobile, extension and VS Code code was not checked for their own tool loops.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Brief item S92.13 cites research-loop.ts:1605 for the approval evaluator. That line is in a plan-step parser. The gate call is at research-loop.ts:2191 (gateResearchCall).
Brief item S92.04 cites tool-argument-validation.ts:76, but that file has 3 lines and only re-exports the validator from the shared package (line 74 there).

Brief item S92.19 cites lib/github-app.ts:865, which is a branch-list fetch, not reconciliation. The reconciliation is writeWithReconciledOutcome, and it covers GitHub comment and review writes only in the code read.
Brief item S92.28 says each run's budget is reserved up front. The code checks spend before each provider operation; I found no reservation in the budget service or migration 0258.
Brief item S92.21 says CLI agents live in .agi/agents. The code reads .agiworkforce/agents and .claude/agents.

Two retry-safety vocabularies. The idempotency guard uses a name list (safe or unsafe) while the tool registry uses idempotent, at_most_once or unknown. The guard does not read the registry, so the two can disagree.
Brief item S92.01 says one registry declares every tool. The Rust protocol file in the brief carries auth shape only in what I read; the risk fields exist only in the web TypeScript registry.

Brief item S92.17 cites tool-loop.ts:2586 as a receipt. That line writes generated office-file metadata. The audit write is recordToolCallAudit at tool-loop.ts:3514. Connector receipts are a separate table written without awaiting, so a receipt can be lost without an error.

Brief item S92.07 cites tool-loop.ts:2099 as a normaliser. That line is inside collectProviderStream. The error normaliser is toolErrorContent at tool-loop.ts:2230. Brief item S92.07 also cites e2b execution-tools.ts:261, which is a routing function; the output cap is capOutput at line 286.

Brief item S92.15 and S92.16 cite tool-loop.ts:4492-4494 for the action-binding check. That range is the empty-provider-step retry logic. The binding check is in cloud-agent-run-service.ts around 1436-1452.
Brief item S92.13 cites tool-loop.ts:2578 for the approval evaluator. That line only passes the user id into the execution context.
Brief item S92.19 says any unknown external outcome is checked against the external system. Only GitHub writes have a check in the code I read.
Idempotency guard is applied by a name list (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:932) and only for the retry-unsafe kind, so a new tool is unsafe unless added to the list.

guide.area: Search, retrieval, and context components (brief area 93)
guide.what_it_is_for: This area decides what the assistant can see when it answers. Before each turn it picks the right context: the account's memory, the user's past chats, the files in a project, and the instructions that apply. It also runs web search, reads a web page for the user, runs a hybrid search over files and chats, and runs Deep Research, which plans, searches in rounds, and writes a cited report. Long chats are shortened into a saved summary so they still fit the model's window. Together these let the assistant answer from the user's own material and from the web, and show where each fact came from.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user in the web chat gets the per-turn context, the long-chat summaries and the web tools, subject to plan and capability gates (see switches). Deep Research is limited to the paid tiers listed in billing-catalog.ts:355. The free plan gets a fixed monthly allowance of 20 search calls (search-budget.ts:32). Temporary chats get no memory, no past-chat recall and no saved summary. Workspace admins control workspace memory through the organization policy (turn-context-service.ts:176-178, 0164 migration header). Developers and operators run the indexing sweep (apps/web/app/api/cron/index-retrieval-documents/route.ts). Temporary and archived content is meant to be excluded (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Per-turn context assembly
features.use: Chooses which sources (memory, past chats, project files, instructions) go into each turn, within a size budget, and keeps a stored record of what was included and what was left out and why.
how_people_use_it: The user does not pick sources by hand. They send a message in a chat, and the platform decides.
Turning memory off in settings, or starting a temporary chat, removes those sources from the turn.
In a project, the project's instructions and files are added automatically.
how_it_should_work: Each source class is admitted or refused before its items are read: a switched-off setting, a temporary chat, or a personal source in a shared project are refused (engine.ts:115-132).
Items are added in authority order, and when the budget is tight the lowest-priority items are dropped first (context-source.ts:132-167).
A source that fails to load is skipped and the turn continues; the failure is logged (engine.ts:134-144, turn-context-service.ts:190-195).
The manifest of included and excluded sources is written after the turn is built. If the write fails, the turn still goes on and only a warning is logged (turn-context-service.ts:198-206).
Empty state: when no source applies, the turn gets no extra context at all (turn-context-service.ts:132-142).
Limits by plan: the memory and past-chat switches are read from the policy, not from the plan name (turn-context-service.ts:124-131).
features.on_each_app: The brief gives one status for this item, 'platform done', and no per-app lines. The assembly runs on the server for the chat endpoint, so every app that calls that endpoint gets it. The code does not show any per-app difference.

features.name: Instruction order
features.use: Makes sure instructions from different layers (system, developer, project, personal, memory, untrusted content) are placed in a fixed order, so a lower layer cannot sit above a higher one.
how_people_use_it: Users do not act on this directly. They see its effect when project instructions or personal instructions change how the assistant answers.
how_it_should_work: Blocks are sorted by layer rank; blocks of one layer keep the order they were built in (instruction-precedence.ts:69-71, 105-125).
Memory and untrusted content are marked as reference only and can never be treated as commands (instruction-precedence.ts:22-26, 37-44).
A check reports any case where a lower layer is placed above a higher one (instruction-precedence.ts:109-117).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief. The layer names in the code differ from the brief (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Long-chat summaries
features.use: When a conversation is too long for the model's window, the oldest turns are replaced by a short saved summary and the turn continues. The summary is reused only while the messages it covers have not changed.
how_people_use_it: The user keeps chatting in a long thread. They do not see a control; a note marks the dropped history inside the prompt.
how_it_should_work: Summaries are created only when the conversation is saved, the chat is not temporary, and the switch is on (context-compaction.ts:434-440).
If summarizing fails, the platform falls back to a plain trim that drops old messages without a summary, and logs the failure (context-compaction.ts:469-474).
A saved summary is reused only when its digest matches the current messages. An edit or delete inside the covered span invalidates it (context-compaction.ts:335-349, 0282 migration header).
Temporary chats and turns with no conversation id get the plain trim only, with no summary (context-compaction.ts:434-437).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief. The code path is the shared chat endpoint.

features.name: Recall of past chats and project files
features.use: Finds past chats and project files that match the current question, so a new turn can use them.
how_people_use_it: The user asks about something from an earlier chat or a project file. They do not pick the source; relevant passages are pulled in automatically.
In a project, the project's own files and sibling chats are used.
how_it_should_work: Past chats: temporary and deleted chats and deleted messages are excluded (past-chat-context-service.ts:255-259, 344-348). Archived chats are not excluded in this query (see things_that_look_wrong).
Semantic recall is used when an index exists; otherwise a keyword search runs. A failed recall tells the model its recall is degraded (past-chat-context-service.ts:405-420, 371-397).

Project files: the indexed passages are used when available; otherwise passages are picked for each request. A file whose index no longer matches its text is dropped (project-knowledge-retrieval.ts:27-70; project-context-service.ts:339-347).
An archived project's files are not loaded (project-context-service.ts:208).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief.

features.name: Building the search index
features.use: Splits files and chats into chunks and turns the chunks into vectors (number lists that represent meaning) so they can be searched by meaning.
how_people_use_it: Users do not act on this. Files and chats are indexed in the background after they are saved. A project file can be re-indexed on request (requestProjectKnowledgeReindex, retrieval-index-service.ts:868).
how_it_should_work: Each document is cut into windows of text; at most 400 chunks per document (retrieval-index-service.ts:42, 417-436).
Embedding is metered: each embedding call reserves usage first. Query embeddings also check a daily allowance (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:204-250).
If embedding fails, the chunks are still stored and can be found by keyword only (retrieval-index-service.ts:508-512).
Failed documents are retried with growing delays up to 24 hours and a maximum of 5 attempts (retrieval-index-service.ts:39, 48-49, 452-455).
A background sweep reserves due documents and starts indexing workflows. It is skipped on low-power cron runs (route.ts:15-33 of the cron route).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief.

features.name: Searching your indexed content
features.use: Finds the best matching chunks from the user's own content by combining keyword matches and meaning matches, then re-ranks them.
how_people_use_it: Users do not run a search. The platform searches when a turn needs the user's own material.
how_it_should_work: Keyword search uses a full-text index; meaning search uses an approximate nearest-neighbour index (0202:131-143).
Both lists are merged with reciprocal rank scoring, then re-scored on term coverage, exact phrase, and title match (rank.ts:24-30, 49-70; retrieval-search-service.ts:521).

Only the user's own rows are returned, within the same organization. Deleted and temporary chats are excluded. Archived items are not excluded in the search query (retrieval-search-service.ts:268-271; see things_that_look_wrong).
If there is no vector index yet, or the query embedding fails, results come from keyword search only and the response says so (retrieval-search-service.ts:146-188).
If the search has no terms and no vector, it returns nothing (retrieval-search-service.ts:~ 'if (!tsQuery && !embedding.vector)').
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief.

features.name: Web search
features.use: Lets the assistant search the public web through a configured provider, and decides when a turn needs a search.
how_people_use_it: The user turns on Web search from the + menu in the web composer (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1307), or asks for a current fact, or starts Deep Research.
The assistant may also search on its own when the question needs fresh facts (required-search.ts:110-125, 218-260).
how_it_should_work: Providers are listed in web-search-providers.json. The list sets the order and names the key variable. Only providers with a matching adapter in code can run (search-provider.ts:131-143; web-search-tool.ts:388-397).
If no key is set, the tool says search is not configured on this server (web-search-tool.ts:399-402).
A retryable failure falls through to the next configured provider (web-search-tool.ts:404-408 comment; executeWebSearch at web-search-tool.ts:409).
Limits: 5 results per call, 3 calls per turn in chat, 10 per AGI Work turn (web-search-tool.ts:54-58).
Free plan: 20 search calls per 30 days (search-budget.ts:32, 66-67). Paid searches reserve and settle a charge per call (search-budget.ts:199, 404).

Results are turned into one source shape, with the provider's delivery tag so an index result is never shown as a live fetch (search-provider.ts:158-180; search-provider.ts types in packages/contracts/types/src/search-provider.ts:157-185).
Empty state: 'No results found for <query>' (web-search-tool.ts:515-516).
Failure: a plain message for the model, with the error code (web-search-tool.ts:185 webSearchFailureForModel).
features.on_each_app: The brief gives one status, 'platform done', and no per-app lines. The web composer has the toggle (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1307; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1596-1599 reads a feature flag). The mobile app has a search card and research state code (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/WebSearchToolCard.tsx; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/researchRunState.ts), which I did not trace further. The desktop build has its own search executor that does not use the provider list (see things_that_look_wrong).

features.name: Reading a web page
features.use: Fetches one public web page the user or the assistant names, and returns its readable text, title, description and date.
how_people_use_it: The user pastes a link, or asks the assistant to read a page. The assistant calls the page reader.
how_it_should_work: Only http and https are allowed. URLs with a user name or password are refused (guarded-fetch.ts:91-95).
Every hop is checked before it is made. Each redirect is checked again, and private or internal addresses are refused by the egress policy (guarded-fetch.ts:124, 138; egress-policy.ts:289-300).
Limits: 10 seconds, 1.5 MB of response, 20,000 characters of text returned, up to 5 redirects, 5 reads per chat turn and 15 per AGI Work turn (url-fetch-tool.ts:30-46).
If a page is read through a research domain policy, redirects outside the allowed sites are refused (url-fetch-tool.ts:560-570).
Empty state: 'No readable text content' (url-fetch-tool.ts:669-671).
Long pages are cut and the cut is stated in the text (url-fetch-tool.ts:673-681).
Failure: a refusal code with a message for the model (url-fetch-tool.ts:541-552).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief.

features.name: Ranking and de-duplicating sources
features.use: Removes duplicate pages, puts the most useful sources first, and labels each source as fresh, recent, stale or unknown by its publication date.
how_people_use_it: Users see the sources in the answer, in the order the platform ranks them.
how_it_should_work: Sources are identified by their canonical URL, so two providers returning the same page merge into one (search-provider types: searchCitationId, dedupeSearchSources at packages/contracts/types/src/search-provider.ts:116-120, 188-216).
When merging, the weaker delivery claim is kept, so a cached page is never shown as live (search-provider.ts types at 188-216).
Freshness: 7 days or less is fresh, 90 days or less is recent, older is stale, no date is unknown (search-provider types at 130-146).
Ranking scores each source on query terms, title, boilerplate and recency, then drops near-duplicates. Ties keep the order the provider gave (packages/ai/search/src/source-ranking.ts:333-345).
features.on_each_app: Platform only, per the brief.

features.name: Citations
features.use: Lets each cited fact point to a place in its source, and keeps the citation links stable when they are saved with the message. The grounding checker is not built.
how_people_use_it: The user sees numbered source links in the answer, and can open them. Citations to files can point to a page, heading, line, cell, slide, timestamp or message.
how_it_should_work: Citation locators are defined in packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts:10.
Numbers follow the order the sources were shown; a source the turn cannot show is not numbered (web-search-tool.ts:515-523; tool-loop.ts:2789 passes the position lookup).

When a message is saved, redirect links in its citations are resolved to the publisher's address. A failure keeps the links as they arrived and never fails the save (persist-message.ts:88; resolve-source-urls.ts:29-41).
A grounding checker that verifies claims against sources is not found in the code. The brief lists it as missing, and a search of the research loop and the libraries found none.
features.on_each_app: Platform only per the brief. The grounding checker is missing on every app.

features.name: Deep Research runs
features.use: A long research run: it plans questions, runs search and read rounds with limits, stops when coverage stops improving, then writes a cited report. Runs are saved and can be resumed after an interruption or cancelled.
how_people_use_it: The user turns on Deep Research in the + menu (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:187, 1307-1311). The run shows a plan card and progress. The user can approve, cancel, or resume a run (useChatStream.ts:310-318 carries research sources and a resume record).
The run ends with a report that has citations.
how_it_should_work: Paid tiers only. The capability check refuses Deep Research for other plans (request-processor.ts:5221; billing-catalog.ts:355).
Defaults: 6 iterations, 12 searches, a 4-minute budget, 3 parallel tool calls, 4 query rewrites. Each can be changed by an environment setting within a fixed range (research-loop.ts:1771-1840).
Stop rules: a coverage threshold, a diminishing-returns check, and the budgets above (research-loop.ts:590-655).
Cancellation is checked at each boundary, from the client abort or a durable cancel flag. A cancelled run keeps what it gathered so a retry can resume (research-loop.ts:2034-2050).

The report is saved to the research report table with its sources, status and cost. A failed save is reported and the run status says so (research-loop.ts:1820-1870 region; research-report-service.ts:212-260; research-run-options.ts:76).
Empty state and failure: a failed or interrupted run is stored with an honest message, not a stub (0094_research_reports.sql:52).
features.on_each_app: Platform only per the brief. The web app shows the plan and progress; other apps' research views were not traced.

features.name: Knowledge graph or wiki
features.use: Would turn content into a browsable graph or wiki. The brief marks it as missing.
how_people_use_it: Not available. No code path for this was found.
how_it_should_work: Nothing to check. The brief status is missing, and I did not find code for it.
features.on_each_app: Missing on every app, per the brief.

how_it_works.step: The turn starts and the context for it is built
how_it_works.detail: The chat endpoint calls resolveInteractiveTurnContext with the user, conversation, project, temporary flag, memory settings and the organization context policy. This function decides whether memory, past chats or project sources apply, and loads them.

how_it_works.step: Each source is admitted or refused, loaded, and budgeted
how_it_works.detail: The context engine checks each source class against user switches, temporary-chat rules and shared-project rules. It loads candidates, drops stale or refused items, and keeps the items that fit the budget, in precedence order. A loader that throws is logged and skipped.

how_it_works.step: Project context is loaded and its passages are picked
how_it_works.detail: For a project chat, the project's instructions, files and sibling chats are loaded. Indexed passages are looked up for the question; if none, passages are picked per request. Blocks are fitted to a character budget.

how_it_works.step: Past chats are recalled by meaning or by keyword
how_it_works.detail: If an index exists, semantic recall runs through the search provider. Otherwise a keyword query runs over messages. Temporary and deleted rows are filtered out. A failure marks the turn's recall as degraded.

how_it_works.step: The manifest is written and the instructions are ordered
how_it_works.detail: The manifest of included and excluded sources is written to the database without blocking the turn. The system instructions are then ordered by layer before they are sent.

how_it_works.step: Long conversations are summarized or trimmed
how_it_works.detail: If the messages do not fit the model window, the oldest are summarized once and the summary is cached with a digest. A summary is reused only when the digest still matches. A failure falls back to a plain trim.

how_it_works.step: The turn decides whether to offer web search
how_it_works.detail: The platform checks whether the user asked for a search, whether the question needs fresh facts, the plan and the capability gates. If yes, the search tool is added to the tools list for the model.

how_it_works.step: A search runs through the configured provider
how_it_works.detail: The search tool picks the configured providers in list order, calls the adapter, retries once on a transient failure, and turns each result into a source with the provider tag and freshness.

how_it_works.step: A page is read safely, hop by hop
how_it_works.detail: The page reader checks the domain policy, then fetches each hop after checking the scheme, the credentials and the resolved address. Redirects are followed by hand. The body is capped and turned into text, with title, description and date extracted.

how_it_works.step: Indexed content is searched and re-ranked
how_it_works.detail: The search provider builds one SQL query that joins the keyword and meaning candidates, filters by owner, organization, deletion and temporary status, then re-ranks the merged list.

how_it_works.step: Deep Research runs and saves its report
how_it_works.detail: A research turn starts a cloud run, runs the research loop (plan, search rounds, stop rules, synthesis), ranks the results, and saves the report with its sources, status and cost. Cancellation is checked at each boundary.

key_files.role: Decides which memory, past-chat and project sources a turn gets, runs the context engine, and writes the manifest.
Admits, loads, orders and budgets context candidates, and builds the manifest.
Registry of source classes with their trust, precedence (line 132) and budget priority (line 154).
Instruction layers, their rank, and which source class lands in which layer.
Summarizes long conversations once, caches the summary with a digest, and falls back to a plain trim.
The web search tool: provider selection, the one registered adapter, limits, and model-facing text.
Provider registry, provider order, and the conversion of results into one source shape.
The page reader: limits, content extraction, title, description and date.
The one fetch path for URLs the platform did not choose; checks every hop.
Hybrid keyword and meaning search over the user's indexed content, with permission filters.
Splits documents into chunks, embeds them, stores them, and retries failures.
Deep Research: plan, search rounds, stop rules, cancellation, resume and synthesis.
Source shape, canonical URL identity, freshness classes and de-duplication.
Creates the document and chunk tables, the full-text index and the vector index.

guide.area: Memory and personalization components (brief area 94, 22 items: S94.01 to S94.22)
guide.what_it_is_for: Account memory lets the assistant remember facts about the person across chats, so replies fit them without repeated setup. The person can say "remember" or "forget" in plain words, see and pin or delete what is stored, and decide what personalization may use (chats, past-chat recall, connectors, imports) and what it must never store. Background jobs expire old memories, and a few features (a recap, scheduled runs with recent chats) read from the same personal data.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in account can switch memory on or off in Settings, as the code shows (capability flags read from user settings, default off for most flags). Workspace admins can switch memory off for a whole organization (organization memory policy). Developers use the /api/llm chat endpoint, where memory is off unless the request turns it on, and the API surface never learns from or saves memory automatically (surface 'api' is excluded). No plan gate was found in the memory code itself; see not_sure.

features.name: Learn facts from chats
features.use: After an ordinary chat turn, the server pulls short personal facts out of the user's message and saves them as memories, merging duplicates and letting a newer contradicting fact replace an older one. Each saved memory records its source chat, turn and writer.
how_people_use_it: Chat normally, e.g. state a fact in a sentence that is not a question.
Nothing else to do: the memory is saved after the reply, unless the chat is temporary, the account has learning off, or the request is from the API surface.
To see where a memory came from, open it in Settings > Memory (source chat and writer are stored with it).
how_it_should_work: Only statements, not questions, and not task-only reminders ('remember this tab id' style runtime notes) become candidates; at most 5 candidates are taken per turn.
Learning is blocked for temporary chats, the API surface, when the per-chat memory override is off, when the workspace has memory off, or when the account's generate-from-history flag is off.

Duplicate wording (for example 'my favorite color is teal' vs 'the user's favorite color is teal') is matched by a normalized key and merged, not stored twice; a merge keeps the stronger expiry and pin.
A newer fact on the same topic supersedes the older one (superseded_by is set so the old one stops being read).

Empty state: no memories, so nothing is injected into replies. Waiting state: learning runs after the reply and does not block it. On failure: the turn still completes; the error is logged and learning is skipped. Limits: 1,000 characters per memory, 8,000 characters total injected per turn, 30 memories per turn, 3650 days maximum expiry.

Sensitive content (credentials, payment instrument numbers, and other prohibited categories) is refused before storage; sensitive topics are stored only when the person asked for them or the include-sensitive-topics setting is on.
features.on_each_app: Web: full (learning, commands, settings UI, retrieval). Desktop: Settings sync of the memory master and tool-assisted switches (test at apps/desktop/src/services/__tests__/managedCloudSettingsSync.test.ts:196-225); chat runs on the hosted web app. Mobile: its own local memory store and memory settings screens; cloud sync engine. CLI: syncs account memory from /api/memory/sync to a local cache and carries it only in Managed sessions. VS Code: an account memory client plus a legacy local store that is read only. Chrome extension: background bridge that lists, adds, updates and deletes memories. The brief gives only 'platform' status for these items, so per-app depth beyond web is not established.

features.name: Explicit remember and forget commands
features.use: The person types a command such as 'remember that I ...' or 'forget ...' in chat. The server stores or deletes the matching memory and the chat reports the result in a short message.
how_people_use_it: Type 'remember ...' or 'forget ...' in the chat composer and send.
For a forget that matches several memories, a confirmation dialog opens; choose Forget to confirm or cancel to keep them.
Read the receipt: 'Saved to memory.', 'Already in memory', 'Not saved: a pinned memory on the same topic takes priority', 'Deleted the matching memories.', 'No saved memory matched'.
how_it_should_work: The hook sends the message to /api/memory/commands only when the text has a remember or forget word; the command result is shown as a toast.
A forget with more than one match asks first, and the dialog says the chats stop using the memory and it cannot be restored.
A temporary chat may still forget, but it can never teach memory anything (per the code comment in memory-commands.ts).
Empty or failed state: if memory cannot be reached, the toast says it is unknown whether anything was saved or deleted; nothing is marked as saved.
Plan limits: none found in this path.
features.on_each_app: Web: the command handler is in the web chat (WebChatPage). Other apps: the server route accepts a surface value (mobile, desktop, web, chrome) and labels the source; the client hook exists only in the web app code read here. Other apps' command UIs were not read.

features.name: Manage saved memories (list, pin, delete)
features.use: Each memory has content, a category (topic), a source, a pinned flag and an expiry. The person sees the list, pins important ones so they are used first, and deletes ones they no longer want.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings > Memory to see the list (paged, 50 at a time by default).
Pin or unpin a memory (pin toggle on the item).
Delete a memory; deleted memories disappear from every read path at once.
how_it_should_work: List is ordered by pinned first, then most recently updated, and the page size is capped.
Pinned memories are preferred when there is limited room (they sort first in the read query and in the ranking).
A delete keeps a tombstone row (is_deleted = true) with the text blanked, so other devices learn of the deletion; a deleted memory is excluded from every read.
Empty state, waiting state and failure state are the settings page's own; not read in depth.
Limit: 30 memories are injected per turn at most.
features.on_each_app: Web: the list and item routes (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts and [id]/route.ts) and the settings section. Mobile has its own list and store. CLI and VS Code show cached or read-only memory. The per-app UI depth was not read.

features.name: Expiry and background upkeep
features.use: A memory can carry an expiry date. A daily job marks expired memories deleted, then merges duplicates and supersedes stale conflicting memories, so no one has to clean up by hand.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to do. An expiry is set when a memory is saved with a time limit, or by a remember command that carries one.
Expired memories stop appearing in replies at once (the read query also checks the expiry time).
how_it_should_work: The daily cron runs at 03:05 UTC and sweeps expired rows in batches of 500, with a time budget of 240 seconds and at most 200 batches per run.
If the sweep is not finished, consolidation is skipped for that run and the next run continues.
Failure: the route returns HTTP 500 and logs the error; unauthorized calls get 401.
The sweep is a soft delete (tombstone), not a row removal.
features.on_each_app: Server-side only; applies to every app's memories because the data is one account table.

features.name: Use memories in replies (retrieval, ranking, scope)
features.use: For each turn, the server loads the account's saved memories, keeps only the ones that fit the current chat, ranks them by word overlap with the request, and adds them to the model's system context.
how_people_use_it: Ask a question that touches an earlier fact; the reply uses it. Nothing to click.
In a project, the project setting decides whether global memories apply or only the project's own (uses_global_memory).
how_it_should_work: Memories with the suppressed source (auto, web, desktop, mobile) are left out; memories tied to another workspace are left out; deleted and expired ones are left out.
When the request has words, memories are ranked by relevance (words of at least 3 characters, a weighting by rarity) with pinned ones kept first; without words, the order is pinned then recent.
Scope: a loose chat uses global memories only; a project uses its own memories plus global ones unless the project is set to its own only.
Failure: if memory cannot be loaded, the turn continues without memory; the failure is logged. If memory is off at the account or workspace level, nothing is read.
Limits: 500 candidates read, 30 injected, 1,000 characters each, 8,000 total.
features.on_each_app: Web: the chat server path. Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and the extension send chats through the same server path, so the same read applies when they use a Managed (cloud) session; local or own-key sessions do not get account memory injected (the CLI notes say only a Managed session's prompt carries it).

features.name: Import and export memories
features.use: The person can export all memories as a JSON file, and import a text list of memories from another source in bulk.
how_people_use_it: Settings > Memory > Export downloads memories-<date>.json.
Settings > Memory > Import: paste or choose text, preview the items, then commit (up to a maximum per request).
A full account export also includes a memories section.
how_it_should_work: Export is capped at a maximum count; over the cap, the request fails with a message asking the person to delete some first.
Import previews items, skips duplicates already present (by import key per source and workspace), and reports blocked items instead of saving them.
Limits: MAX_IMPORT_ITEMS per commit; text over the import size limit is refused.
Failure: export read errors return a generic internal error; import validation errors return a message.
features.on_each_app: Web: the endpoints and dialogs. Account data export (apps/web/app/api/user/export/route.ts) includes the memories table in its own section. Other apps' import/export UI was not read.

features.name: Personalization source choices and never-remember rules
features.use: The person chooses which sources personalization may use (suppress automatic, web, desktop, or mobile memories), lists words that must never be remembered, and can keep temporary chats out of memory, recall, search and history.
how_people_use_it: Settings > Memory: tick 'Suppress: Automatically captured from chats' (or Saved on web / desktop / mobile).
Settings > Memory: type a term in the never-remember list (minimum 3 characters, up to 50 terms).
Start a temporary chat: it is excluded from learning, past-chat recall, search and the history save.
how_it_should_work: Suppressed sources are read on every memory load, so a suppressed source is not used in replies (the enforcement is in the read path).
A memory whose text contains a never-remember term is refused on write, with a message naming the term; if the exclusion list cannot be read, the write is refused rather than saved.
Credential and payment-instrument patterns are refused on write regardless of the list.
Temporary chats are excluded in past-chat queries (is_temporary filters), search (route filters), retrieval search, memory sync and the history save; the reflect recap also excludes them.
Failure: an unreadable exclusion list refuses the write with an error message.
features.on_each_app: Web: the settings controls (MemoryExclusions). The server rules apply to every app that writes to the account memory table. Temporary chat behaviour is server-side.

features.name: Attribution of replies to memories and past chats
features.use: A reply records which memories and past chats were used to shape it, so the product can show where an answer came from.
how_people_use_it: Read the citation list shown with a reply (the citation display itself was not read).
how_it_should_work: Memory citations are built from the memories actually injected into the turn and are stored with the assistant turn; citations are not created for memories that were not used.
If memory was off or unavailable, no memory citations are recorded.
features.on_each_app: Web and any surface that uses the same chat server path; the display side was not read.

features.name: Personal recap and scheduled-run context
features.use: A recap summarises the person's recent chat activity over a chosen range (day, week, and so on). Scheduled agent runs can draw on the project, memory, web and recent chats (last 24 hours) they are allowed to read.
how_people_use_it: Open the recap view for a range; it shows totals, active days, topics and ongoing work.
When creating a schedule, tick the sources the run may use: project, memory, web, recent chats (ScheduleAccessFields).
how_it_should_work: A recap is produced only when the memory-enabled setting is on; otherwise the result is 'memory-disabled'. Temporary chats are excluded from the recap.
Recap insights describe patterns without scoring; long lists are sampled and the recap says so.
A scheduled run's context is built only from the sources the schedule selected; 'Recent chats' is read only while Search past chats is on.
Empty state for recent chats: a fixed notice saying there were no chats in the last 24 hours.
Failure: an unavailable recent-chat read returns a fixed unavailable notice.
features.on_each_app: Recap: web and mobile (mobile has a reflect settings screen and a reflect service). Scheduled context: server-side for scheduled runs on any surface that creates a schedule.

features.name: Agent-specific memory and writing-style profile (not built)
features.use: Intended: a separate memory per agent, and a profile of the person's writing style built from their text. Neither exists in the code read.
how_people_use_it: Not available. The only writing-style control is a four-option tone picker in the composer (formal, casual, concise, detailed) stored on the device, which is not a generated profile.
how_it_should_work: Per the brief: a store separate from personal memory (S94.14) and a profile generator (S94.16). No code for either was found.
Note: persistManagedAutoMemoryFacts accepts an agentId and provenance records an agent id, but no separate store reads it.
features.on_each_app: Not present in any app read (the brief marks them missing on the platform).

how_it_works.step: 1. The person types a remember or forget command in the web chat
how_it_works.detail: The chat calls the explicit command hook after the send is accepted. The hook returns a report and posts to the commands API.

how_it_works.step: 2. The chat request reaches the server and memory is decided for the turn
how_it_works.detail: The server reads the per-chat memory override and the personalization switch, and turns memory off for the turn when either is false. It checks the organization policy and the user's own switches before reading or learning anything.

how_it_works.step: 3. Saved memories are loaded for the turn
how_it_works.detail: The turn context service loads the suppressed sources and the project scope, then runs the memory loader. The loader reads active, unexpired, undeleted rows for the user and workspace, sorts pinned first, ranks by relevance when there is a request, and keeps at most 30.

how_it_works.step: 4. Memories are added to the model's system context and cited
how_it_works.detail: The loaded memories are formatted as a system block and inserted into the context. The memory citations are kept with the turn.

how_it_works.step: 5. After the reply, candidate facts are extracted from the user's message
how_it_works.detail: Learning is allowed only when the policy has memory and history on, the chat is not temporary, the per-chat override is not off, and the surface is not the API. The sentence splitter and rules in the agent core pick up to 5 candidate facts; Google user data turns are skipped.

how_it_works.step: 6. Each write passes the eligibility gate, then duplicates and conflicts are handled
how_it_works.detail: The admission check refuses prohibited content (credentials, payment numbers), applies the never-remember list, the organization policy, the user policy and the sensitive-topic rule. Then a single SQL statement either merges a duplicate by normalized key, or inserts a row and supersedes conflicting older memories on the same topic.

how_it_works.step: 7. The row is stored with provenance
how_it_works.detail: The row stores content, category, source (web, desktop, mobile or auto), pinned flag, expiry, project, workspace, and the source conversation and turn, plus a provenance record.

how_it_works.step: 8. The person manages memories in Settings
how_it_works.detail: The settings list reads the memory route. Pin and delete call the item route, which sets the pinned flag or writes the tombstone. Source toggles and never-remember terms are saved as the 'memory' preference namespace in user settings.

how_it_works.step: 9. A daily job expires and consolidates
how_it_works.detail: The cron route checks its secret, sweeps expired rows in batches, and then merges duplicates and supersedes stale conflicts.
Import previews text, then commits items through the eligibility gate and an import-key insert that skips repeats. Export downloads the user's memories as JSON, with a cap.

key_files.role: Core of memory: policy reads, scope, load and rank, write admission, duplicate merge, supersede, expiry sweep, consolidation, provenance.
Builds the per-turn context: loads memory and past chats, applies suppressed sources and project scope, returns the prompt block and citations.
The chat server path: decides whether memory is on for a turn, injects memory, learns new facts after the reply, and records citations.
Explicit remember and forget: ports, scope, outcomes and the turn note sent back to the model.
Web client hook that sends remember or forget commands, shows receipts, and asks confirmation before a multi-match forget.
List, create and delete-all memory endpoints.
Update (pin, text, expiry), delete (tombstone) and read for one memory.
Prohibited (credential, payment) and sensitive-topic rules applied before any memory is stored.
Shared candidate-fact extraction from a message and shared relevance scoring, used by web and mobile.
Settings controls for suppressed sources and the never-remember term list.
Daily job entry point: expiry sweep then consolidation, guarded by the cron secret.
Persists candidate facts after a turn, skipping Google-user-data turns and attaching project and conversation provenance.

Their exact storage was not read in full.

switches.name: Account memory master switch (capabilities.memory)
switches.effect: Off means no memory is read or learned for the account; the policy returns disabled.

switches.name: Generate from history (capabilities.generateFromHistory)
switches.effect: Off stops automatic learning from chats; reading saved memories still works.

switches.name: Search past chats (capabilities.searchPastChats)
switches.effect: Gates past-chat recall, and the recent-chats source for scheduled runs.

switches.name: Tool-assisted generation (capabilities.allowToolAssistedGeneration)
switches.effect: Stored and shown in settings; the read of this flag in the chat path was not established.

switches.name: Include sensitive topics (capabilities.includeSensitiveTopics)
switches.effect: Lets sensitive-topic memories be stored unless the person asked for them directly.

switches.name: Organization memory policy (allowMemory)
switches.effect: Workspace off disables memory for all its members, both read and write.

switches.name: Per-chat memory override (memory_enabled) and personalization switch (personalization)
switches.effect: False skips memory reads and writes for the turn; personalization false sets memory_enabled to false.

switches.name: Temporary chat
switches.effect: Blocks learning and recall for that chat; forget is still allowed.

switches.name: Suppressed sources and never-remember terms (settings.memory)
switches.effect: Suppressed sources are not read; listed terms are refused on write.

switches.name: Project uses global memory
switches.effect: When off, a project reads only its own memories.

switches.name: Daily expiry and consolidation job
switches.effect: Runs at 03:05 UTC each day; if it is not configured or the secret is wrong it does not run (401).

switches.name: Memory sweep limits
switches.effect: Batch size 500, at most 200 batches, 240 second budget per run.

switches.name: Injection and candidate limits
switches.effect: 500 candidates read, 30 injected, 1,000 characters each, 8,000 total, 5 new candidates per turn, 3,650 days max expiry.

guide.shared_code: Shared across apps: packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts (candidate extraction, relevance scoring and key normalization, used by web and mobile); packages/contracts/context (content policy and context source classes); packages/contracts types (parseManagedMemoryCommandResponse, used by the web hook); packages/platform/context-engine (context types); packages/ui/unified-chat (writing style choice, shared by web and other surfaces). guide.what_it_is_for: This area lets a person add files to AGI Workforce (in chat, in a project, or to their library), keeps those files safe, and lets them find, reuse, restore and download them later. The model can read the text of a file, so a PDF or an office document can answer questions. Uploads go through two steps and a safety check, so a bad file is refused before it is kept.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-in users. Every upload route calls getUserScopedDb and a CSRF check first (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:60-64), so anonymous requests are refused. Storage use is limited by plan tier (apps/web/lib/server/file-storage.ts:38-73). Sharing a project with an organisation needs the content.share permission (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:264-266). Developers reach the audio transcription route through the /api/llm/v1 API (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts). Paid-only gates were not established from the code opened.

features.name: Upload a file (two steps, resumable for large files)
features.use: Sends a file to private storage and records it only after the server checks it. Large files can be sent in parts and resumed after a dropped connection.
how_people_use_it: Choose or drop a file in chat, a project, or the library (the UI gesture was not verified from code opened).
For a large file, the app sends it in parts; after an interruption it asks the server which parts are already stored and sends the rest.
how_it_should_work: Step one (presign) checks the file name, type, and size, and the checksum for a project file, then returns a place to put the bytes. Refused if object storage is not configured or the type is not supported (presign/route.ts:80-110).
Step two (complete) runs the safety checks and writes the record. No record exists before this step succeeds (chat-attachment/complete/route.ts:24-57; chat-attachment-completion.ts:397-417).
A failed check deletes the stored bytes and returns a validation error with a fixed message.
Resume: the server lists pending multipart uploads and the parts already stored, and returns them so the client can continue (files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:97, 127-136).
Rate limit per request (withRateLimit 'uploads-presign').
features.on_each_app: The brief gives one platform status (done) and no per-app lines. The upload routes are on the web server, which every app calls. Which app screens call them was not verified.

features.name: Safety checks on uploads (content inspection and malware scan)
features.use: Checks the real content of a file, not only its declared type, and asks a virus scanner service to scan it. Files with active content, executables, or credentials are refused.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to do: the check runs on every chat upload during step two. A refused file shows a message that names the finding (uploadRefusalMessage, chat-attachment-completion.ts:416).
how_it_should_work: Structural inspection and credential scanning run on the bytes (upload-scan.ts:601-611). A credential detection that names a format refuses the file; an entropy-only finding is reported and not refused (upload-scan.ts:194-200).

The external virus scanner runs when UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL and UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN are set. The scanner streams the file to the virus engine, returns clean or infected, and refuses with 503 if it cannot finish before its deadline (services/upload-scanner/src/server.ts:99-130).
Scanner failure fails closed: the response is 503 and the upload is not kept (server.ts:141-147).
A refused upload's bytes are deleted, not moved to a quarantine area (chat-attachment-completion.ts:414).
Empty or stale signatures make the scanner health report stale or unavailable (server.ts:188-200).
Files over the scanner's size cap are not scanned and get a 413 (server.ts:113-116).
features.on_each_app: Brief status is partial for the platform: complete once the scanner is deployed and the two environment values are set. Per-app differences were not established.

how_it_should_work: Extracted text and anchors are saved for reuse (knowledge-files route and project-knowledge-extraction.ts are the owners named by the brief; their line citations do not match the files, see things_that_look_wrong).

Thumbnails: only jpeg, png, webp and gif sources up to 30 MiB and 8192x8192 pixels get one. The image is auto-rotated and resized to a 640 pixel edge, saved as webp at quality 80 (library-thumbnail.ts:1-60). Other files get no thumbnail (hasLibraryThumbnail, library-thumbnail.ts:21-31).
A thumbnail URL appears in the library list only when hasLibraryThumbnail is true (api/library/route.ts:76).
Preview generation for other file types is not applicable. Image preprocessing beyond the thumbnail (stripping metadata, normalising) was not found.

how_it_works.detail: The client asks for a place to upload. The server checks the request, CSRF token, rate limit, file name, type and size, checks that object storage is set up, and returns an upload target. No record is written yet.
code: apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:66-93 (rate limit, schema, checksum rule, storage check, validation)

how_it_works.detail: For a large file the client sends parts. The server lists pending parts so an interrupted upload can continue.
The client tells the server the upload is done. The route checks CSRF, rate limit and private storage, parses the request, and hands it to the completion code.
The completion code reads the stored bytes and runs the scan. A refused file is purged from storage and the user gets a message.
Structural checks and a credential scan run on the bytes. Credential detections that name a format refuse the file.
The web app sends the bytes to the scanner service with a bearer token. The service streams them to the virus engine and answers clean, infected, or unavailable.
Pictures get a small webp thumbnail on request. The library list adds a thumbnail link only for pictures that qualify.
The file gets one media_assets row. Plan storage is checked before a new file is accepted.
Delete sets a deleted time by default. Permanent delete is a separate flag. The daily job later removes the stored bytes.
The download route checks access for each request and sends the bytes with safe headers.

key_files.role: Step one of an upload: checks the request and returns an upload target.
Step two of a chat upload: scans the bytes, purges refused files and writes the record.
Byte inspection, credential scan and the call to the external scanner.
Web-side client that reads the scanner URL and token and calls the scanner.
Separate HTTP service that streams uploads to the virus engine and answers clean, infected or unavailable.
Resumable multipart session: lists stored parts so an upload can continue.
Owns the media_assets table: insert, library list, soft delete and the 30-day trash rule.
Plan storage allowance and the check that refuses an upload over it.
Picture thumbnail rules and rendering with sharp.
Per-request authorised download with safe headers.
Daily purge of expired trash and its stored objects.
Shared library screen, with optional folder hooks the hosts may supply.

guide.area: Area 96: Artifact and generated-application components (web platform, server side)
guide.what_it_is_for: An artifact is a piece of output a chat produces: a code page, a document, a spreadsheet, a presentation, or a small app. This area keeps those pieces findable across the account, lets the user preview them safely, generates Office and PDF files on request, and lets the user publish an artifact as a link that others can open. It matters because without it, artifacts are lost when a device cache is cleared, and published pages would run with no isolation from the user's session.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user sees the artifact index and previews in chat (code shows no plan gate on the index route). Publishing, the published-app storage and connected-data runs need a signed-in user; the publisher alone can unpublish or restore versions. Viewers of a public link need no account. Workspace (organization) members can open apps shared to their organization (apps/web/db/neon/0184_organization_shared_artifacts.sql). Moderators use the takedown and content-report admin routes. Voice-session users trigger office file generation (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts). Developers change this area through the server routes and services listed below.

features.name: Account-wide artifact index
features.use: Lets the Artifacts gallery list every artifact the account has produced, not only ones this device has opened.
how_people_use_it: Open the Artifacts gallery in the web app.
Optionally filter by project (the server accepts a projectId filter).
how_it_should_work: The index holds metadata only (id, title, type, language, conversation, message, time), never the artifact content.
Rows are written by the server when an assistant message is saved, not by the client.
Indexing failures must never fail or delay saving the message; the index can be rebuilt from messages.
Default page size is 200, maximum 500.
Each user only sees their own rows (row-level security in the database).
features.on_each_app: Brief gives one status for the platform (server side) only. Code opened is in apps/web. Per-app status for desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome was not given in the brief and not checked.

features.name: Artifact version store
features.use: Keeps each successive version of a managed artifact so a version can be read back or restored.
how_people_use_it: Edit a desktop artifact, then sync; earlier versions stay on the server.
Restore an earlier version from the publication's version list (see the publishing feature).
how_it_should_work: Only managed artifacts whose content has diverged from the message are stored here; re-derivable web artifacts are not pushed.
Version rows are append-only and keyed by artifact and version number.
Last writer wins on the current row; history is union-merged.
Rows are isolated per user by row-level security.

how_it_should_work: Links use an unguessable 24-character token; knowledge of the token is the read grant.
Publish is CSRF-checked and rate-limited; the per-user cap (MAX_PUBLISHED_PER_USER) returns a conflict message when reached.
Republishing the same artifact keeps the same link.
Published apps have no expiry; revocation is explicit.
Unpublish returns not-found if the token is not the caller's.
Moderators can take down a publication, and content reports go to a review queue.

how_it_works.step: Save an assistant message and index its artifacts
how_it_works.detail: When a chat sync saves an assistant message, the server schedules indexing for it. Indexing deletes the message's old index rows and inserts one row per artifact found, using the derived artifact id. Failure is only logged.
The gallery asks the index route. The route checks the rate limit, validates the limit and projectId query, runs a join to conversations that are not deleted, and returns metadata only.

how_it_works.step: Preview an artifact in the sandbox frame
how_it_works.detail: The preview frame loads from the sandbox origin read from an environment value. Code refuses an origin that is the app's own origin. The frame sends a render message; the sandbox replies with ready, render-complete or render-error. A timeout switches to the fallback frame.

how_it_works.step: Generate an Office or PDF file from a voice request
how_it_works.detail: The voice tool list includes the office file tool. The tool runner checks the tool name, calls the generator, and persists the bytes with origin 'managed-office-tool'. The generator validates the request, builds a docx, pptx, xlsx or pdf file and checks the output.

how_it_works.step: Export a document in the browser
how_it_works.detail: The user's export choice calls one of three functions. Markdown is a text download. PDF and Word are built from the markdown in the browser and downloaded through a temporary link.

The publish route checks CSRF and the rate limit, validates the body (kind, content up to the size cap), runs the publication policy, then stores the row with a new random token. The admission step takes a per-user lock so the quota check is safe. It writes an audit event and returns the share URL.

The viewer page first looks for a public row by token. If none, it checks the viewer's signed-in access: organization sharing first, then invited viewers. If nothing matches, it shows an unavailable or invite-only page. Public row content is rendered by kind; HTML and React go through the sandbox frame.

A published app calls the storage route with an operation (get, set, delete, list). The route checks the token, CSRF, account status and rate limit, then reads the runnable artifact and applies the scope and size rules.

Unpublish deletes the publication for the caller by token and returns success. Restore is a separate versioned route that restores the server's stored snapshot. Moderators' takedown removes publications by token and logs the action.
