guide.area: Named technology options (brief area 104): the libraries and engines behind each product feature
guide.what_it_is_for: This area is the set of named technology choices under the product: the web framework, the chat answer renderer, the document, code and slide editors, the PDF text reader, the terminal, the on-device data store and model runtime, the search and vector store, the job queue, the cloud sandbox, sign-in, payments, key management and monitoring. A person does not see this as one screen. They meet it as answers that render math and diagrams, artifacts they can edit, files they can read, and background work that keeps running. The brief records whether each named technology is in the code, missing, or not applicable.
guide.who_uses_it: Every end user meets parts of it through chat and artifact screens. Cloud parts are gated by plan or beta: the cloud sandbox is checked against a managed-compute private beta gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:3 imports it; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:221 checks it). Workspace admins choose a key provider for customer-managed keys (apps/web/lib/crypto/kms-providers.ts:38-44). Developers maintain the libraries and guard tests. Which plans get which other parts was not established.

features.name: Chat answers: formatting, code, math, diagrams and embedded app cards
features.use: Shows an answer as formatted text, highlighted code, typeset math, Mermaid diagrams, and small connector app cards that run in an isolated frame.
how_people_use_it: Ask a question and read the answer as it streams in.
Read code blocks, which are highlighted.
Interact with an app card inside its frame when a connector returns one.
how_it_should_work: The answer is parsed as Markdown and sanitized before display (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx:2-5, 15).
Math is typeset with KaTeX; its stylesheet loads with the component (MarkdownContent.tsx:3, 57).
Code is highlighted by a Shiki highlighter (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/shikiHighlighter.ts:1).
Mermaid is loaded lazily the first time a diagram renders (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MermaidDiagram.tsx:135-137).

App cards render in a sandbox frame; if the sandbox origin is unavailable the card shows the error code sandbox_origin_unavailable (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:245).
Not verified: what a person sees when a diagram or formula fails to render, and what the empty state looks like.
features.on_each_app: Web renders through MessageBubble.tsx:111 using the shared unified-chat package. The brief gives one status per item (platform), not per app. The shared package is used by desktop, web, Chrome and VS Code (AGENTS.md section 5). Mobile has its own math tests (apps/mobile/__tests__/MathBlockOffline.test.tsx) and a KaTeX vendoring script (apps/mobile/scripts/vendor-katex-math-styles.cjs), so mobile math is handled on the device.

features.name: Artifacts: documents, code, charts, slides, images, and two items not built
features.use: The side panel where a person views and edits an artifact: a rich document, code, a chart, a slide deck, or an image.
how_people_use_it: Open an artifact from an answer.
Type in the rich document editor.
Edit code in the code editor.
Look at a chart or step through slides.
Mask, crop or annotate an image in the mask dialog, or describe an edit in the composer.
how_it_should_work: The rich document is edited with a Tiptap editor (ArtifactDocumentEditor.tsx:26); Markdown must round-trip back to the same document (document-editor-markdown.ts:81 roundTripsAsDocument).
Code editor has an aria label and turns spellcheck off (ArtifactCodeEditor.tsx:142).
Charts render with recharts (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/ChartCanvas.tsx:18) and are mounted by ArtifactPreview.tsx:1977-1979.
Slides render as navigable slides (PresentationArtifact.tsx:40) and are written to a real .pptx file by pptxgenjs (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts:23).
Image mask dialog lives in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ImageMaskDialog.tsx:91.
Spreadsheet grid (S104.05) and video editing (S104.08) are marked not applicable; no code was found for them.
Not verified: failure and empty states for each editor.
features.on_each_app: Web: ArtifactPreview.tsx hosts all viewers. Mobile: artifact tests exist (apps/mobile/__tests__/artifact-export-fidelity.test.ts) but the mobile viewer was not read. Desktop, Chrome and VS Code share the unified-chat artifact components where they mount them. The brief gives one status per item, so per-app depth is unknown.

features.name: Files and PDFs: reading PDFs and storing uploads
features.use: A PDF attached to chat has its text pulled out so the assistant can use it, and uploaded and generated files are kept in object storage.
how_people_use_it: Attach a PDF in the composer.
Wait for the file to be read, then ask about it.
Upload a large file in parts (resumable upload).
how_it_should_work: PDF text is extracted on the server with the pdfjs legacy build (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:196-204), then truncated to a fixed size limit (pdf-attachment-content.ts:144).
Resumable uploads use a session lifetime tied to orphan multipart age (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/resumable-upload.ts:50).
Files are written through an S3-compatible adapter (packages/platform/object-storage/src/adapters/s3.ts).
Not verified: an in-product PDF viewer on the web. No client-side PDF viewer was found in apps/web; PDF rendering libraries are used on the server only.
Not verified: upload failure messages and limits by plan.
features.on_each_app: Web: server-side text extraction; no web viewer found. Mobile: a PDF viewer is vendored (apps/mobile/scripts/vendor-pdfjs-viewer.cjs), so mobile has an on-device viewer. Desktop and Chrome were not read.

features.name: Web app building blocks: framework, shared controls and server-data cache
features.use: The base of the web product: pages, shared dialogs and menus, and the cache that keeps server data fresh.
how_people_use_it: Not used directly. People see it as pages that load, dialogs that open, and menus that respond.
how_it_should_work: The web product is a Next.js app with a root layout (apps/web/app/layout.tsx) and client providers (apps/web/app/Providers.tsx:1, apps/web/app/ProductRuntimeProviders.tsx:12).
Shared dialog and popover primitives are built on Radix (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Dialog.tsx:1, Popover.tsx:1).
Server data is cached with TanStack Query; the QueryClientProvider is set in apps/web/shared/stores/query-client.ts:2 and :118.
Not verified: how the shared primitives are mounted by every screen (the brief cites WebChatPage.tsx:134, which is an import line).

features.name: Terminal panel for local code sessions

Type commands and read output.

features.name: Live updates, live voice and co-editing (not built)

how_people_use_it: Watch an answer appear as it streams.
Start a live voice conversation.

Web voice builds a WebRTC peer connection and waits for ICE gathering (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:304, 447).
Voice sessions are created on the server (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:331 area).

features.name: Native apps and CLI shells
features.use: The desktop app (Electron), the mobile app (Expo React Native), and the command-line app (Rust with a terminal UI).
how_people_use_it: Install and open the desktop, mobile or CLI app.
Use the desktop to pick a screen or window to share (a system picker callback is at apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:884).

features.name: On-device data and on-device models
features.use: The mobile app keeps data in an encrypted database on the phone, and can run a model on the device for free when the phone is capable.
how_people_use_it: Use the mobile app offline; chats are stored on the phone.
Go through onboarding, which recommends a model for the device.
Check device capability in performance settings.
how_it_should_work: Mobile opens an encrypted SQLite database with a 256-bit key kept in device secure storage (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:23 file name, :25 key storage id, :27 unreadable-database pattern).
Encryption is turned on in the Expo config (apps/mobile/app.config.js:454).
Unreadable database files are set aside, not deleted (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts imports unreadableFiles).
On-device model runtime is in packages/platform/local-llm/src/tier3.ts:30 (loaded at runtime; the package name is not repeated here).
Onboarding decides whether a device is capable (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:158).
Desktop does not import the on-device package; it checks a local model server instead (apps/desktop/src/services/ollamaHealthService.ts:1).
Not verified: what a person sees when the device cannot run a model.
features.on_each_app: Mobile: encrypted database and on-device model. Desktop: local model server check, not the on-device package. Web: none found. Chrome, VS Code and CLI: not read.

features.name: Search and stored knowledge
features.use: Finds past chats and matches uploaded knowledge by meaning as well as by words.
how_people_use_it: Type in the search box.
Ask a question that uses uploaded knowledge.
how_it_should_work: Data lives in Neon Postgres through a data adapter (packages/platform/data-layer/src/adapters/neon.ts:65).
Keyword search uses full-text search (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-search-service.ts:220-223).
Meaning search uses a vector distance query (retrieval-search-service.ts:235-239) over an embedding index (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:142).
Queries are scoped to the user (retrieval-search-service.ts:204).
Search route reads the role parameter at apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:308.
No separate search engine was found; search runs inside the database.
Not verified: result limits and ranking details.
features.on_each_app: Web: search and retrieval. Mobile: local data only. Other apps: not read.

features.name: Background jobs and durable agent runs
features.use: Work that takes a long time (agent runs, indexing, cleanup) runs in the background and survives a closed tab.
how_people_use_it: Start a cloud agent task and leave; the result appears later.
Not directly visible for other jobs.
how_it_should_work: A cron route drains queued jobs every schedule (vercel.json:150).

The drain checks cron authentication, skips work in low-power mode, and stops after a 250-second budget with at most 12 jobs in flight (apps/web/app/api/cron/drain-background-jobs/route.ts:20-26 and constants at :17-18).
Permanent job errors are raised as permanent failures (apps/web/lib/jobs/job-handlers.ts:261).
A durable workflow runs the cloud agent, and waits for the device to be present up to a set budget (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts:34).
Low-power mode is read from AGI_DB_LOW_POWER (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:9-11).
Not verified: retry counts and what the user sees when a job fails.
features.on_each_app: Web server side. Desktop and mobile trigger cloud agent work; their handling was not read.

features.name: Cloud code sandbox and browser automation
features.use: Cloud code runs in a hosted sandbox. The Chrome extension drives a real browser tab through the browser debugger protocol.
how_people_use_it: Start a cloud code session on the web (needs the sandbox switched on).
In the Chrome extension, approve a browser task; the agent clicks and types in the tab.
how_it_should_work: Sandbox runs only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION is 1 and an E2B key is set (see things_that_look_wrong: the gate code is looser than this).
When the sandbox is off, runtime refuses with not-configured (apps/web/lib/e2b/runtime.ts:796).
The extension attaches the debugger to a tab (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/debuggerSession.ts:65) and detaches on the debugger detach event (debuggerSession.ts:152).
Commands to one tab are serialized through a guard (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cdpDriver.ts:329).
Not verified: user approval flow before the first action.
features.on_each_app: Web: cloud code sandbox, off by default. Chrome extension: browser automation. Desktop, mobile, CLI and VS Code: not read.

features.name: Accounts, payments, encryption keys, monitoring and release builds
features.use: Signs people in, takes payment, protects organization data with customer-managed keys, reports errors and traces, turns features on per user, and builds and signs releases.
how_people_use_it: Sign in with the hosted account service.
Pay through checkout.
Admins choose a key provider for their organization.
Developers read errors and traces.
how_it_should_work: Sign-in uses the hosted account provider with telemetry off (apps/web/lib/identity/Provider.tsx:27); the web proxy is at apps/web/proxy.ts:25.
Checkout creates sessions (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:391); payment webhooks are checked with signature verification (apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/verify.ts).
Key providers are built only when their credentials exist, so an unconfigured provider cannot answer (apps/web/lib/crypto/kms-providers.ts:18-19); the AWS and GCP credential variables are at :38-44.
Monitoring starts only when configured; OpenTelemetry export and Sentry init are at apps/web/instrumentation.ts:98 and :101.
Feature flags are read from the database with a cache (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/flag-store.ts:115); the entitlement bundle is built in apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:197.
Release builds sign and notarize macOS installers (.github/workflows/release-desktop-cloud.yml:212-236).
features.on_each_app: Web: sign-in, checkout, flags, monitoring. Mobile: sign-in provider used at apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx. Desktop: release signing. Other apps: not read.

how_it_works.detail: The chat screen renders the answer through the shared Markdown renderer. Math, code and diagrams are handled inside the renderer.
Markdown is parsed, math is typeset with KaTeX, and HTML is sanitized before it is shown.

how_it_works.step: 3. Code and diagrams load on demand
how_it_works.detail: Code highlighting uses Shiki; Mermaid is loaded only when a diagram appears.
The artifact viewer mounts the document editor, code editor, chart or slide viewer for the artifact type.

how_it_works.step: 5. Attached PDF is read on the server
how_it_works.detail: The server extracts PDF text with the pdfjs legacy build and caps its length before it goes to the model.
Conversations and search data go to Neon Postgres through the data adapter; files go to S3-compatible storage.
Keyword search uses full-text search; meaning search uses a vector distance query, scoped to the user.

how_it_works.step: 8. Background work drains on a schedule
how_it_works.detail: A cron route runs queued jobs within a time budget; cloud agent runs use a durable workflow.

how_it_works.step: 9. Cloud sandbox is checked before use
how_it_works.detail: Before any cloud code run, the sandbox gate checks the switch and key. If off, the run is refused.
Flags are read from the database per subject; errors and traces are exported when configured.

guide.what_it_is_for: A developer uses this area to create projects and API keys, then call the AGI Workforce gateway from their own code, scripts or the command line. Each key can be limited by scope, expiry and project, and spend can be capped per project and per workspace. The area also holds webhooks (automatic messages sent to the developer's server when something happens), rate-limit readouts, prompt templates with test cases, and the API reference. It matters because it is the only path for a developer to use the platform outside the apps, and because a spend cap must hold when a key is used.
guide.who_uses_it: Developers on a plan that includes the managed API capability (the server checks this with canUseBillingPlanCapability(planTier, 'managed_api') in apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:85). Workspace admins and owners for service accounts and the workspace spend cap (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/admin-api-keys/route.ts and spend-limit/route.ts, which use role checks). Anyone can read the public API docs at /api-docs. The code does not show a separate free-plan rule for the console beyond the managed_api check, so the exact plan list is in the types package, which I did not open.

features.name: Projects with monthly credit limits

how_it_works.detail: The Developer console page renders the cards in order: API keys, projects, playground, prompts, logs, webhooks, rate limits and reference links.

The key form posts to the settings API keys route. The route checks the CSRF token, the managed_api plan capability, the 20-key limit and the project, then asks for a step-up check. The service makes the key, stores only its hash, and returns the full key once.

how_it_works.step: Use the key on the gateway
how_it_works.detail: A call to the chat gateway sends the key. The service looks up the key where it is not revoked and not expired, and updates its last-used time. Then the project spend check runs: if the project is over its limit, the call gets HTTP 429.

Before the turn runs, the chat route checks the workspace cap. If the check is refused, the call gets HTTP 429 with the cap's reason. If the check itself errors, the code lets the call through (see things that look wrong).
GET models filters the catalog by the plan, by the surface, and by kill switches, then returns the list with capabilities and any retirement date.

An event is written to the deliveries table. The first attempt runs after the response. The delivery signs the body with the endpoint secret, opened with the platform key, and posts it. Failures are retried by a queued job.
Archiving a project revokes its keys, writes an audit event for each one, and queues an api_key.revoked webhook event.

key_files.role: The console page that lays out every card and the reference links.
Lists and creates API keys; enforces plan, key limit and step-up.
Revokes one key (DELETE).
Makes keys, stores their hash, checks expiry and revocation when a key is used.
Refuses calls from a project that has reached its monthly credit limit.
Gateway model list, filtered by plan, surface and kill switches.
Workspace spend cap check before a managed turn.
Webhook endpoints, deliveries, signing secret handling, retries.
List of webhook event types, retry limits and timeout.
Browser form that sends a test request and builds a copyable curl command.
Test cases, CSV import, runs and per-case diffs for a prompt.
Public API documentation page: auth, scopes, webhooks, migration, deprecations.

how_it_works.step: Slack sends an event to the web app
how_it_works.detail: Slack posts to /api/webhooks/slack. The handler rate-limits the request (trigger-webhook), reads the body (limit 256 KB), and checks the Slack signature against SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET. If the secret is missing it refuses with 503. It answers the one-time URL check with the challenge. Non-event callbacks get 'received'.

readSlackAssistantEvent keeps direct messages and app mentions. It drops bot messages, most subtypes, empty text and code-only messages. It also handles app uninstall and token revoked events. A mention in a direct-message channel is dropped.

how_it_works.step: Handler runs after the reply is sent
how_it_works.detail: Slack gets its acknowledgement first. The assistant handler then runs in an after() callback, so Slack does not retry while the answer is being made. Every event is also passed to the trigger ingest, which is a separate path for routines.

how_it_works.step: Account link and channel policy checks
how_it_works.detail: The workspace installation is found by team id. The Slack user is resolved to an AGI account. If unlinked, a link prompt is sent. If the channel is off, a notice is sent. The run mode (answer or task) is chosen from the channel policy and task availability.
A run row is inserted per installation and Slack event id, so a repeated delivery does nothing. The working reaction is added to the message.

how_it_works.step: Context is built from Slack history
how_it_works.detail: Thread messages (or the last 12 hours of direct messages) are read from Slack with the bot token. Text is cleaned and limited. Task mode creates or reuses a conversation when the route is chosen.

how_it_works.step: The turn runs under the person's account
how_it_works.detail: Content is checked (moderation, the user's content-safety preference, secret handling). A model route is chosen through managed-cloud admission. The request runs in work mode for tasks. Output streams into the run. Tools are limited to the channel allow-list.

how_it_works.step: The answer or approval is posted to Slack
how_it_works.detail: An answer is split into Slack blocks and posted in the thread, then the run is marked completed. If approval is needed, an ephemeral (private to the person) approval message with Approve and Deny buttons is posted, a notification is recorded, and the run waits. A click goes to the interactions webhook and resumes the run. Any failure posts a generic notice and marks the run failed.

key_files.role: Slack Events API receiver: signature check, challenge answer, hands events to the assistant and trigger ingest.
Decides which Slack events are assistant messages (direct messages and mentions) and which are app-uninstall or token-revoke events.
Main Slack flow: link check, channel mode, run start, answer or approval posting, failure notices.
Runs the assistant turn: content checks, model route, streaming output, approval pause and resume.
Builds the conversation from Slack history (thread or direct-message window) with size limits.
Calls to the Slack Web API: post message, ephemeral message, reactions, read thread and history, rate-limit retry.
Bot scopes, environment reads (Slack app id, secret, app origin), context limits, TTLs and the working reaction name.
Per-channel mode (off, answer, task), tool allow-list, and installer-only writes.
Task mode: creates the AGI conversation, reuses a thread's conversation, settles the task.
Reads Approve and Deny clicks and decides the approval.
Links a Slack user to an AGI account through a one-time link request.
Settings UI for channel mode and tools (web only).

switches.name: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
switches.effect: Without it, every Slack event is refused with 503; with a wrong value, 401.

switches.name: SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID and SLACK_APP_CLIENT_SECRET
switches.effect: Both needed for the install (OAuth) flow; without them Settings > Slack reports unavailable.

switches.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
switches.effect: Must be https, or http on localhost. Otherwise links, OAuth and replies are refused and messages are not answered.

switches.name: Connector token storage availability
switches.effect: Needed for Slack to be configured at all.

switches.name: slack_app plan capability
switches.effect: Decides whether the workspace may use Slack on the plan.

switches.name: Work capability and managed compute access
switches.effect: Decides whether a channel run may be a task; otherwise it is an answer.

switches.name: Channel mode (off, answer, task)
switches.effect: off stops answers in that channel; answer never runs tasks; task runs tasks when allowed.

switches.name: Channel tool allow-list
switches.effect: Limits the tools a channel run may use; an unreadable list gives no tools.

switches.name: Rate limits
switches.effect: Per workspace and per Slack user limits on assistant messages; per-event rate limit on the webhook.

switches.name: Context limits
switches.effect: How many messages, pages and characters the assistant reads from Slack.

switches.name: Approval window (24 hours) and link window (15 minutes)
switches.effect: How long an approval or a link request stays valid.

switches.name: Answer time budget
switches.effect: Caps how long one answer may run.

switches.name: Bot token scopes

guide.what_it_is_for: This area covers what people see beyond their own chats: public shared chats, a gallery of examples, public work by other users, and the rules for reporting and removing content. A visitor can read a shared chat, copy it into their own account and keep going, reuse a gallery example's prompt, and report harmful or infringing content. Most of the discovery side the brief describes (personal feed, topics, follows, blocking, collections, comments) has no code in the repository yet, so the area is mostly sharing, gallery examples, reporting and operator takedown.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-out visitors and anyone with a share link (read a public shared chat, browse the curated gallery). Signed-in users (copy a shared chat into their account, report an AI answer or a shared item). Platform admins only (review the report queue and copyright notices, unpublish content). Publishers and partners (plugin directory submission and marketplace sources; the partner page is a contact page). The brief marks no paid-plan gate for this area, and the code I opened shows none.

how_it_works.detail: The API returns the share with a 410 response when the link has expired, a 404 when it is missing, and a rate limit on the share-view bucket.

how_it_works.step: Copy the chat into the viewer's account
how_it_works.detail: The continue screen reads the workspace, fetches the share, creates a new conversation with the title and model, then posts messages in batches of 200 to the bulk-message route. Artifacts from the shared chat are saved in the local artifact store. On success it opens the new chat. On failure it deletes the partial conversation.

The web message menu sends a report with the harmful category, the message ID, the conversation ID and up to 500 characters of the message. The report goes to the content-report route, which is the same handler as the mobile route.

The handler checks the CSRF token and a rate limit, validates the body with a schema, and reads the user if signed in. It inserts a row into the reports table, using the client report ID as a unique key so repeats do nothing.
The mobile app keeps reports in on-device storage and can open the mail app with the report filled in. The intake route comment says the device copy is an offline fallback only.

Platform admins list notices and record decisions. Marking a notice actioned calls the takedown route, which needs an admin session, a CSRF token and an audit event. A not-found result leads to a separate confirm step that records the notice without removing anything.

guide.area: Specialist workspaces (area 108): finance, health, legal, research, study, business and shopping/travel workspaces
guide.what_it_is_for: Specialist workspaces give a person focused tools for one field of life or work: money, health records, legal and contract work, research with cited sources, study, sales, support, HR, marketing, shopping and travel. Most of the brief's 35 items are not built yet. Built today: the bank-accounts dashboard (web), the Health space (web, partly), deep research with cited reports (all apps), Study mode (web and mobile), and skill-driven business workflows. Each area is a separate feature, and some of them carry legal limits (US only, not in organisation workspaces, owner sign-offs still pending) that the product must enforce.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person for Study mode (no plan check found in apps/web/app/api/study/sessions/route.ts). Paid plans only for linked bank accounts (connectors capability: PAID_TIERS, packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:351). Deep research only on Pro and higher plans (PRO_TIERS, billing-catalog.ts:354-355) and never on a free-trial turn (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:567). The Health space only for an individual, in the United States, not inside an organisation workspace (apps/web/lib/services/health-space-service.ts:23-29). Workspace admins: no admin-only control for these features was found. Developers: the skill files under .agents/skills define the business workflows.

how_it_works.detail: The Finance route renders the FinanceDashboard component inside the web app shell.

how_it_works.step: Link a bank through the hosted Plaid window
how_it_works.detail: The person clicks link. The client lists linked banks, then posts to the link endpoint. The server checks CSRF, rate limit, setup, US region and the connector policy, then asks Plaid for a hosted-link or link token. Plaid runs the bank sign-in in its own window.

how_it_works.step: Exchange the Plaid public token and store the item
how_it_works.detail: After the bank sign-in, the exchange endpoint receives the link token and stores a new bank item. The access token is encrypted before it is written to the bank_account_items table.

The server reads bank items for the user, decrypts each access token, and calls Plaid's balance and transactions endpoints. The dashboard fetches an overview from a finance overview path with a period parameter (that route was not opened).
In a chat turn, the bank read tools are added to the tool list for the turn. Only read-class tools are offered for sensitive connectors. Mobile turns never get them.

A Research turn checks the plan capability and the free-trial state. If both allow it, the turn goes to the research loop instead of the one-shot path. The loop plans, searches in rounds within fixed bounds, always runs a final synthesis, and streams cumulative sources.
The finished report, with its sources and steps, is written to the research_reports table, and reports are read back for the reports screens.
The availability endpoint returns available or unavailable with a reason. When available, the Health space is a per-user project row, created once.

Study starts from the study page. The session endpoint validates the topic, mode and level strictly, then writes the session to the study_sessions table. The study instruction is composed and ranked against account and request instructions.
Business workflows are skill files. The skill catalog lists them for the person unless they turned them off. The skill runs as chat instructions. Its lock entries pin its content.

Health space availability reasons and the per-user Health project row.

Chat completions route; branches a Research turn into the research loop unless it is a free trial.
Which plan tiers have each capability (connectors, deep research and others).

Study session API: start, read and end a session for a conversation.

guide.shared_code: Shared across apps: the bank and Health contracts in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts (apps/web/lib/connectors/plaid-config.ts:1-6 re-exports the bank constants; apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:19-22 uses the same paths); plan tiers in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts; interactive card types (packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts); the chat completions API that web, desktop (hosted web app) and the CLI call. Skills under .agents/skills are shared content delivered through the skill catalog. Separate per app: the web finance page and Health space UI (apps/web/features/finance, apps/web/features/health); mobile's own study screen (apps/mobile/src/features/study), research reports screen (apps/mobile/src/features/research) and feature flags (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts); the Chrome extension has no code for these features that was checked.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Brief cites plaid-config.ts:32 for the gates. Line 32 is the Plaid Link script URL constant. The real gates are the mobile exclusion at lines 15-18 and the credential and environment functions at lines 45-58.
Brief cites oauth-scope-allowlist.ts:234 for the HealthEx entry. The file has 40 lines and no HealthEx entry. HealthEx is registered in the connector catalog.
Brief names the env var CONNECTOR_OAUTH_HEALTHEX_CLIENT_ID. No code reading that name was found; OAuth providers are read from CONNECTOR_OAUTH_PROVIDERS_JSON.
Brief marks Study mobile as missing. A mobile study route and screen exist, and the composer menu on mobile links to it.

Brief says travel 'can make reservations'. The itinerary tool does not book anything; its guidance tells the model to use a booking connector. The only reservation code in the file is for search billing.

Brief cites ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:877 for research. That line is the Study menu row. The web Research toggle is checked at ChatComposerNew.tsx:1621, and mobile's research toggle is at AddToChatSheet.tsx:230-235. Brief cites AddToChatSheet.tsx:116 for research, but line 116 is the cloud-access prop.

Brief cites vendor directory entries and route.ts:798 for curriculum generation. Those are directory entries and a route line, not curriculum code. Curriculum output comes from the study prompt and plan request (study-session.ts:115-122).

Reproducible environments: the sandbox harness is spawned by name, and the template list is declared in code. The file header does not show a pinned version per template, so reproducibility is not established by this code.
Contract review, sales, support, HR and marketing are marked done, but the code read is skill files and the catalog. No runtime path showing these skills run to completion was checked.

Privacy text says Health-space chats go only to providers recorded as not training on user data, and refuses others. The availability code read does not enforce this; the enforcement was not found in the lines read.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area lets a person reach AGI without opening the main app. On the desktop, a menu-bar icon, global keyboard shortcuts and a small floating Quick Ask panel start chats, capture the screen or a window, and start dictation. On the phone, widgets, a hardware Action or Control button, and Siri or a headset can start a chat or ask a question. A desktop companion lets a paired phone watch and steer desktop coding sessions. Many items are still missing, especially on the desktop widget, selected-text rewrite, telephone, wearable, lock-screen and spatial surfaces.
guide.who_uses_it: Desktop users (menu bar, shortcuts, Quick Ask, capture, dictation) and phone users (widgets, Control button, Siri Ask). Remote Control (the companion) is limited to paid plans by the plan capability 'remote_control' (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352, PAID_TIERS), and on the phone it is hidden in the shipped build because the flags companion and dispatch are false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:12,16). Ask from Siri needs a switch turned on in the app and a valid token. Local-model screens on the phone are for any user who installs a model. Chrome users get the in-page floating panel. CLI and VS Code have no local-model download, storage or hardware features.

features.name: Menu-bar quick menu (desktop)
features.use: One click from the menu-bar (macOS) or tray icon to start a new chat, open Quick Ask, capture the screen or a window, start dictation, stop agents, or open the Shortcuts submenu.
how_people_use_it: Click the menu-bar icon.
Click an action such as New Chat, Quick Ask, Screenshot, Window or Voice.
Open Shortcuts to pick a different key chord for each action.
how_it_should_work: The menu shows the current accelerator next to each action.
Running agents and sessions waiting for approval are listed above the actions, with Stop All Agents enabled only when a turn is running.
The tray icon appears only when Show in menu bar is on, computer use is granted, or an agent is running (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1858-1864).
If a shortcut cannot be registered, the menu marks it with the reason (taken, duplicate or malformed) and a notification explains it.
No plan gate was seen for the tray.
features.on_each_app: Desktop (Electron) only: done. Tauri build not checked. Mobile and Chrome are n/a. CLI and VS Code are not in the brief.

features.name: Screen and window capture to chat (desktop shortcuts)
features.use: A global shortcut captures the whole screen, or one chosen window, and pastes the image into the main chat window.
how_people_use_it: Press the Screenshot shortcut (default Command or Control plus Shift plus 2) for the whole screen.
Press the Window shortcut (default Command or Control plus Shift plus 1) and then the window in front of the chat is captured.
The image is pasted into the chat composer, and the previous clipboard text is put back.
how_it_should_work: The capture is put on the clipboard, then pasted into the chat window (apps/desktop/electron/screenshot.ts:142 and :190).
If the chat window is closed, the image stays on the clipboard and a notification says so.
If no other app window is in front, or the permission is missing, a notification says what to fix.
A second press while a capture is running is ignored (a shared 'capturing' flag).
Shortcut choices are offered in a fixed list (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:161-168).
features.on_each_app: Desktop: done (both). Chrome has a screenshot-to-chat path in apps/extension/manifest.json:75 and bridgeServer.ts (brief says done; not traced in detail). Mobile n/a.

features.name: Compact floating Quick Ask panel
features.use: A small always-on-top window that takes one prompt over other apps without opening the full app.
how_people_use_it: Press the Quick Ask shortcut (default Alt+Shift+Space on the desktop).
Type a prompt in the panel and send it.
Press Escape or click away to hide it. Use the handoff to open a longer conversation in the main window.
how_it_should_work: The panel is 480 by 620 pixels, frameless, and always on top, and it is shown at the top centre of the display under the cursor (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:6-7, 139-144).
It is warmed up at launch and reloaded if the first load failed or it left the Quick Ask page.
Navigating to any page other than Quick Ask sends the main window to that page and hides the panel (quickAsk.ts:29-41, :97-105).
In Chrome, an in-page panel is mounted on the page by setup code (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:55-65). The mobile app has no floating panel (missing).
If the page cannot load, the panel stays blank until a reload is triggered. No explicit error UI was seen.
features.on_each_app: Desktop: done (Electron Quick Ask panel). Chrome: done (in-page panel in apps/extension). Mobile: missing.

features.name: Global dictation from anywhere (desktop and phone)
features.use: Start speaking to AGI from any app on the computer or phone without opening AGI first.
how_people_use_it: Press the Dictation shortcut (default Alt+Shift+V on the desktop).
Speak. Press again to stop.
If the main window is hidden, the panel opens and a notification says 'Press the dictation shortcut again once the window is open.'
how_it_should_work: The press goes to Quick Ask when it is visible, otherwise to a visible main window, otherwise Quick Ask is raised (apps/desktop/electron/voiceDictation.ts:34-45).
A press also tries the 'dictate into focused app' path first when it is turned on or already listening (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1921-1930).
The desktop sends a toggle message to the page, which does the capture (voiceDictation.ts:47-49).
Failures are recorded as telemetry events (voice_shortcut, refused or failed).
features.on_each_app: Desktop: done. Mobile: done (brief cites apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:579, which does not hold dictation logic; see things_that_look_wrong). Chrome: missing.

features.name: Phone home-screen widgets and hardware button
features.use: A phone widget with New chat, Camera and Voice buttons, and an iOS Control or Action-button control that opens AGI.
how_people_use_it: Add the 'AGI Mobile' widget to the home screen (small or medium size) and tap New chat, Camera or Voice.
On iOS 18 or later, add the Open AGI Mobile control to Control Center, the Lock Screen or the Action Button and press it.
how_it_should_work: Each widget button opens a deep link agiworkforce://intent/<verb> (Android: apps/mobile/native/android/widget/AGIQuickActionsWidget.kt:12-22; iOS: AGIWidgets.swift:77-107 using AGIWidgetLink values).
The app routes intent links to chat or voice (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:161).
The widgets are added through a config plugin (apps/mobile/native/ios/withAGIWidgets.cjs) and generated iOS project output is not hand-edited.
Widget content is static (no live data was seen).
Desktop widgets and a Stream Deck or macropad integration were not found (desktop missing, chrome missing).
features.on_each_app: Mobile: done for widgets and the iOS control (the brief marks these 'missing' for home-screen and 'done' for hardware, see things_that_look_wrong). Desktop: missing. Chrome: missing.

features.name: Siri and headset invocation (phone)
features.use: Say 'Ask AGI Mobile' to Siri, or use a headset button, and hear the answer without opening the app.
how_people_use_it: Turn on 'Ask from Siri' in the app's Settings, Security and login section.
Say or type the question to Siri, or trigger the App Intent.
Hear the answer, or read the error message the intent speaks back.
how_it_should_work: The intent sends the question to the server over HTTPS with a bearer token kept in the device keychain (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:11-97).
Questions over 2,000 characters or empty questions are refused locally.

The server checks the token, rate limit, MFA and IP allow list, then checks chat permission and managed compute access for the 'mobile' surface, then routes the question and reserves usage (apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent/ask/route.ts:24-70; apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:150-215).
A 401 tells the user to set the intent up again. A missing token says Ask from Siri is off.
The request times out after 50 seconds on the server and 55 on the phone.
features.on_each_app: Mobile iOS: done. Desktop: missing. Chrome: missing. Android equivalent not found.

features.name: Desktop companion pairing (phone controls desktop work)
features.use: Pair a phone with the desktop app so a paid user can start, watch and approve desktop coding sessions from the phone.
how_people_use_it: On the desktop or web settings page, open Remote Control and show the pairing QR code or 6-character code.
On the phone, scan the QR code (companion screen) or enter the code.
In the desktop, confirm the phone by its pairing code in the dialog, then watch sessions and answer approvals from the phone.
Stop Remote Control, or disconnect, to end the pairing.
how_it_should_work: The web or desktop asks the server to start a pairing (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:66); a closed screen-share switch or a non-paid plan refuses it with a message.
The desktop shows a confirmation for each phone, and an approval request from the agent times out after 120 seconds (apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:85, :196-210).
Pairing codes expire (default 300 seconds, allowed 30 to 900 seconds).
The VS Code extension can also start a pairing and relay its session approvals (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts:150-170).
The mobile companion screen is hidden in v1 (flags off), so the phone side is not reachable in the shipped build.
features.on_each_app: Desktop: done (Electron remote service). Web: done (settings section, paid-plan message). VS Code: done (initiator 'desktop'). Mobile: code exists but feature flags companion and dispatch are false (hidden).

features.name: On-device model library (download, storage, delete)
features.use: Browse on-device models, download them with progress, cancel or resume, and see and delete how much space each uses.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker, choose the On-device scope, and tap a model that says download required.
Watch progress. Tap cancel to stop. Wi-Fi is required unless cellular download is allowed in settings.
Open Settings, Storage to see the size of each model and delete one.
how_it_should_work: Downloads check free space and Wi-Fi/cellular consent before they start (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts:213-240).
Cancelling pauses the resumable download and reports 'Download was cancelled' (modelDownload.ts:303-310, :363-367).
A model that is replying cannot be removed; the user is told to try again later (modelDownload.ts:68).
Model files are excluded from device backup (modelDownload.ts:100).
The picker shows a loading state while installed models are read (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:350-360).
Failures are reported with a kind (ModelDownloadError, modelDownload.ts:41-61).
features.on_each_app: Mobile: done. CLI: missing. VS Code: missing. Desktop and Chrome are not listed in the brief.

features.name: On-device runtime controls and health
features.use: See the phone's hardware capability, load a local model into memory or unload it, and see whether the local runtime is healthy.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, Performance to see RAM, accelerators and runtime tier.
Tap load or unload for a model.
Run the benchmark button; the app announces it is running and shows an error if no model is downloaded.
how_it_should_work: Capabilities come from the local-llm package (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts:150-170, loadedLocalModel).
A message says when a tier is downloadable or downloading (performance.tsx:67-80).
A benchmark with no installed model shows: 'Choose an available on-device model in Models before running a benchmark'.
Runtime errors such as thermal throttling are mapped to a plain message (chatExecutionStore.ts:1389-1416).

CLI and VS Code: the brief marks load controls missing. The CLI has a probe for local servers (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:175-290, discover_all), which is a different feature (local servers, not on-device models); its health output is at apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4765-4791.
features.on_each_app: Mobile: done. CLI: missing (probe of local servers exists but is not this feature). VS Code: missing.

features.name: On-device performance dashboard
features.use: Show speed (tokens per second), first-token latency, memory and thermal state for local replies over time.
how_people_use_it: Send a message to an on-device model.
The app records one performance event per local reply.
The dashboard (Performance screen) shows the recorded values.
how_it_should_work: tokens/s = tokens divided by decode time, rounded to 0.1 (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3138-3149).
First-token latency and thermal state are recorded; peak memory is recorded as the value passed in, which stays 0 in the current code.
No dashboard view over the stored events was checked (not_sure).
features.on_each_app: Mobile: partial. CLI: missing. VS Code: missing.

features.name: Hybrid local and cloud task, and approval before cloud escalation
features.use: Split one task between an on-device model and the cloud, and ask the user before a local task is sent to the cloud.
how_people_use_it: Not reachable: no UI or code path was found on any app.
how_it_should_work: Intended: a task can use local and cloud models in one run; before the cloud step, the user approves the escalation.
Search of mobile, CLI and VS Code for an escalation gate found only unrelated matches (approval notifications, exec policy).

features.name: Channels not built yet (lock screen, selected-text rewrite, phone calls, messaging, wearables, spatial)
features.use: Planned ways to reach AGI from outside the main apps.
how_people_use_it: Not reachable from any app except messaging (see the next note).
how_it_should_work: Lock-screen widget, selected-text rewrite, wearable voice, telephone access and spatial interface: no code found (desktop, mobile or web).

Messaging: a Slack events route exists (apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts) and calls the trigger ingest path, but the brief says the owner still has to create the Slack app, set secrets and apply migration 0333 before it works. The GitHub webhook route at apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:253 handles review requests, not chat.

how_it_works.step: Shortcut or menu press on the desktop
how_it_works.detail: The main process holds the handlers for each action and passes them to the shortcut registry. A chord is registered with the operating system, or the press is refused with a reason.
code: apps/desktop/electron/shortcuts.ts:150-169 (changeGarnishShortcuts, restores old chords when an always-on chord is lost)

how_it_works.detail: Each action has a default chord and a fixed list of alternatives, shared by the desktop and the page. Empty text means the action has no shortcut.

A capture reads the clipboard, takes the screen or chosen window thumbnail, puts the PNG on the clipboard, focuses the chat composer and pastes. It then restores the old clipboard text if the user has not copied something new.
A frameless 480 by 620 window loads the Quick Ask route of the cloud app in a separate session partition. Navigation to other pages is handed to the main window.
A dictation press goes to the visible Quick Ask panel, or the visible main window, or raises Quick Ask. The page then toggles its own voice capture.

how_it_works.step: Remote Control pairing request (desktop, web, VS Code)
how_it_works.detail: The client asks the server to start a pairing. The server checks the screen-share switch, the plan and the account, then returns a code, a relay socket address and a token. The desktop then shows the code and confirms each phone.

how_it_works.step: Phone widget and Siri entry points
how_it_works.detail: Widgets and Control buttons open a deep link. Siri calls the server with a stored token, and the server answers with the chat route chosen by the plan.
Before a download starts, the app checks free space, Wi-Fi or cellular consent and then streams the file with a resumable downloader. Cancel pauses it. Removal is refused while the model is replying.

how_it_works.step: Performance event after a local reply
how_it_works.detail: When a local reply finishes, the app computes tokens per second and latency and records one event with the thermal state.

key_files.role: Registers, checks and changes the global desktop shortcuts; restores old chords if an always-on chord is lost.
Single list of desktop shortcut keys, default chords and alternatives, shared with the page.
Screen and window capture to the chat, clipboard handling and restore.
The compact floating Quick Ask panel: window, navigation handoff, show and hide.
Decides which window receives a global dictation press.
Menu-bar or tray menu: actions, running sessions, shortcut submenu.
Desktop side of Remote Control: pairing, phone confirmation, approvals, relay of session events.
Server route that starts a Remote Control pairing and applies the plan and switch checks.
Siri and App Intent 'Ask AGI Mobile', which calls the server with a keychain token.
Server answer path for Siri and widget asks: checks, routing, usage reservation.
On-device model download (resumable, cancel), free-space and Wi-Fi checks, removal.
Device capability, load and unload, and benchmark screen for on-device models.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the remote-control contract (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/remote-control.ts) used by desktop and VS Code; the desktop shortcut contract (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts) read by the desktop shell and the page; the plan capability table (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts) used by web, mobile and the server; the remote-control utility (@agiworkforce/utils/remote-control) used by desktop; the mobile-intent server path used by iOS and Android deep links. Separate per app: desktop tray, shortcuts, capture and Quick Ask (apps/desktop/electron); the Chrome in-page panel (apps/extension); the iOS widget, Siri intent and Control widget (apps/mobile/native/ios); the Android widget (apps/mobile/native/android); on-device model code (apps/mobile/services and stores); VS Code remote control service (apps/extension-vscode). The CLI has its own local-server probe (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs), not the on-device feature.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Brief marks mobile home-screen widgets 'missing', but a working iOS widget and an Android AppWidgetProvider exist and are wired by a config plugin.
Brief marks mobile companion 'done', but the companion flag and the dispatch flag are both false, so the screen and pairing never run in the shipped build.
Brief cites DrawerContent.tsx:130 as the companion entry. That line is not a companion entry; the only companion reference in the drawer is a route match.
Brief cites apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1120 for the menu-bar, but that line is window policy code. The tray wiring is at main.ts:1858-1872 and 1936-1939.
Brief cites apps/extension/src/background.ts:3833 for the floating assistant, but that line is scheduled-task recovery code, not the panel. The panel is mounted from setup.ts.
Brief cites apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:253 for messaging access. That line handles pull-request review requests; the chat-from-Slack path is apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts.

Brief cites apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1182 and :2250 and VS Code ChatStateManager.ts:1441 and :3863 as local runtime health. These lines are not local-runtime health code (CLI lines are a cloud-handoff argument list and discovery command; VS Code lines are a composer reset and context-warning preference).
Brief cites apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:579 for global dictation. That range is the app-lock and storage reset code; dictation is driven from the desktop and the page.
Brief says peak memory is a gap, and the code records peakMemoryMB as whatever local value is passed in, so the dashboard receives 0 when no sampler is installed.

Brief marks the desktop Quick Ask and capture as done, but the desktop shortcuts only register if the user keeps a non-empty chord. A chord another app holds is reported as taken and the user gets a notification.
Brief says the Chrome in-page panel is done, but the panel is mounted without any plan check that was seen in setup.ts.

not_sure: Whether the Siri ask token storage on the server (resolveMobileIntentToken) and the in-app Ask from Siri switch were traced end to end; I read the client and route only.
Where the mobile performance events are stored and whether any screen displays them (recordPerfEvent destination not traced).
Whether the desktop dictation page capture (the page side of the toggle message) works; I did not open the web page code for it.
The Chrome screenshot path (apps/extension/manifest.json:75 and the bridge server) was not traced beyond the file's existence.
Whether the desktop Window-to-chat capture uses frontWindowIdOutside correctly on every platform; only the call site was read.
Android equivalents of the Siri and hardware features; none were found.
Items 06 (animated companion) and 14 (automotive voice) are marked not applicable in the brief; I did not look for them in code, and they are not in a feature group.
Whether a Stream Deck or macropad integration exists outside the iOS Control button (desktop and Chrome were searched only by brief reference).
Whether the phone's home-screen widget data is ever live; the iOS provider looked static and was not traced further.
Whether the desktop, VS Code or CLI Remote Control approval timeout matches the mobile side (only the desktop 120 second timeout was read).

guide.what_it_is_for: These are the places where one piece of work moves across the product: a chat answer becomes an editable document or a slide deck, a voice request becomes a background task, a finished task becomes a reusable skill or a scheduled routine, a coding session moves between the web, desktop, terminal, editor and phone, and a shared artifact can be copied, versioned or reconnected. A person gets to keep working on something without retyping it or losing its history. It matters because most of the value of the product is in these hand-offs, and they are where the brief shows the most gaps (audio overview, image to video, Project sources, and the phone remote are missing or switched off).
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user for chat documents, voice, publishing and sharing. Paid-plan gates apply to the background work task (plan capability 'agi_work', live-voice-tools.ts:400-401) and to remote control (companion/index.tsx:105). Cloud coding needs the server's sandbox provider key and the managed-compute beta switch (see switches). GitHub mentions only start work for members of the repository (github/webhook/route.ts:228). Workspace members use organization sharing with read-only or can-edit access (OrganizationSharingSection.tsx:196). Developers and operators use the environment switches and the CLI slash commands.

features.name: Editable chat documents and slide decks
features.use: A document the assistant writes in chat can be opened and edited like a document, and saved as a new version. A chat answer or an uploaded document can also be turned into a PowerPoint file.
how_people_use_it: Open the artifact from the chat reply.
Click into the document and type, or use the formatting toolbar.

how_it_works.step: Chat answer becomes an artifact and is edited
how_it_works.detail: The web chat keeps artifacts in browser storage under a fixed key. The artifact view opens the rich editor for a document. Leaving the editor or pausing writes the draft back through upsertArtifact, and a content change creates the next version in the artifact store.

how_it_works.step: Office file tool makes Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV files
how_it_works.detail: The model is offered one tool that writes a real file. A slide deck is built from an outline of up to 40 slides with a presentation library. Only Word and Excel files can be used as a source to edit.

how_it_works.step: Voice tool list is built per turn
how_it_works.detail: The server decides which tools the voice model may call: the web search and page fetch tools, the office file tool, the work-task tool (only with the 'agi_work' plan capability and a client hand-off), and the sandbox tools (only when the sandbox is provisioned).

how_it_works.step: Voice work-task call becomes a work-mode chat turn
how_it_works.detail: The voice client receives the tool call, checks the goal, and calls back into the chat page. The chat page sends the goal as a work-mode turn, so it runs as a tracked task in the chat.

how_it_works.step: Cloud execution is gated by switches
how_it_works.detail: Cloud coding and code execution are refused unless the sandbox key and switch are set, the sandbox rate is priceable, and the managed-compute beta is on (on by default when unset).

how_it_works.step: GitHub mention becomes a coding task or review
how_it_works.detail: The GitHub webhook checks the comment for a mention and the commenter's standing on the repository. A review request or a coding task starts in the background. The coding task replies on the issue or pull request.

how_it_works.step: Publish, version and restore a shared artifact
how_it_works.detail: Publishing writes a publication row. Restoring an older version writes its content back to the same row in one transaction. Versions are listed from a separate versions table. Unpublish deletes the row.

how_it_works.step: Email event starts a tracked run
how_it_works.detail: A new Gmail message is ingested as a trigger event. The trigger builds the run prompt and puts the event data in a block marked as data, not instructions.

how_it_works.step: Desktop and VS Code list local sessions from the CLI app server
how_it_works.detail: The desktop app runs the CLI app server and asks it for the thread list, page by page. VS Code asks the same server for the thread list and resumes a thread by id. The CLI app server implements the thread calls.

When a connector tool needs authorization, the result carries a reconnect flag, a reason and a connect URL. The client is told to send the request again. An expired token also records a reconnect notification for the user.

key_files.role: Artifact view on web: editing draft, saving to the store, version chip, publish and comment controls.
Rich document editor; falls back to Markdown source when the document would not survive a round trip.

Office file tool: builds Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and CSV files for chat and voice.
Decides which tools a voice turn may use, including the work-task hand-off and sandbox tools.
Single place for the sandbox switches: key, flag, and priceable rate.
Publish, restore, list versions and unpublish for shared artifacts.
GitHub webhook: turns a repository member's mention into a review or a coding task.
Reads new Gmail messages and ingests each one as a trigger event.
Upload scanner: structural checks, optional external scanner, and the production refusal when no scanner is set.
Desktop side of local sessions: talks to the CLI app server (thread list, start, archive, rename).
CLI slash commands: save-skill, save-routine, continue-with-cloud hand-off drafts.
Mobile v1 feature switches; companion and dispatch are off in this build.

switches.name: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION
switches.effect: Set to 1 to turn on the cloud sandbox switch. Needed for cloud coding, code execution and the voice sandbox tools when used with the key.

switches.name: E2B_API_KEY
switches.effect: Sandbox provider key. Setting it alone turns on some sandbox paths (e2bExecutionEnabled); cloud coding also needs the flag.

switches.name: AGI_E2B_CHAT_TEMPLATE
switches.effect: Sandbox template name used for office rendering in chat; empty means no office rendering template.

switches.name: AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA
switches.effect: Managed-compute beta switch. On when unset; off when set to 0, false or off. Cloud coding is refused when off.

switches.name: UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL and UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
switches.effect: External scanner endpoint and bearer token. Without the URL, uploads get structural checks only, unless the scanner is required.

switches.name: UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED
switches.effect: true or false overrides the default. The default is required in production, so uploads are refused with scan_unavailable when no scanner is set.

switches.name: AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING
switches.effect: Skill authoring is on unless set to 0.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the web chat UI and connector reconnect helpers are in packages/ui/unified-chat, used by web and other surfaces (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/index.ts:487-495). Shared contracts: the work-task tool name (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/live-voice-tools.ts:53), the GitHub and Gmail trigger event types (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/triggers.ts:17-30), and connector reconnect detection (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-connect-required.ts). Server routes under apps/web serve web, desktop and mobile clients. Separate per app: the web artifact store (apps/web/features/chat/stores/artifacts-store.ts), the mobile artifact and voice code (apps/mobile/src/features/...), the desktop runtime (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/...), the CLI in Rust (apps/cli/src/...), the VS Code extension (apps/extension-vscode/src/...), and the Chrome extension (apps/extension/src/...). A second artifact version rule exists in packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifact-store.ts; whether the web app uses it was not established.

things_that_look_wrong.what: The brief cites upload-scan.ts:264-282 for the production refusal. Lines 264-282 are a credential-scan helper. The refusal is in uploadScannerStatus and runExternalScanner at lines 408-435, and the brief does not mention UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED.

The sandbox switches use different rules in different places. e2bExecutionEnabled is true with the key alone or the flag (used by runtime and templates). e2bCutoverEnabled needs the flag only (used by the code-runs route and the tool loop). e2bProvisioningReady needs flag, key and priceable rate. Setting only the key can enable some paths and not others.
Mobile remote control (S110.21) is marked done, but the v1 build turns off the companion and dispatch switches, so the phone remote screens show unavailable.

CLI voice (S110.07, S110.08) is marked done. The cited release workflow line is a Node smoke step and the cited voice.rs line writes a WAV file. The CLI voice module is push-to-talk transcription into the session; no code found starts a background task or makes a document from voice.

CLI cloud hand-off (S110.22) is cited at lib.rs:2774, which is marketplace code. The real hand-off is the /continue-with-cloud draft, which sends a selected transcript (default 8 messages) and says unlisted context is not available. The brief's 'repo state and pending work' is not carried by that code.

Browser page to Project source (S110.09) cites mobile share-preview index.tsx:93, which is identity capture. The share intake stages text and files into the chat composer. No save to a Project was found.
Project grounding (S110.24, S110.25) cites request-processor.ts:2548, which is a search budget helper, not Project context.

Email trigger (S110.10): the Gmail trigger fires for every new email. The brief's 'forwarded, addressed or picked from a connected mailbox' is not in the code; the panel says 'Runs for each new email'.

Viewer-authorized connected app (S110.17) is marked missing for web, but the shared-artifact page has a sign-in prompt and a connector consent card. The brief cites the sandbox HTML, whose CSP blocks network calls from the page (connect-src 'none').

Connector reconnect and resume (S110.27): the brief cites VS Code ChatStateManager lines, which are MCP server reconnect and write tracking. The connector reauthorization path is the server response in the API spec, which asks the client to resend. No automatic resume of the interrupted turn was found.

Presentation from an uploaded document (S110.02): the office file tool accepts only Word and Excel files as an editable source, so an uploaded PowerPoint or PDF cannot be the input to a new deck through this tool.
Team mention (S110.11) is marked partial in the brief and cites only the sandbox gate. The GitHub mention flow exists in the webhook route, so the brief's status and citation do not match the code.
Two artifact version stores: the web store keeps artifacts in browser localStorage, and a shared store package has its own version rule. Which one is used by which app was not established.

# How the AGI Workforce codebase fits together

Written for a new engineer and for a QA tester. All paths are relative to the project root `~/Desktop/agiworkforce`. Nothing was built, run or edited to write this page. Citations use `(path)` or `(path:line)`. A line number appears only where the file was opened and the number was visible.

When a document and the code disagree, this page says so and trusts the code. The rank order is in (AGENTS.md:§2). The disagreements found are collected at the end of section 7.

---

## 1. The product in five lines

1. AGI Workforce is one AI product on six apps: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI (the command-line app), VS Code extension and Chrome extension (ARCHITECTURE.md:29-41).
2. There are three separate ways of running a chat. Local means a model on your own device and nothing leaves it. Own key (also called BYOK, "bring your own key") means your own provider account, reached directly. Cloud (also called Managed Cloud) means AGI hosts the model access, and it is the only metered path (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:10-20, :64).
3. Not every app offers all three. Web and Chrome are Cloud only. Mobile has Local and Cloud, with no own key. Desktop chat is Cloud only. CLI and VS Code have all three (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:34-41).
4. The user chooses the model, or leaves it on Auto, where routing code picks one (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:52-58). A named model is never swapped for another by routing (docs/architecture/provider-routing.md:97-98, README.md).
5. One account, one plan and one usage allowance cover the suite. The server owns all quota, credit and plan numbers, and the apps only display them (ARCHITECTURE.md:164-169).

---

## 2. The apps

Terms used here:
- **Monorepo**: one repository holding many apps and libraries.
- **pnpm workspace**: the tool that links the TypeScript packages together.
- **Cargo workspace**: the same idea for Rust.
- **Turborepo**: the task runner that builds the packages in order.

Two workspaces share the repository. The pnpm and Turborepo one covers `apps/*`, `packages/*/*`, `packages/ai/providers/*`, `services/*` and `infrastructure/*` (pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-6). The Cargo one covers `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, `apps/desktop/gpui`, `apps/cli` and `crates/*` (Cargo.toml:2-7).

### Web
- **Folder:** `apps/web`.
- **Built with:** Next.js 16 with the App Router (a file-based routing system) and React 19 (apps/web/package.json; ARCHITECTURE.md:36). The Web UI features live in `apps/web/features` (docs/architecture/overview.md:22).
- **How it starts:** `next dev` for development and `next start` for production (apps/web/package.json scripts).
- **Server code:** the server routes sit in `apps/web/app/api`. The routing middleware is `apps/web/proxy.ts`, which exports `proxy` (AGENTS.md:§5; apps/web/proxy.ts:316). Next.js 16 renamed the old `middleware.ts`, so do not restore that name.
- **Shares:** chat UI (`packages/ui/unified-chat`), types, cloud contracts, routing and provider packages, data layer, identity and key-value packages (apps/web/package.json).

### Desktop
- **Folder:** `apps/desktop`. It builds two programs, and mixing them up is called the most expensive mistake in the tree (ARCHITECTURE.md:43-46).
- **The public Desktop app is Electron.** The host is Node code in `apps/desktop/electron`, and it shows the hosted web app in its window (ARCHITECTURE.md:48-54; apps/desktop/README.md).
  - The window loads `https://agiworkforce.com` by default (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:17).
  - A packaged build ignores the `AGI_CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN` variable. Only an unpackaged run, or an explicit `--agi-cloud-app-origin=` argument, can point the window at another allowed origin (apps/desktop/electron/config.ts:58-75).
  - Because it shows the hosted web app, a change to `apps/desktop/src` never reaches the Electron window (ARCHITECTURE.md:53-54).
  - Device features cross one bridge, `window.agiHost` (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts). Its contract is `apps/desktop/src/lib/tauri-electron/bridgeContract.ts`.
  - Privileged calls go through `apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts`. That file checks a permission grant (`permissionManager.ts`) and contains file paths (`pathGuard.ts`) (ARCHITECTURE.md:82-88).
  - Chat on Desktop is Cloud only. The dispatcher refuses local-inference commands (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3367). Local coding sessions run the bundled CLI (docs/architecture/desktop.md:112-117).
- **The older retained code is Tauri.** It is a Rust host in `apps/desktop/src-tauri` that loads a Vite and React renderer from `apps/desktop/src`. It is kept for internal value and compatibility, and it is not a second public product (docs/architecture/desktop.md:7-10; docs/architecture/overview.md:24-26).
  - Its React code reaches Rust only through registered Tauri commands. `apps/desktop/check-wiring.sh` fails drift in both directions (ARCHITECTURE.md:79-81).
- **Also present:** `apps/desktop/gpui`, an opt-in native migration host built with GPUI that talks to the CLI over typed process input and output (ARCHITECTURE.md:56-59). Its own docs say it is not a replacement release yet (docs/architecture/desktop.md:30-33).
- **How it starts:**
  - Electron: `pnpm --filter @agiworkforce/desktop dev:electron`, which builds the Node host and runs `electron .`. The package `main` is `electron/dist/bootstrap.cjs` (apps/desktop/package.json).
  - Tauri: `tauri dev` (apps/desktop/package.json `dev`).
- **Shares:** Rust crates by path dependency (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32-39) and shared TypeScript packages (section 3).

### Mobile
- **Folder:** `apps/mobile`.
- **Built with:** Expo (a React Native toolkit) and React Native 0.86. Screens are routed by Expo Router from `apps/mobile/app` (apps/mobile/README.md; apps/mobile/package.json). Features live in `apps/mobile/src/features` (docs/architecture/overview.md:23).
- **How it starts:** `expo start`, `expo run:ios` and `expo run:android` (apps/mobile/package.json).
- **Native projects:** `apps/mobile/ios` and `apps/mobile/android` are generated by prebuild and gitignored. Native changes go through config plugins in `apps/mobile/native` (apps/mobile/README.md).
- **Modes:** Local and Cloud only (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:45).
- **Shares:** `packages/platform/local-llm` for on-device models, plus unified-chat, cloud contracts, sync and others (apps/mobile/package.json:66 and manifests).

### CLI
- **Folder:** `apps/cli`, a Rust program (ARCHITECTURE.md:39).
- **Binaries:** `agi` is the main one, with `agiworkforce` as an alias (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:15-21).
- **How it starts:** running `agi` opens a terminal interface (apps/cli/README.md). `agi login` signs in to an AGI account with a device code. Logging in with a provider name stores your own key (apps/cli/README.md).
- **Also hosts the developer session server.** The CLI runs `agi app-server`, which the VS Code extension and Desktop code sessions use (repo-map.json surfaces; apps/extension-vscode/README.md).
- **Shares:** only Rust crates (apps/cli/Cargo.toml:40-50), not TypeScript packages.

### VS Code extension
- **Folder:** `apps/extension-vscode`. The package name is `agi-workforce` (apps/extension-vscode/package.json).
- **Built with:** TypeScript and esbuild. The entry point is `./out/extension.js`, from `src/extension.ts` (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:83; esbuild.js).
- **How it starts:** VS Code loads it and it starts a local `agi app-server`, but only in a trusted workspace (apps/extension-vscode/README.md).
- **Shares:** `packages/client/ide-runtime`, client-runtime, sync, unified-chat and others (manifests). It reads the CLI binary on the user's machine. It never talks to a model itself for Local or own-key use.

### Chrome extension
- **Folder:** `apps/extension`.
- **Built with:** Manifest V3 (MV3, Chrome's current extension format) and Vite. The background is a service worker, the panel is `src/side_panel.html`, and the permissions include `sidePanel`, `storage`, `nativeMessaging` and `scripting` (apps/extension/manifest.json).
- **How it starts:** `vite build` (and `vite build --watch` for development), then load the folder in Chrome (apps/extension/package.json).
- **Mode:** Cloud only. Its local `chrome.storage.local` copy stays authoritative, and eligible all-Cloud chats are mirrored to the shared account history (docs/architecture/trust-boundaries.md:58).
- **Shares:** cloud contracts, sync, unified-chat, provider-runtime and others (manifests).
